Tonga Frizell (Vaimauga 28, Taumalolo 64), Wong (Olakau’atu 41), Olakau’atu (Fonua-Blake 38, Utoikamanu 66), Taumalolo (Halasima 31), Foketi; Hopoate, Watene-Zelezniak, Koula, Toia, Fifita, Fainu (Lolohea 17), Katoa, Fonua-Blake (Utoikamanu 21, Wong 52).

Referee Gerard Sutton (Australia).

England’s Rugby League World Cup challenge could well be over, just 80 minutes after it started.

Brian McDermott’s hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals were all but shattered in his side’s first pool match in a brutal encounter in which Pacific Island physicality and passion ultimately earned Tonga a famous victory.

England displayed huge attacking courage with their offload strategy – in all, they made 26 – but their adventurous intent could not find the finishing touch and was not enough to topple a ferocious opposition defence in Perth. Despite excellent performances from captain George Williams and Dom Young, they were ultimately blown off HBF Park.

On their seventh attempt, this was Tonga’s first win over England and although this intense contest was for, so long, much closer than the scoreboard finally showed, there can be no doubting the excellence of Kristian Woolf’s team and the ruthlessness they displayed in the last quarter in which they never stopped tackling refused to stop coming.

News.title: ‘The boats don’t stop’: The deadly coastline that has become a trafficking superhighway
News.content:
The dangers were illustrated earlier this month, when a boat carrying more than 300 migrants sank near Obock on its way to Yemen. At least 139 people drowned, including 15 children. There were 700 drownings or people lost at sea on the route in 2025.

“The boats don’t stop, day or night,” the local coastguard chief told the Telegraph as he looked out at the waterway, walkie-talkie in hand, one day earlier this month.

The chief, who declined to be named, pointed to skiffs and fishing boats moored in a lagoon outside his outpost, that he had confiscated from smugglers and traffickers.

The world has become familiar with the 18-mile-wide Bab el-Mandeb strait as one of the globe’s most congested and strategically important maritime choke points.

Sitting to the south of the Suez Canal, the East-West artery flowing through the strait carries approximately 12 to 15 percent of global maritime trade.

What is less well known is that there is also a migration superhighway running across the strait, linking Africa via Djibouti to Yemen and the Gulf beyond.

Many tens of thousands of people cross the waterway each year and while Yemeni refugees fleeing the Houthi offensive have made headlines in recent weeks, the majority of those braving the waterway are heading the other way.

This maritime migrant route out of Africa has recently been busier than all the crossings across the Mediterranean into Europe, according to the International Organisation for Migration (IOM).

The IOM estimates there were nearly 64,000 crossings across the Bab el-Mandeb in the first four months of 2026, compared with a total of just over 23,000 across the Western, Eastern and central routes of the Med.

The vast majority heading east are Ethiopians so desperate to find work in the Gulf that they are prepared to trek through war-torn Yemen, which has been tipped into a humanitarian crisis by its civil war.

The IOM recorded some 202,000 migrant trips into Djibouti from Ethiopia in 2025 and by early October, the figure for 2026 had already hit 177,000.

The reignited war in Ethiopia’s Tigray region is expected to increase the numbers wanting to leave, yet the exodus is also being held up by escalating fighting along Yemen’s coast between Houthis and the government.

Fewer are now able to get across the strait, leaving them stranded on the western side, or forced to take more dangerous routes.

News.title: Asia’s vaccine self-sufficiency drive gets $650m boost
News.content:
An “innovative” partnership to boost vaccine security across Southeast Asia will inject up to $650 million into regional manufacturing, in a bid to reduce reliance on imported shots.

The five-year initiative, announced at the annual meetings of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund in Bangkok on Friday, will see major lenders, non-profits, and the private sector come together to invest in the region’s vaccine industry.

Currently Southeast Asia’s production base remains limited and exposed. The majority of shots are imported, and any capacity the region does have is highly concentrated – one analysis this year estimates 60 to 90 per cent sits with a single vaccine manufacturer.

Even before Covid-19 hit, this vulnerability was recognised. The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), a regional bloc of 11 countries, endorsed a vaccine security and self-reliance initiative in 2019, driven by Thailand’s National Vaccine Institute (NVI).

These concerns have mounted since the pandemic, but up until now investment as well as political will has been lacking. The partnership announced on Friday, led by NVI, hopes to remedy this, and develop a model that can be copied worldwide.

​​“If we can do it here in Asia, then that really provides a model for the world,” said Aurélia Nguyen, deputy CEO of the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (Cepi), a a vaccine research non-profit. “We can build it out in Africa, in Latin America, and that really gives us the resilience that we want the next time we have a major epidemic.”

Cepi has committed up to $20 million of “catalytic funding” for the programme, which is backed by the World Bank as well as organisations like the Singapore-based AVPN investment network.

In all, the package of loans and grants will include at least $174m in public financing, and up to $460m in private capital mobilisation for regional vaccine manufacturing. Further details, including recipients, have not yet been announced.

But Paschal Donohoe, the managing director and chief knowledge officer of the World Bank Group, told a panel in the Thai capital that “we believe this has the ability over time to mobilise up to $650m of finance”.

He added that the group would use public loans and grants alongside investments by its private-sector arm, the IFC, while its guarantee arm, MIGA, would help cover investors against risk.

“It’s really important because each element of the World Bank Group is involved in it,” Donohoe said. “We’re not just talking the talk, but walking the walk.”

Speaking to the Telegraph after the event, Nguyen added: “Innovative models and partnerships like this, where we’re each bringing a piece to de-risk scientific technology, [allow us] to leverage larger quantities of capital.

“But I think what’s also helpful in this model is, beyond the financing, [we] have a sort of coordinating umbrella through Asean,” she said. “So you can be smart and [avoid] duplicating investments, which brings commercial sustainability and resilience for health systems.”

Nakorn Premsri, the director of NVI, added that the investment model will help “build a more sustainable and resilient regional vaccine ecosystem, to meet both routine needs and the demands of health emergencies”.

Sports.title: PSG star Maghnes Akliouche shares picture of ankle cut open after Strasbourg opponent escapes red card for wild tackle
Sports.content:

MAGHNES AKLIOUCHE was left with a bloodied ankle following a lunging tackle by Jeyland Mitchell.

But the match referee opted NOT to send the defender off during the closing stages of Paris Saint-Germain‘s 3-1 win at Strasbourg.

Summer arrival from Monaco Akliouche was handed his third consecutive start by boss Luis Enrique following goals against Le Mans and Manchester City.



PSG trailed for much of this encounter at Strasbourg, courtesy of Giovanni Reyna‘s 17th minute effort.



But Enrique’s men turned the game on its head late on, despite a missed penalty by Ousmane Dembele.

Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner subsequently teed up Ilia Zabarnyi to score the equaliser.

The winger then completed his atonement by putting his side in front on 85 minutes.

With just one minute of regulation time remaining, Akliouche attempted to skip past a challenge by Mitchell.

The Costa Rican initially won the ball with his flying challenge.

But his follow through nastily caught Akliouche’s ankle.

The 24-year-old writhed in pain following the tackle – although no red card was forthcoming from the referee.

With PSG having already used all their substitutions, Akliouche gutted it out and completed the match.

And Desire Doue scored deep into stoppage time to seal PSG’s impressive comeback win.

After the game, Akliouche showed off the damage done by tackle.

In a picture posted by RMC Sport reporter Arthur Perrot, a nasty gash could be seen on Akliouche’s ankle through a tear in his sock.

Insiders have been left bewildered at Mitchell not receiving a red card for the challenge.

PSG were handed a further injury scare as Nuno Mendes did not complete the match.

GRIMSBY defender Edon Pruti was sensationally sent off while suffering a suspected DOUBLE LEG BREAK n an X-rated challenge.

The Mariners fell to a 2-0 defeat against a Northampton side which was taken over by Alexandre Pato last month.



And Pruti, 24, was left writhing in agony as Grimsby desperately searched for a way back into the League Two showdown.

The former Burnley youngster crashed into a full-blooded challenge with Joe Wormleighton minutes after Jon Guthrie had doubled Northampton’s lead.



Both sets of players quickly gestured for medics to rush onto the pitch when it became clear Pruti was in serious pain.

But referee Martin Woods was in an unforgiving mood as he had already taken the red card out of his pocket before pleading for medical attention.



Pruti was then carried off on a stretcher and rushed to hospital – after being given his marching orders.

And Grimsby chief David Artell hit out at Woods for brandishing a red card following the horrific injury.

The former Crewe boss, who has been in charge at Blundell Park since 2023, said: “It looks like a double leg break, unfortunately.

“I assume he will have an operation but I haven’t been able to speak to him yet. We obviously wish him a speedy recovery.

Sports.title: Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink says returning Sunderland star Brian Brobbey is ‘unappreciated’ in Holland… just like he was
Sports.content:
Next

BRIAN BROBBEY is back from his hamstring injury — and not a moment too soon for struggling Sunderland.

The Black Cats take the long trip south to Bournemouth on Sunday desperate to halt their Premier League slide following three-straight top-flight defeats.



Boss Regis Le Bris is hoping the return of his Dutch powerhouse will provide the firepower to stop the rot.

And legendary Prem hitman Jimmy-Floyd Hasselbaink believes compatriot Brobbey is the ultimate weapon — even if the purists back home in the Netherlands do not appreciate him.



Dutch fans might pine for the silky grace of Dennis Bergkamp, Marco van Basten, or Patrick Kluivert, but Hasselbaink insists Sunderland’s star offers something far more destructive.

The ex-Leeds, Chelsea and Middlesbrough forward, who scored 127 goals in 288 Prem appearances, exclusively told SunSport via MrQ, said: “Brobbey’s a little bit like me.



“He’s not being appreciated as much because of the more physical style that he has. But the Dutch have been, and still are, a little bit spoiled with attacking talent.

“He’s totally different. The Dutch team, and the Dutch fans, have to adapt to that a little bit more. Sometimes they don’t want to adapt, because in Holland, they like to compare everything with the Van Bastens, the Kluiverts, the Bergkamps.

“Brobbey’s doing exceptionally well for Sunderland. He’s exceptionally good at what he does.

“He’s a different kind of talent. He’s a different kind of footballer. And he had to really work really hard to get where he is now.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

While Brobbey may be underappreciated in his homeland, he is worshipped on Wearside.

The 24-year-old achieved icon status with a last-ditch winner at North East rival’s Newcastle and capped a fantastic first season in England by firing the Black Cats into the Europa League.

He was unstoppable last month as he fired in a hat-trick in a 5-3 defeat at Manchester City before that momentum was ended when he picked up a hamstring injury on September 24 against Germany.

Sunderland failed to land a glove on Brighton last week as they slipped to a 2-0 home defeat. But Brobbey was back on the bench for Thursday’s 2-1 win at Portuguese minnows Torreense.



Wilson Isidor sat out midweek and remains a doubt to take on the Cherries after picking up an undisclosed knock against the Seagulls.

But Le Bris has confirmed Brobbey is ready to go and is set to be unleashed today at The Vitality.

Hasselbaink, 54, says his return will have a huge impact throughout the whole team. However, the only problem is that the big guns could start circling if the frontman picks up where he left off before his setback.



Hasselbaink said: “The thing is, we need to forget about the goals with Brobbey. What he does best is that he holds the ball up really well.

“When you make it a fight with the centre-half, he always wins. It doesn’t matter how big the centre-half is, he always wins.

“He holds the ball really well. He brings his team-mates into the game.



“For Sunderland, that works exceptionally well because that’s the way they get out of their half.

“Another team like Manchester United might not want to play this way. If he can do that around the opposition’s box, then he can cause problems.”

United and Bayern Munich have both been linked with moves for Brobbey. And Hasselbaink added: “That’s just one of those things with football.

“If he keeps on scoring like he’s doing now, it’s going to be difficult to keep him around for much longer.”

Sports.title: Labour minister’s Dubai trip & £7.5k flights to meet firm run by Man City owners – at height of club’s ‘cheat’ probe
Sports.content:
Next

A CABINET minister held talks with the firm run by Man City’s ­billionaire chairman — just as Premier League chiefs were studying the club’s massive financial breach case.

Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds met Mubadala Investment Company during the top-secret hearing — and for a second time just six weeks after it concluded.



Mr Reynolds is a key ally of the PM and his fellow Manchester MPs were behind the “Etihad Coup” — named after City’s home stadium — which led to Andy Burnham replacing Sir Keir Starmer.

One Conservative MP said: “The Etihad Coup has come back to bite the PM.”



Mr Reynolds met Mubadala representatives on a taxpayer-funded trip to Dubai on November 1, 2024. Group chief executive of Mubadala is Khaldoon Al Mubarak, Man City’s long-time chairman.

In 2013, Education Secretary and Labour deputy leader Lucy Powell also went on a paid-for jaunt to the Gulf.

Department for Business and Trade records show Mr Reynolds’ trip — which included talks with Gulf trade ministers and Dubai ports giant DP World — was set up “to discuss investment in the UK”.

They add that Mr Reynolds’ flights cost £7,596.

Six weeks after the Premier League hearing ended, on ­January 21, 2025, Mr Reynolds met Mubadala again on the day he arrived at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

Again, the meeting was “to discuss investment opportunities in the UK”. Mr Al Mubarak was also in Switzerland that day. Records do not say if the City chairman was present during his firm’s meeting with Mr Reynolds.



Mr Reynolds, MP for Stalybridge and Hyde in Greater Manchester, was removed as Business Secretary in September 2025, but was returned to the key post when Mr Burnham entered No10 in July.

He met Mr Al Mubarak there on September 14 to discuss UAE investment in Britain. The talks were a fortnight before the commission’s verdict against City became public.

When the news broke that City had been found guilty of more than 100 charges Mr Burnham said he would be “really concerned to lose” the club’s owners.

He called them “a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester”.



Mr Reynolds’ links with the Emirates go back more than a decade.

In November 2012, he flew to Abu Dhabi and Dubai on a five-day £3,500 trip funded by the UAE government, the Commons register of interests shows. His entry says the visit was to meet ministers and “senior UK and Emirati business figures” and promote trade and investment.



He was given two Wembley tickets worth £466 by the Football Association for City’s 2023 FA Cup semi-final against Sheffield United.

The FA gave him two more, worth £338, for the 2024 final against Manchester United.

Mr Powell did not deny meeting Mr Al Mubarak but a Department of Business, ­Innovation, Science and Trade spokesman said: “This is a matter between Man City and the Premier League.

“The Business Secretary’s meetings were crucial in helping us boost UK investment, jobs and strike a multi-billion-pound free trade deal with the Gulf Co-operation Council.”

Andy Burnham has ordered a “manual trawl” of his own dealings with City after an investigation in The Sun.



He told a podcast he had held only one “significant” meeting with City’s owners, in 2021.

But we revealed he was twice wined and dined by Mr Al Mubarak at the Etihad while Manchester mayor. Both dinners were logged on a ­register of interests he signed in December 2020.

Details were removed from the Greater Manchester ­Combined Authority (GMCA) website, a move it said was in line with policy.

The Sun revealed Mr ­Burnham joined a lunch with “senior representatives” of City Football Group in China in 2018, taking his City meetings tally to at least seven.

Two months after the first dinner, the GMCA he chaired approved a £24.5million loan to Manchester Life, a property venture between Manchester City Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group, founded in 2008 to buy Man City.



Earlier this month it was reported City and the Premier League held settlement talks centred on a “sizeable financial payment” rather than relegation or the stripping of titles.

The talks “quickly fell apart”, Bloomberg claimed.

City, whose prime playing asset is £190million-rated striker Erling Haaland, have called the Premier League ruling an “opinion”.



The club deny wrongdoing and are appealing. Meanwhile, the Emirati government paid for Ms Powell’s 2013 Gulf jaunt.

The close Burnham ally flew to the UAE from March 23 to 26 just four months after ­winning the Manchester Central by-election.

The UAE government covered her £3,500 travel and accommodation costs, according to her register entry.

She declared it as a visit by the UAE All-Party Parliamentary Group to meet ministers and business figures.

Lifelong City fan Ms Powell has been given thousands in terms of hospitality from them, accepting tickets to five City matches in 11 months worth £2,360.



In 2014, she welcomed a ­£1billion housing deal in her constituency between ­Manchester City Council the Abu Dhabi United Group.

A report by lobbying watchdog Spinwatch from 2018 said the UAE had run an “intense ­lobbying campaign” to win over MPs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It quoted a leaked email from a UAE official stating one meeting was “very effective”. It did not mention to which visit the email referred or name Mr Reynolds or Ms Powell.

A spokeswoman for Ms Powell said: “As a constituency MP, Lucy has always valued the partnership and investment from the club and others, which has helped transform East ­Manchester from a barren, ­contaminated former industrial wasteland into one of the most desirable, happening places, with new jobs and opportunities for local people, anywhere in the region.”

Sports.title: Michael Carrick’s a lovely guy but I never saw a manager in him, says former boss Harry Redknapp amid Man Utd slump
Sports.content:
Next

ELLAND ROAD is a scary place to go at the best of times and Michael Carrick needs his players to stand up for him on Sunday.

Leeds away is the sort of game where you need people like Harry Maguire, some strong characters.



You can’t have people go hiding.

It would have been tough for Manchester United in any event but it’s been made even harder after the whole Lisandro Martinez stuff when they lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid.



Maybe you don’t want a player saying that in public but I’m sure a lot of United fans think he was telling the sort of truth the club doesn’t want to hear.

What Martinez was saying was basically, ‘You can keep blaming the manager but unfortunately we’ve got a team here that’s not good enough to be doing any better than what we’re doing. This is what we are’.

And that is what they are, Manchester United.

We always think of them as a club that had great teams. I go back to the Matt Busby days, then Sir Alex Ferguson came along and they produced some incredible teams.

The kids came out of the youth team and Fergie made great signings like Roy Keane, Jaap Stam, Nemanja Vidic, Rio Ferdinand, Andy Cole and Dwight Yorke.

And Michael, too, of course.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But Alex admits his last side, the one that won the league title in 2013, was probably the worst team he’d had — getting older, needing rebuilding.

Since then, nobody has been able to make a success of it.

I’ve known Michael since he was 12 years old at West Ham.

When I went to Portsmouth, I wanted to sign him. We even had a deal for £2.5million and he was coming down for a medical. But he got a phone call from Tottenham and so we lost him.

When I went to Spurs, Daniel Levy said he knew he had to be a player as I wanted to sign him having worked with him before - because only an idiot signs someone he knows is no good.



Daniel took a gamble and it paid off, even though Jacques Santini, who was the manager at the time, didn’t know who he was and didn’t play him.

I can’t say I always saw a manager in him.

Michael’s always been a lovely guy from a lovely family, a really intelligent footballer who knew the game, read it, controlled matches. But he’s always been a quiet lad, too, laid-back. It’s what he is.

When United scored against Tottenham the other day, he wasn’t running up and down the touchline — the complete opposite to Roberto De Zerbi, kissing the ball and all that when they equalised.

Results haven’t been great but I hope he turns it around and keeps the job because I love him.



I know that some of the fans want the United manager to be a bigger character. I get that.

Michael is a bit more like Ole Gunnar Solskjaer or Ralf Rangnick. But they’ve had Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho as well, big personalities, and it’s just not worked.

Everybody since Fergie’s tried it and we’re not talking mugs here. They’ve had great managers but none have been able to even look like winning a title.



And whoever comes in next, it’s still a massive rebuilding job to do.

In terms of recruitment, they’re short. Recruitment, recruitment, recruitment, that is the problem.

The players that are there are not good enough to take them where they want to go, they’ve not got a team that is good enough to be challenging Arsenal and Manchester City.

You can change Michael tomorrow and they are still not going to finish any higher than fifth or sixth this season. That’s how I see their team.

They’re nowhere near good enough to challenge for a title.

That’s what Michael is dealing with. And it would be the same for anyone else, whoever they bring in.

Sports.title: Man Utd stars fear Amazon Prime documentary is reason for disastrous start to season under Michael Carrick

MANCHESTER UNITED stars fear Amazon documentary cameras are affecting their season — because staff and players are holding their tongue in post-match debriefs.

The acclaimed fly-on-the-wall sporting series All or Nothing is focusing on United this season.



But with just two wins this term, there are fears it could become a video nasty for boss Michael Carrick and the club.

A source told SunSport players believe the cameras stifle dressing-room chat during and after games, to the detriment of performances.



The source said: “The players view the cameras as a pain.

“They not only have to meet with them every couple of weeks to do filming, they think that having them in the dressing room means the players and the managers aren’t being as open as they could be about what has been going wrong and what needs to be done to fix it.

“Some of the players are more keen on it than others but the ones that don’t like them think punches are being pulled in the wake of games.”

It comes after Lisandro Martinez hit out at the club’s executives after United’s 2-0 Champions League loss against Atletico Madrid.

Defender Martinez has since been fined and apologised for his outburst, with United’s winless streak extended to five matches.

Head coach Carrick has insisted that his team has already put the incident behind them, but the Argentine hopes to depart the club on a free transfer over the summer.

Sports.title: Beaming Match of Day couple Mark Chapman & Kelly Cates spotted together for first time since romance revealed
Sports.content:
Next

MATCH of the Day lovebirds Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates are seen stepping out together as a couple for the first time.

The presenters were snapped on Saturday morning heading to work at the BBC in Manchester.



Kelly, 51, pushing a small suitcase, exited a multi-storey car park with Chappers, 53, before the pair chatted away along the street.

They were wearing matching Adidas trainers and even checked their phones in a similar manner.



Kelly was preparing to host MOTD on BBC1, while Mark presented daytime sports coverage on Radio 5 Live.

An onlooker said: “Mark and Kelly were smiling and laughing together and walking in sync.



“He had his hands in his pockets and she was wheeling a small suitcase. They kept chatting all the way towards the studios.”

Mark was dressed in casual jacket, jeans and cardie while Kelly wore a pink shirt and wide-legged slacks.



The passer-by went on: “They were wearing matching trainers which was quite sweet.

“She went towards the TV studios and he walked into the radio section, next to it.”

We told how the couple — appointed hosts of MOTD along with Gabby Logan last year — quietly started dating in May.



The romance began soon after Mark ended his three-year relationship with Dubai-based estate agent Clere Collier in April.

The mum of two regularly travelled to the UK to see Mark and they were pictured househunting last year.

An associate of the couple said at the time: “Mark admitted the relationship, but insisted there was no overlap between the two women and that he hadn’t cheated on her.

“He told her that he had been a single man when he started spending time with Kelly. Of course, it left a bad taste in Clere’s mouth, and she didn’t believe him.”

Mark, one of the BBC’s highest-paid broadcasters on around £340,000 a year, also teamed up with Kelly, daughter of Liverpool footie legend Kenny Dalglish, on Channel 4’s Celebrity Gogglebox.



Last week we told how Mark extended his World Cup trip in the US this summer for a secret date with Kelly in New York.

Mark lost his wife of 19 years, Sara, to cancer aged 44 in 2020. They had three children together.

Kelly split from her TV producer husband Tom, father of her two children, in 2021.



Speaking to Gabby that year on her podcast The Mid-Point, Kelly confessed she struggled to comprehend the idea of dating again.

She said: “I don’t have a picture in my head of why a middle-aged, slightly overweight mother of two could possibly be attractive.

The thought of going on a date, spending an evening with someone and at the end thinking, ‘Well, I don’t really like you,’ I’d be so resentful of them taking up my time.”

Sports.title: Man Utd boss' fate was sealed in 'blow up' meeting before Leeds match
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss' fate was sealed in 'blow up' meeting before Leeds match

A LOOK BACK: The Manchester United manager knew he was facing down the handle of an axe before his players stepped on the pitch to face Leeds

View 3 Images Ruben Amorim saw his time at Manchester United end with this very fixture (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Michael Carrick will hope to avoid the same fate as Ruben Amorim at Elland Road as he heads to face Leeds under some serious pressure. Manchester United fans will feel the eerie resemblance to earlier in January when the Portuguese manager was sacked after a 1-1 draw.

‌



‌



Amorim had been handling calls for his axe for a number of weeks before the Leeds game after picking up just 30 points out of a possible 60 during the 2025/26 season. His side managed maximum points in just eight of 20 games that campaign alone and ended his reign with a dismal 40% win rate and a measly draw against bitter rivals Leeds.

‌



But it was revealed later that Amorim's fate was sealed two days before the Elland Road visit after he "blew up" in a meeting with United's director of football, Jason Wilcox. The club chief had planned for the meeting to be productive and to assess where the team stood days after a 1-1 draw with bottom-placed Wolves.

‌



But when Amorim's unchanging views on the 3-4-3 system were brought up, he reportedly "blew up", and any hopes of reconciliation ended. The Telegraph reported at the time that a decision was made to get rid of the manager, without the need for a board meeting.

The one Man Utd player at centre of Lisandro Martinez row 'revealed' as real reason for outburst emerges READ MORE :

The report claims this verdict was reached with the full support of United's co-owners, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family, meaning Amorim was a 'dead man walking' before he went postal after the Leeds draw. In his post-match press conference, the Portuguese head coach was asked if he still had the backing of the club chiefs - and this didn't go down well.

Amorim said: "Guys, to stop with that, and I noticed that you received selective information about everything. I came here to be the manager of Manchester United, not to be the coach of Manchester United. That is clear. I know that my name is not Tuchel, is not Conte, is not Mourinho, but I'm the manager of Manchester United.

‌



View 3 Images Amorim was on the way out before the Leeds game began (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"It's going to be like this for 18 months or when the board decided to change. That was my point. I want to finish with that. I'm not going to quit. I will do my job until other guy is coming here to replace me. I just want to say that I'm going to be the manager of this team, not just the coach. I was really clear on that. That is going to finish in 18 months, and then everyone is going to move on.

‌



"That was the deal. That is my job, not to be a coach. If people cannot handle the Gary Nevilles and the criticises of everything, we need to change the club. No, no guys, I would say that I came here to be the manager of Manchester United, not to be the coach. Every department, the scouting department, the sport director needs to do their job. I will do mine for 18 months and then we move on. Thank you, guys."

The next morning, chief executive Omar Berrada and Wilcox formally sacked Amorim in what a senior United source called "a sad, tough and disappointing day." An insider source claimed Amorim wanted to "blow it all up" at the club due to his "erratic behaviour."

View 3 Images Carrick will need to be careful (Image: Alberto Gardin/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



They added: "We supported Ruben through thick and thin – through bad results, erratic behaviour, all those public statements – so to turn around now and say it’s a power struggle is ridiculous. There has barely been a cigarette paper in the relationship between Jason, Omar and Ruben. This is a manager who basically decided to blow it all up. He’s been looking for the opportunity. He wanted out."

Now, Carrick is facing the same fixture with some wildly similar surroundings. He has won just one Premier League match this season, losing two and drawing three as United sit in 13th place.

The team are in the same position in the Champions League, having beaten newcomers Sabah 4-0 and lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid midweek. Carrick does have some merit left at Old Trafford thanks to his history with the club, coupled with his success as interim last season, which ended with a third-place result in the league.

Article continues below

But the current United boss is all too aware of the team's last visit to Elland Road and just how important it is to secure a win against their rivals.

It's another big European week for Liverpool, who will follow up their Premier League trip to Brentford with another night under the lights at Anfield. Villarreal are the visitors in the Champions League on Tuesday and Andoni Iraola's team have a chance to make it three wins from three in the competition.

‌



‌



Iraola has been without some key players of late, not least in the league loss at home to Manchester City. Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in that game but only received a one-match ban so will be available going forward after missing Saturday's game in West London.

‌



Summer signing Bradley Barcola got off the mark last Wednesday, scoring a hat-trick in a 6-3 win at LASK. However, another of the Reds' big-money stars, Florian Wirtz, has found himself in the spotlight this season.

‌



We've got the latest on Wirtz after speculation over a January exit, as well as more on another attacking player who the Reds weren't able to sign in the past. Here are our latest lines from around Anfield.

Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta makes telling Kai Havertz prediction after clear Viktor Gyokeres decision

Kai Havertz has been installed as Arsenal's first-choice striker by Mikel Arteta, with Viktor Gyokeres having to settle for a place on the bench just a year after the Gunners paid £64million for him

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta was full of praise for Kai Havertz (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has backed Kai Havertz to become a 25 goal-a-season striker for Arsenal. Arteta was glowing about Havertz’s all-round qualities as Arsenal’s centre forward and his character after several injury setbacks.

‌



‌



But Havertz has only managed one season in his career - at first club Bayer Leverkusen - when he has managed 20 goals and has only hit double figures once in the Premier League which was 13 in 2023-24. Since then, Havertz has been hit by injuries but Arteta is convinced he can become more prolific and also prove that he can be a goal scorer as well as valuable member of the attack.

‌



Gunners boss Arteta said: “He has that ability. That is why he is playing there as well, and that is why we signed him. I think he has it, and he needs that volume of games and actions. If you give him that, I am a big believer that yes, he can do it.”

‌



Arteta is a huge fan of Havertz and has clearly backed the Germany striker ahead of Viktor Gyokeres this season. Last season, Havertz struggled with injury but came back for the run-in and helped Arsenal get over the line to win their first Premier League title in 22 years.

Havertz went to the World Cup and has carried on his form into this season and has managed three goals already as well as providing an assist in the midweek win over Lille in the Champions League. But Arteta revealed that Havertz - who came on as a substitute in midweek as Arsenal rotated for their European tie - came off the pitch frustrated with himself.

Arteta said: “He’s so competitive, Kai. For example, after the game with Lille, he came in and he’d made a massive impact and you could see straight away what he did on the pitch.

“But he left the pitch so upset because he did not score a goal. He was happy to help the team but so upset. That is the character we want: a player who wants to evolve and improve every single day.

‌



”He loves the game, he loves to run, he loves to feel important and loves to feel he can help other players as well. He is a giver and that’s why.

How many goals will Kai Havertz score this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Kai Havertz started the season well before his injury (Image: Nigel French/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

‌



”From a very difficult season, he was out for a long period of time and to get back at the highest level is not easy and it can take time. But Kai has done it almost immediately from pre-season and I’m not surprised because his mentality is top.”

Havertz may actually be under appreciated in the wider football world but Arteta insists the whole dressing room know his qualities for Arsenal. Former Chelsea striker Havertz is a deep thinker and Arteta says his game intelligence and ability to read the game are huge qualities.

Arteta added: “I don’t know what people think is but if you ask anyone in that building, ‘what do you think of Kai?’ The first thing that will be said is something positive, for sure. I don’t have that impression and certainly I value him a lot.

‌



“His football IQ is something else. He understands everything at such speed and he can break down information better probably than anyone else on the team. That’s something that’s not easy to say especially when we talk about a striker.”

View 3 Images Viktor Gyokeres is playing second fiddle to Kai Havertz (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Havertz bulked up last season to put on extra muscle and also make himself more resilient as he came back stronger and more determined after two injury disrupted seasons. There was also new competition from Gyokeres but the Sweden striker has quickly found himself behind Havertz in the pecking order which just highlights how highly Arteta rates him.

Sports.content:
Phil Foden brings inflatable banana to interview as Man City star makes defiant claim

Phil Foden scored in Manchester City's 3-2 win against Ipswich, their first home Premier League match since it was confirmed that the club had been found guilty of breaching financial rules

View Image Phil Foden interview (Image: Manchester City)

Defiant Phil Foden claims that the Premier League's damning verdict on Manchester City hasn't affected their dressing room 'one bit'. City were recently found guilty of breaching 114 financial rules between 2009 and 2018, leaving a stain on their success both during that period and since.

‌



‌



The club strongly deny the charges which were first brought against them in February 2023, launching an appeal as their legal battle with the Premier League continues. It's been pretty much business as usual for City on the pitch, winning both of their league games since the verdict was confirmed.

‌



Foden, 26, scored the opening goal in Saturday's 3-2 victory over Ipswich, a win that ensures they'll end the weekend top of the table. In his post-match interview, the midfielder was notably clutching an inflatable banana.

‌



"I'm going to get one for my son as a present, I think," Foden told club media. "I think he wanted one, so I can give him one now."

The bananas have become a symbol of City's defiance against the verdict which Foden insists hasn't changed anything for the players. "It hasn't affected us one bit," the 26-year-old added to Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit
Sports.content:
Viktor Gyokeres eyeing Arsenal January exit after Gunners' transfer pursuit

Viktor Gyokeres has struggled to find his footing in Mikel Arteta's Arsenal set-up over the past 12 months, with his future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious doubt as January transfer talk intensifies

View 2 Images Viktor Gyokeres could be looking for a move away from Arsenal (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Viktor Gyokeres is reportedly keen to leave Arsenal due to a lack of first-team opportunities. The Swedish frontman was the subject of intense speculation in north London last summer, with the Gunners eventually wrapping up a £63.5million agreement with Sporting CP for the 28-year-old following a lengthy and protracted transfer saga.

‌



‌



Yet Gyokeres has found it difficult to establish himself in Mikel Arteta's system over the past 12 months, with his long-term future at the Emirates Stadium now under serious scrutiny. This season, Gyokeres has been restricted to a mere 56 Premier League minutes in total, and has unsurprisingly failed to register a single goal or assist despite his endeavours.

‌



Arsenal also devoted considerable energy towards landing Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez during the summer window, only to come away empty-handed owing to the La Liga outfit's firm refusal to sell combined with the Argentine forward's preference to join Barcelona instead.

‌



With the Madrid club making clear they have no intention of selling their prized asset to their Catalan rivals, and with Alvarez's relationship with the Atletico faithful somewhat strained following his Camp Nou ambitions this summer, Arsenal could be well-positioned to make a renewed push for the striker come January.

That would also all but cement Gyokeres' standing at his current club, with Alvarez likely to spearhead Arteta's attack upon his arrival given the substantial fee Atleti would demand for his services.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



According to TEAMtalk, Atletico Madrid also remains a possible destination for Gyokeres should he depart Arsenal. The La Liga outfit expressed an interest in the striker during their meetings with Andrea Berta over the summer, with discussions over a potential deal for Alvarez also regularly featuring in those conversations.

However, a number of other clubs across the Premier League, Italy and Germany are also keeping tabs on Gyokeres, meaning Arsenal could face a hectic period when the transfer window swings open again at the start of 2027.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez remains a target for Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite shining in the Nations League with Sweden, netting four goals in four appearances throughout the recent international break, Arteta continues to place his trust in Kai Havertz as a false-nine rather than handing Gyokeres the opportunity to lead the line.

That's also despite Gyokeres' track record for thriving on English soil. The striker racked up 43 goals and 17 assists for Coventry City between 2021 and 2023 before securing his move to Sporting.

Article continues below

There, he enjoyed a further 97 goals and 28 assists in 102 games before landing in North London last summer.

Whether the Gunners boss deviates from his current approach or gives Gyokeres the chance he deserves on paper when Arsenal make the trip to the City Ground to face Nottingham Forest on Sunday, 18th October, remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Premier League trio including Man City star refuse to take knee as initiative returns
Sports.content:
Premier League trio including Man City star refuse to take knee as initiative returns

Premier League matches have seen the reintroduction of taking the knee, but several players opted to stand while the anti-racism gesture was being observed before kick-off on Saturday

View 2 Images The taking the knee initiative has returned in October

A trio of Premier League players, including Manchester City's Marc Guehi, refused to take the knee on Saturday as the 'No Room For Racism' month of action began.

‌



‌



The England defender chose to remain standing before their clash with Ipswich at the Etihad, whilst on the opposing team fellow defender Issa Diop also refused to take the knee.

‌



Earlier in the afternoon, prior to Everton's loss to Chelsea, Ainsley Maitland-Niles refused to kneel despite everyone else on the pitch doing so.

‌



Neither of them have spoken out but it is well documented that several players believe the gesture, which began in the aftermath of the Covid lockdown, has lost its value.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Players and staff have the opportunity to perform the pre-match gesture for the next two weeks in October. The Premier League have maintained their "commitment to tackling discrimination and highlight the importance of diversity in football".

Ahead of the 2021/22 season, Luton stated that they would not be taking the knee and instead all stood in the centre circle. That was at a time when players were still taking the knee before every game, but that idea came to an end in August 2022.

A decision was then made to limit the gesture so that it only took place during match rounds that fall during the No Room For Racism initiative. It was agreed by Premier League captains ahead of the season that they would continue to perform the gesture twice per season.

‌



View 2 Images Ainsley Maitland-Niles stood whilst others took the knee during the lunchtime kick-off (Image: TNT Sports)

In 2021 ex-Crystal Palace star Wilfried Zaha described kneeling as "degrading" and then Brentford frontman Ivan Toney said: "We are kind of being used as puppets, in my eyes; take the knee and the people at the top can rest for a while now, which is pretty silly and pretty pointless. Nothing is changing."

The move started in the UK in 2020 following the death in US police custody of George Floyd, which sparked the Black Lives Matter movement.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's bold Liverpool change pays off as nine-man Brentford cause their own undoing
Sports.content:
Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford 2-1, with a change from Andoni Iraola sparking their turnaround. The Reds came away from the Gtech Community Stadium with all three points thanks to second-half goals from Victor Munoz and Alexander Isak.

But the stage was set by a dramatic first half that saw two decisions overturned by VAR and a deserved lead for Brentford. Keane Lewis-Potter fired the Bees in front shortly after Liverpool thought they'd been given a penalty.

But Keith Andrews' side - who went into Saturday unbeaten - were reduced to 10 when Yehor Yarmolyuk was deemed to have headbutted Jeremy Jacquet. Munoz and Isak eventually punished Brentford, although it wasn't straightforward for the visitors - even after another Brentford red card.

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Liverpool dealt Szoboszlai blow

When team news was confirmed, Liverpool fans were delighted to see the return to Dominik Szoboszlai. The Hungarian had missed his side's last two games but was back in the starting XI.

Unfortunately for Szoboszlai, he only lasted 32 minutes. The 25-year-old went down off the ball in what appeared to be an aggravation of his prior injury.

All eyes will be on Iraola's post-match comments and whether Szoboszlai will be fit to face Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. And talk about bad things coming in threes...

‌



Where will Liverpool finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Dominik Szoboszlai's return from injury was short-lived (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

VAR dominates first half

It was all going wrong for Liverpool as half-time neared. Shortly after Szoboszlai's substitution, the Reds were given a penalty by John Brooks, as Dango Ouattara went sliding in on Alexis Mac Allister, and quickly had it taken away.

Replays showed that the only contact Brentford winger Ouattara made was with the ball, prompting Brooks to overturn his decision on the recommendation of video assistant referee Darren England. But VAR wasn't done getting involved - more that shortly.

‌



Brentford made the most of their reprieve, as Keane Lewis-Potter's header put the hosts 1-0 up. The goal came about after Mac Allister had lost possession inside his own half, allowing the hosts to pounce.

View 5 Images Keane Lewis-Potter broke the deadlock (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

The ball ended up at the feet of Igor Thiago, whose cross was perfectly converted by Lewis-Potter. Then finally something went right for Liverpool.

At a corner, Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet was having it out with Yehor Yarmolyuk, and the Brentford midfielder lost his cool with a headbutt akin to Rodrigo Bentancur's against Manchester United last weekend. England spotted in the incident and Brooks had no choice but to show Yarmolyuk a red card.

‌



No penalty was awarded because the ball wasn't in play at the time of the incident. Liverpool still had it all to do, but facing 10 men gave them a huge advantage.

View 5 Images Yehor Yarmolyuk was sent off for a headbutt (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

Iraola's bold change pays off

For a spell early in the second period, Brentford held their own with 10 men, testing Liverpool before their onslaught came about somewhat inadvertently. Jeremie Frimpong, brought on as a half-time substitute, had to come off just seven minutes after his introduction due to injury.

Would Iraola turn to Joe Gomez or opt for something bolder?

‌



The answer was the latter. Rio Ngumoha entered the fray, offering more of an attacking threat.

Ngumoha's introduction forced Victor Munoz to right-back, but it didn't put the Spaniard off bombing forward. Munoz would equalise with a brilliant solo goal, cutting inside and producing a cool finish from inside the 18-yard box.

View 5 Images Andoni Iraola made a game-changing attacking substitution (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

Iraola's men kept up the pressure and would be rewarded when Mac Allister picked out Bradley Barcola, who was free at the far post. His header wasn't ideal but Alexander Isak showed superb centre forward play to take the ball away from his man and slot past Caoimhin Kelleher.

‌



Although Ngumoha wasn't involved in either of the goals, the winger's presence changed the dynamic for Liverpool. Gomez did eventually come on to help the Reds over the line, a task made easier by Vitaly Janelt's second yellow card for a foul on Barcola in stoppage time.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso issues Emi Martinez injury update as Chelsea star taken to hospital
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso issues Emi Martinez injury update as Chelsea star taken to hospital

Emi Martinez was forced off in Chelsea's win at Everton following a nasty collision, and Xabi Alonso has confirmed that his goalkeeper was taken to hospital

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso was quizzed on Emi Martinez's condition (Image: TNT Sports)

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso has confirmed that Emi Martinez was conscious when he left the Hill Dickinson Stadium and his visit to hospital is "precautionary".

‌



‌



The Spaniard was unable to give any more information with the Blues boss being quizzed shortly after his side's win at Everton as he awaits a full report on their goalkeeper.

‌



Martinez needed to be stretchered off midway through the second half after a major collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. The Everton defender, after receiving treatment, was able to jump back to his feet and continued.

‌



The Argentine, though, was still being tended to by medical staff. The stretcher was bought out, with Martinez being assisted off as the Hill Dickinson Stadium applauded him. The pause would result in 11 minutes of added time.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Alonso said: “As far as I know, he left the stadium conscious. Now he is in the hospital doing precautionary tests. Let’s see, but this is what I know so far.”

Chelsea would secure their first clean sheet in nine months on Merseyside. Martinez needed to be alert to deny Jack Grealish in the first half whilst the Blues' shut out was completed by Mike Prenders, who came on and spent the final 25 minutes on the pitch.

Matchwinner Neto said after his two goals secured the three points: "We are really pleased. Shame for Emi [Martinez] but we wish you all the best. This win is for him."

‌



He also added: "We need a clean sheet to be honest. I think we did a very good game. Emi deserved this, Mike [Penders] did as well."

View 2 Images The Chelsea goalkeeper had to be taken off on a stretcher

The ex-Aston Villa No.1 will now be sidelined for at least two weeks as per the concussion protocols. It means he will miss the clash with Tottenham next week and is a doubt for the Carabao Cup tie at Anfield against Liverpool as well as the game against Manchester United on October 31.

Article continues below

In recent years, the Football Association (FA) have implemented strict head injury procedures and Martinez will now have to go through the process.

Sports.title: Van Gerwen suffers another early exit as Van Veen makes history
Sports.content:
Dutch favourite Michael van Gerwen suffered a shock second-round exit at the Dutch Darts Championship on Saturday, losing 6-5 to Irishman William O'Connor.

The defeat extends Van Gerwen's poor run of form, having lost his opening match at four European Tour events this season before arriving in Maastricht: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It marks his most first-round exits in a single season since the tour began in 2012.

O'Connor produced a superb display, firing in three ton-plus checkouts of 136, 131 and 121 to seal his victory and book his place in round three.

Elsewhere on Saturday, Gerwyn Price's return to the stage ended in glory as he beat Scott Williams 6-3, while Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Earlier this year, Laura Turner and Chris Murphy reviewed Van Gerwen's limp loss to Dirk van Duijvenbode at the World Matchplay and suggest he's becoming like Manchester United

Martin Schindler and Stephen Bunting also jumped into the qualification spots for Dortmund.

Van Veen averaged a staggering 120.24 in whitewashing Sebastian Bialecki, breaking the previous record of 118.66 by Dave Chisnall.

Schindler sealed his spot at the European Championships later this month with his victory over Karel Sedlacek.

Bunting left it late to secure his place at the European Championship, beating already-qualified Cameron Menzies 6-2 to book his spot. The former Masters champion needed a strong finish to get over the line.

The 41-year-old pinned six out of ten attempts at the outer ring in his victory over the Scot, and jumped into the qualifying places, knocking Kim Huybrechts out of the running.

Image: Dutchman Gian van Veen broke the European Tour record average on Saturday

Brendan Dolan remains the only player capable of pushing Sedlacek out of the European Championship qualifying spots after beating Heine Uuldriks 6-4. The Northern Irishman had led 4-1 before being pegged back.

Nathan Aspinall ended Michael Smith's hopes of qualifying for Dortmund with a dominant 6-1 victory. The World Grand Prix semi-finalist averaged over 102 to dispatch the former world champion.

Wessel Nijman and Danny Noppert also secured their places in Sunday's action, with the Dutch pair defeating Jeffrey De Graaf and Dave Chisnall respectively.

Niels Zonneveld edged a last-leg decider against Krzysztof Ratajski, hitting seven maximums for the second consecutive match to book his place in round three. Fellow Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena also progressed, beating Host Nation Qualifier Jimmy van Schie 6-2.

European Tour ranking leader Ross Smith will face Ryan Searle in round three after overcoming Ryan Joyce and Dirk van Duijvenbode respectively.

Sports.title: Rangers miss chance to go top as Jones earns Dundee a point
Sports.content:
Callum Jones scored a second-half equaliser as Rangers were held to a 2-2 draw by Dundee and missed the chance to go top of the Scottish Premiership.

Dundee opened the scoring when Rangers failed to deal with a routine long ball, with Bradley Fink capitalising to round the goalkeeper and slide home.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bradley Fink's composed finish gave Dundee the lead against Rangers.

The lead did not last long, though, as Badredine Bouanani cut inside and curled in a stunning equaliser to open his account for Rangers.

Nico Raskin scored the goal of the game when his shot from outside the area went in off the underside of the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nicolas Raskin produced an outrageous strike to put Rangers back in front against Dundee.

But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

Rangers remain second and move one point behind Celtic, who host Hearts live on Sky Sports on Sunday from 2.30pm.

The key moments from Dens Park

8: BLOCKED! Kim has a shot blocked with the goal gaping. Rangers cry for handball but nothing doing.

14: SHOT! Forrest drives from midfield and shoots from the outside of the area, but Pandur gathers comfortably.

23: SHOT! Hay has a speculative shot and again it's saved comfortably by Pandur.

28: SAVE! Hamilton whips a free kick across and Astley heads towards goal from outside of the area tipped behind by Pandur.

29: OFF THE BAR! Hay leaps to meet the corner and it rattles the bar.

36: CLOSE! Hamilton takes an early shot after Dundee win the ball back and it goes just wide.

37: GOAL! Fink rounds the goalkeeper and scores!

42: GOAL! Bouanani curls into the top corner for his first goal for Rangers!

56: SAVE! Gassama shoots from the edge of the area, and it's saved one-handed by the 'keeper

60: GOAL! Nico Raskin scores a screamer off the bar from outside of the area.

69: GOAL! Neil dwells on the ball and is dispossessed by Jones who slots past the goalkeeper to get Dundee level!

74: CLOSE! Ball falls to Neil in the six-yard box but Dundee somehow scramble the ball clear!

McInnes: We shouldn't need three goals to win

Rangers boss Derek McInnes:

"I thought Dundee's press was good, as expected, and we wanted to try and draw the centre-backs out at times and try and hit spaces and feed our wide players and try and get 1v1.

"It never quite materialised.

"We shouldn't need to come away from home and need to score three goals to win a game.

"Two goals should have been enough tonight. We had a few chances when it went to two each.

"Dundee are a good team, but I think we gifted an opportunity there not to take all three points.

"We're disappointed not to come away with three points."

Pressley: We showed grit and determination

Image: Callum Jones scores for Dundee to make it 2-2

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"I think it was a game of two halves.

"I thought we were outstanding in the first half, really aggressive, controlled a lot of the game.

"We were really strong on second balls, had one or two moments where we should have capitalised and restricted Rangers to very little.

"We obviously expected a reaction from Rangers and they gave that reaction. They put us under a lot of pressure in the second half.

"We showed grit and determination.

"The game was getting away from us but we never gave up, we kept going and going and (Callum) Jones got his reward for a really strong performance today."

Boyd: Dundee asked questions of Rangers

Sky Sports' Kris Boyd:

"Dundee are a good team. They're not there [in the table] by fluke or luck.

"They've got a style of play, Steven Pressley has got a group of players willing to run themselves into the ground for him and that's hard to get.

"They put in a shift and even when they're asked to dig in and suffer like they did for the first 20/25 minutes of that second half.

"They then got a second wind and came back at Rangers and asked questions of them.

"A draw was a fair result. It took wonder strikes to get Rangers two goals.

"There was a lack of creativity at the top end of the pitch and it's something they're going to have to improve."

Sports.title: Dubois smashes through Wardley to win world title rematch in two rounds
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois smashed Fabio Wardley to defeat in the second round of their world championship rematch at London’s O2 Arena.

Dubois retained the WBO heavyweight title he won from Wardley in May in crushing style, picking up just where he left off in their first fight.

Dubois and Wardley were renewing hostilities only five months after a frenetic and ultimately brutal contest.

Then London's Dubois had needed to rise twice from early knockdowns to punch out a savage 11-round victory over Wardley, hurting the Ipswich fighter even though Wardley was stopped on his feet.

Image: Dubois finishes Wardley in a corner.

Wardley, determined to win back his world title as soon as he could, exercised the rematch clause in his contract and forced this second fight to take place.

But Dubois snuffed out his hopes with brutal speed.

A powerful right cross from Dubois sent Wardley briefly down to one knee in the opening seconds of the first round. Wardley sprang back to his feet immediately, inviting the right uppercut that followed.

The referee administered a count, and that proved to be just a momentary reprieve. Dubois set about him with shuddering force for the rest of the round.

Dubois' jab rocketed in. Wardley missed with a wild right and the champion knocked him back on his heels. Dubois dashed his right down, hitting Wardley almost at will.

He had Wardley under terrible pressure at the end of the first and trainer Ben Davison climbed up onto the ring apron, moments away from pulling Wardley out as the bell chimed to end the round.

Image: Dubois picked up where he left off in their savage first fight.

The champion continued his onslaught in the second. Wardley couldn't escape from those thunderous punches and he swayed, pained back into the ropes.

Another Dubois cross connected clean, with such force it loosened Wardley's legs beneath him. Bravely he kept himself upright. But he could not stave off the attack.

An unrelenting Dubois positioned his prey in a corner and went in for a finish. He hacked right hooks over and lashed in huge punches to the head.

He hammered those shots into him, jolting Wardley's head on his neck with a salvo of stunning punches, until Wardley's trainer Davison could leave it no longer. He threw in the towel and the referee rushed in to end it.

Image: Dubois has his hand raised in victory

'Bad intentions from the beginning'

"I had bad intentions from the beginning," Dubois said. "Our back was against the wall first time. We just had to go out there and show we meant business tonight."

Wardley reflected: "It's never fun to lose. It is what it is, I've always thrown myself in with the biggest, toughest, meanest guys around, there's no shame in testing yourself against the best.

"Daniel is testament to coming again and I'll come again."

On the undercard Bakhodir Jalolov, a two-time Olympic super-heavyweight gold medallist, showcased just what makes him so formidable as he hammered out a 10 round unanimous decision victory over Solomon Dacres.

Image: Bakhodir Jalolov dominates Solomon Dacres (Photos: Leigh Dawney/Queensberry)

But he also displayed what can make him so frustrating to watch. The towering southpaw controlled virtually the whole bout and struck Dacres over early in the fifth round.

The knockdown was superb, Jalolov using his right to take Dacres' left glove away from his guard, opening up a path for the Uzbek's booming left cross - a shot that sent Dacres to the canvas and bloodied his nose.

But Jalolov didn't capitalise and continued to work in single shots, albeit excellent single shots, as he dominated without turning up the pressure, winning 99-91 and 99-90 twice.

20-year-old Irish heavyweight prospect Adam Olaniyan made short work of journeyman Dan Garber.

Image: Adam Olaniyan takes out Dan Garber

In his fifth pro fight, Olaniyan maintained his 100 percent finish rate stopping Garber in the second round.

Busy without rushing his work, Olaniyan's right cranked Garber's back into a corner post at the end of the first round.

He picked up from there for the second, trapping Garber on the ropes and putting him down with another heavy cross.

Garber's corner threw in the towel, then threw in a second. But the referee kicked them out the ring and Garber tried to fight on. He was though promptly crumpled a second time. After rising unsteadily the referee waved it off at 1-15.

In a British and Commonwealth lightweight title fight Michael Gomez Jnr looked to have dominated Louie O'Doherty over 12 rounds, only to be held to a majority draw.

Sports.title: Munster beat Racing amid Foley tributes as Saracens and Bath suffer defeats
Sports.content:
Champions Cup: Munster honour Anthony Foley with emotional win over Racing 92; Leinster, Glasgow shine as Saracens and Bath fall

Brian Gleeson was among the try scorers as Munster beat Racing 92 in Cork on a day of emotion and tributes a decade on from the death of Anthony Foley

A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.

The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson - wearing 24 with Foley's old number of 8 retired for the match, as it was in 2016 - joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and centre Joseph Manu, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

Glasgow, Leinster post big opening away-day victories | Saracens lose at Connacht

Elsewhere, Glasgow Warriors extended their unbeaten start to the new season by pulling away to claim an impressive 47-27 win at Sale Sharks.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Glasgow's winning score might have looked convincing but they only secured victory in the final 20 minutes after Rekeiti Ma'asi-White had temporarily reduced Sale's deficit to four.

The game looked in the balance until late tries from Rory Darge, Ollie Smith and debutant Otavio Tuipulotu helped Glasgow pull away and wrap up a precious bonus-point win.

Leinster made a flying start to their campaign with an emphatic 48-23 victory away to Clermont Auvergne. Tadhg Furlong, Dan Sheehan (two), Sam Prendergast, Jack Conan and Tommy O'Brien all crossed the line, while a penalty try completed a dominant seven-try display.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Connacht pulled off a stunning 45-36 victory over Saracens in Galway, scoring tries through Cian Prendergast (two), Cathal Forde, Shamus Hurley-Langton, Ciaran Frawley (two) and Caolin Blade.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Bath also endured an evening to forget as they were dispatched at home by Montpellier 32-14 at the Rec in a shock result.

Lions face La Rochelle a day after death of team-mate Andrews

Players stood in silence, with some visibly emotional, as La Rochelle and the Johannesburg-based Lions paid tribute to South African lock Hyron Andrews before Saturday's Champions Cup clash. The 31-year-old died in France on Friday, on the eve of the fixture.
