World.title: Utomi faces backlash over defence of Kila despite academic credentials controversy
World.content:
Pat Utomi, a Nigerian political economist, has faced criticism for defending Anthony Kila despite evidence questioning the authenticity of the academic qualifications and titles the latter claims.

Mr Utomi, in a Facebook post on Saturday, said Mr Kila was a “smart and good man” and described suggestions that he had never attended school as “spectacularly stupid”.

However, several Facebook users objected, arguing that Mr Utomi’s defence focused on Mr Kila’s intelligence and character rather than addressing the central issue of whether he obtained the qualifications and academic titles attributed to him.

Ekokoi Solomon, a law lecturer at the University of Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, said Mr Utomi was addressing an issue different from the allegations against Mr Kila.

“Pat Utomi is saying something entirely different from the allegations against Mr Kila. The issue here is about spurious and fraudulent claims about certification,” Mr Solomon wrote in the comment section.

Babajide Brown also challenged Mr Utomi’s comparison of the controversy surrounding Mr Kila with the public scrutiny of Jason Arday, the British sociologist who became a professor at the University of Cambridge, accused of plagiarism in July 2026, and was later found dead at his home in London on 14 August 2026.

Mr Brown said the two cases involved fundamentally different allegations, noting that the controversy surrounding Mr Arday concerned dishonesty and failing to attribute intellectual work, rather than whether he possessed the academic qualifications he claimed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The fact that he talked intelligently and that he is a ‘good man’ is beside the point and totally irrelevant to the discourse,” Mr Brown wrote.

Jolayemi Babajide similarly questioned the relevance of Mr Utomi’s post, asking how it answered questions about Mr Kila’s academic credentials.

Isaacs Oguntuase said the controversy concerned integrity, credibility, and accountability, especially given Mr Kila’s academic background.

He called on Mr Utomi, as a professor and respected member of the academic community, to encourage Mr Kila to present verifiable evidence of his qualifications or acknowledge any misrepresentation or error.

“If we are to preserve public confidence in our academic institutions, we must be willing to demand accountability from everyone, regardless of their eloquence, reputation, or perceived intellectual ability,” Mr Oguntuase wrote.

Kukei Umoye also criticised what he described as double standards, referencing the controversy over President Bola Tinubu’s academic certificate.

Mr Umoye said Mr Kila should provide empirical evidence of his professorial status to resolve the dispute.

PREMIUM TIMES investigations

The backlash follows PREMIUM TIMES investigations published on 3 and 10 October that questioned Mr Kila’s professorial title and the academic qualifications he claimed to have obtained from undergraduate to doctoral level.

The first investigation found no evidence that a recognised academic institution had awarded Mr Kila a professorship. Mr Kila told the newspaper that the European Centre for Advanced and Professional Studies awarded him the title in 2016, but the investigation found no evidence that the institution existed.

In the second report, PREMIUM TIMES documented discrepancies in his claimed academic qualifications, with some institutions disputing or failing to verify the credentials attributed to them. The newspaper said its investigation was continuing.

Mr Kila has maintained that he is a professor and stands by his academic and professional credentials.

Mr Utomi said in his post that he learnt about the controversy late and had never asked Mr Kila about his certificates or letters of appointment. He said he could not personally vouch for those documents.

He also recounted facing questions about his professional history and academic standing, arguing that public figures can be subjected to unfair attacks.

Drawing a parallel with Mr Arday, Mr Utomi criticised what he described as online bullying and questioned the motives of those challenging Mr Kila.

However, his critics insist that the allegations require documentary verification rather than a defence based on personal acquaintance, intelligence or character.

Mr Utomi faced a similar backlash on X, with one user urging him to take down the post.

“I think you should be smarter about this issue. The man himself has said nothing about this. No rebuttals. Nothing. Why don’t you wait for him to do so before you disgrace yourself? The friend of a thief may also be a thief,” said an X user who commented under Mr Utomi’s post.

World.title: 2027: Keke riders endorse Mbah, Tinubu, as governor extends tricycle operation time to 10pm
World.content:
The Tricycle Riders Association of Enugu State has endorsed the state governor, Dr Peter Mbah, for a second term in office, citing improved security, road infrastructure, and social amenities in the state.

The association, popularly known as Keke Riders, also endorsed President Bola Tinubu, citing the Enugu–Onitsha Road, Enugu–Port Harcourt Expressway, New Artisan Bridge, Obinagu Flyover, and strategic appointments.

This was even as Governor Mbah scrapped the N750 daily payment by tricycle operators and also extended their operational time from 9pm to 10pm.

Mbah also said they would continue to operate at no cost at all the state’s modern transport terminals.

Leading the endorsement at Okpara Square, Enugu, during the conclusion of a “One Million March” event on Saturday, the state Chairman of the Tricycle Riders Association of Nigeria, Kingsley Edeh, said the endorsements were predicated on achievements, especially those that have impacted the lives and businesses of tricycle riders, their families, and the people of Enugu State in general.

“Which will we reel out and leave the other? Is it the security and good roads, which now enable us to ply our trade without any problems, the 267 Smart Green Schools, the completion of long-abandoned projects such as the International Conference Centre, Nigergas Limited, Sunrise Four Mills, Hotel Presidential, and many more?

“We can also see the infrastructure President Tinubu is building in the South East and the support he is giving to our governors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“So, we will vote APC from top to bottom come 2027,” he declared.

Corroborating the position of the Tricycle Riders Association in Enugu, the body’s National Secretary, Sunday Enang, described Mbah as a ‘magician’ in the art of governance, stressing that no governor anywhere had done what he was able to accomplish in three years.

“Your ‘Tomorrow Is Here’ vision is evident in the construction of modern transport terminals, the establishment of Enugu Air, investment in an asphalt plant, intra- and inter-city road construction, and efforts to improve traffic flow and urban transportation.

“These initiatives are promoting safer, more organised, and more efficient movement across the state.

“We also commend the policy allowing tricycle operators to use designated terminals without paying toll fees. This support recognises their contribution to the economy and the livelihoods of thousands of families.

“These practical policies reflect disruptive innovation and demonstrate how effective leadership can turn vision into tangible opportunities,” he said.

In his response, Mbah described tricycle operators as critical players in the state’s economy, stressing that while his administration was focused on growth, it was equally determined to eradicate poverty, hence the various interventions to increase their disposable incomes.

“You are the powerhouse of our economy because you set out early in the morning, working long hours, navigating traffic, taking our workers to work, taking our students to school, moving our people from urban areas to rural communities, connecting businesses, and helping traders get to their businesses. A lot of people earn their living because of what you do.

“But we also see your struggles. So, I have started engaging with your executives on how we can make life better for you. As the Managing Director of the Transport Terminal just said, no more payment by our tricycle riders at any of the transport terminals.

“Let me also recognise something. Our government, as you know, is not just about growth. We are also interested in ending poverty and making sure that you have more money or disposable income to take care of your family. And so, the issue of tickets is sealed. No more tickets for you.

“Again, when we came into the office in 2023, we inherited a curfew on tricycle operators such that they could only operate from 6am to 9pm. There was a sit-at-home, but we have ended that with your support. Today, Enugu State is safe. So, we will be shifting your operational time limit from 9pm to 10pm,” he said.

While acknowledging their commendation for the rapid construction of roads, Mbah said this was part of the government’s deliberate steps to increase their disposable incomes by reducing their spending on repairs, assuring them that his administration would construct and reconstruct all the remaining 1,022 urban roads in the state.

“Because I understand how bad roads can be terrible, not only for your tricycles and the money you spend on repairs, but also for the time you spend at the mechanic, all the roads in Emene, Abakpa, Idaw River, Trans-Ekulu, Awkunanaw Area, Coal Camp, New Haven, Thinkers Corner, Uwani, among others, are paved or being paved.

“I can assure you that there will be no road in our city that will be unpaved. We are going to pave all the remaining 1,022 roads,” he emphasised.

Meanwhile, Mbah has vowed that his administration would take every step within the law to preserve the security and peace that the people of Enugu had worked to build in the state.

“You must treasure it. You must protect it. Enugu is on an upward trajectory. We will not allow those deceptive voices and politicians who campaign in poetry but only govern in prose. With our government, you have experienced real development and real growth.

“Let me also warn that we have worked extremely hard to establish a safe state. Nobody, no matter their ambition, will take that away from us. And we will not stop at anything, deploying all means necessary within the law to bring to book any violator or anybody who tries to import thugs to disrupt the peace and public safety we enjoy in this city and this state. We have zero tolerance for violence.”

He enjoined the people to make good their endorsements by getting their PVCs ready for the 2027 elections and voting massively for him, all APC candidates, and President Bola Tinubu, whose policies, he said, ensured the availability of resources to execute the numerous projects they listed.

Other speakers at the event were the Enugu State Chairman of the APC, Martins Chukwunweike; Grand Patron of the Enugu State Traditional Rulers Council, HRH Igwe Greg Ugwu; and the Managing Director, Enugu East Zone Transport Terminals, John Egbo.

World.title: $7bn Deep Seaport: Ogun govt tackles PDP candidate over alleged ‘Broken Promise’ remark
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has strongly condemned the description of the proposed $7 billion Gateway Deep Seaport investment as “another broken promise” by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) senatorial candidate for Ogun East, Abdul-Hameed Omotayo, describing the remark as a reckless distortion of facts, an attempt to politicise a landmark investment and evidence of disregard for the economic prospects of the state.

In a statement on Saturday, the government accused Omotayo of playing dirty politics with an investment initiative backed by formal agreements signed with global port operator DP World in Paris on 24 September 2026, insisting that the agreements, investment commitments and plans for the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone were matters of public record that could be independently verified.

The government said it was particularly troubling that a candidate seeking to represent Ogun East in the Senate would dismiss an investment expected to transform the economic landscape of the host corridor, create employment opportunities and strengthen the state’s industrial and maritime capacity without adequately engaging with the facts surrounding the project.

The statement, signed by the Special Adviser on Media and Strategy to Governor Dapo Abiodun, Kayode Akinmade, said the agreements covering the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone were signed in the presence of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, and DP World Group Chief Executive Officer, Yuvraj Narayan.

According to the government, the participation of senior Nigerian officials and the leadership of the international port operator underscored the significance of the agreements and the scale of the proposed investment, which is expected to strengthen Ogun State’s maritime infrastructure, expand industrial activities and create employment opportunities.

The government also cited a statement from the State House, signed by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, which reported an initial investment exceeding $7 billion and projected the creation of 50,000 direct jobs.

It maintained that the project should be assessed on the basis of the agreements reached, the commitments made by the parties and verifiable milestones towards implementation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“How can you describe the deep seaport as another broken promise when concrete steps have been taken to advance the project?” the statement asked.

Akinmade said the multiplier effects of major infrastructure investments were too significant to be dismissed on partisan grounds, adding that the initiative had attracted commendation from residents who recognised its potential to expand economic opportunities, attract businesses and create jobs.

He accused Omotayo of being economical with the truth, insisting that responsible political discourse required an appreciation of the distinction between a project backed by formal investment agreements and one that existed only as an announcement.

He stressed that signing an investment agreement marked an important step in the development process, while acknowledging that financing arrangements, regulatory approvals and construction were among the subsequent stages required to bring the project to fruition.

The government also described as laughable Omotayo’s boast that he would defeat Abiodun before noon on election day, dismissing it as political bravado that failed to address the substantive development issues confronting Ogun East.

It characterised the PDP candidate as a political daydreamer, arguing that his focus on electoral boasts rather than the details of major investment initiatives raised questions about his understanding of governance and the processes involved in delivering large-scale infrastructure projects.

Akinmade further questioned the PDP’s political credibility and direction, citing the exclusion of its governorship candidate, Ladi Adebutu, and his running mate from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) final list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun governorship election.

He said the development followed INEC’s enforcement of statutory requirements governing the submission of party membership registers, adding that the controversy raised questions about the PDP’s internal processes and compliance with electoral regulations.

According to him, the party should address its internal challenges rather than seek to discredit investment initiatives with far-reaching economic implications for Ogun State.

The government maintained that political criticism should be grounded in facts and substantive engagement with policy issues, rather than unsupported allegations or declarations about electoral victory.

On infrastructure development in Ogun East, Akinmade said the Abiodun administration had constructed and rehabilitated more than 243.3 kilometres of roads in the district since 2019, as part of a statewide total exceeding 1,600 kilometres across the 20 local government areas.

Among the projects he cited were the Ijebu-Ode–Mojoda–Epe Road, Sagamu–Iperu–Ode–Sapaade Road, Ejirin–Idowa–Ibefun–Itokin Road in Odogbolu, Tam Balogun Road in Ijebu-Ode and Imodi–Imosan Road.

He also referenced the approval of the J4–Gao Road in Ogun Waterside, alongside the administration’s reported delivery of more than 150 blocks of classrooms, primary healthcare interventions across the district and the Gateway International Agro-Cargo Airport at Iperu-Remo.

The government said the projects formed part of its broader development agenda aimed at improving connectivity, expanding access to essential services and creating an environment conducive to economic growth across the state.

“These are tangible development interventions whose details can be examined and verified. The debate should be about facts, project delivery and the future of Ogun East, not unsupported allegations,” Akinmade said.

The administration maintained that its infrastructure programme and investment initiatives provided a basis for assessing its development record, urging political stakeholders to subject their claims to scrutiny against available evidence.

It also called on residents to distinguish between project announcements, the agreements underpinning them and the subsequent stages required for implementation, stressing that the progress of the proposed Gateway Deep Seaport should be assessed against verifiable developments.

The Gateway Deep Seaport and Blue Marine Special Economic Zone are expected to expand Ogun State’s maritime and industrial capacity, attract domestic and international investment, strengthen logistics and trade, and generate employment opportunities, subject to the successful implementation of the agreements.

The government reiterated its commitment to pursuing investments and infrastructure projects that would broaden the state’s economic base, stimulate private-sector growth and support long-term development.

World.title: Police arrest 67 suspected Vikings cultists at anniversary celebration
World.content:
The Police Command in Delta State has arrested 95 suspected cultists and recovered five firearms and 12 live cartridges during coordinated operations across four local government areas of the state.

The operations, conducted on Thursday, also led to the recovery of seven expended cartridges, suspected cult insignia, branded jackets and charms, according to a statement sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Friday by the police spokesperson, Bright Edafe.

The statement said the arrests followed intelligence-led operations by the Department of Operations, Rapid Response Squad (RRS) and Command Anti-Cultism Unit in Asaba, Ika South, Ughelli South and Okpe local government areas.

The Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, directed operatives to intensify the crackdown on cultism and related violent crimes, the statement said.

67 suspects arrested at alleged cult anniversary

The largest operation occurred at a hotel along Abraka Road in Asaba, where police said suspected members of the Supreme Vikings Confraternity, also known as Aro Bagger, had assembled for an alleged cult anniversary celebration, Mr Edafe said.

“A combined team of police operatives raided the premises and arrested 67 suspects, comprising 55 males and 12 females,” Mr Edafe added.

The police said they recovered two pump-action guns, a locally fabricated cut-to-size gun, 10 live cartridges, five expended cartridges, 11 caps bearing suspected cult insignia and two branded cult jackets.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In a related operation in Agbor, Ika South Local Government Area, operatives arrested 15 additional suspects, comprising 14 males and one female, with items suspected to be linked to the same confraternity.

Three arrested in Ughelli South, 10 in Okpe

In another operation, police operatives raided a suspected criminal hideout at Jeremy Community in Ughelli South Local Government Area following intelligence about a gathering of suspected members of the same cult group.

The operation, conducted by the Command Anti-Cultism Unit’s Ovwian-Aladja Sector in collaboration with a civilian anti-cult group, resulted in the arrest of three suspects identified as John Pius, 32; Oghene Ochuko, 28; and Akinbule Godstime, 24.

The police said other suspects fled the scene.

Two locally made pistols, two live cartridges, two expended cartridges, two caps bearing suspected cult insignia, and suspected charms were recovered, according to the statement.

At Jeddo Community in Okpe Local Government Area, operatives arrested 10 additional male suspects over alleged involvement in cult activities.

The police said the suspects and recovered exhibits were in custody, while investigations continued.

Police warn cult groups

Mr Erale commended the operatives for the arrests and directed area commanders, divisional police officers and tactical commanders to intensify operations against cult groups across Delta State.

He warned that the command would not tolerate cult-related activities capable of threatening public peace and urged residents to provide credible information to support security operations.

The arrests come amid renewed attention to the activities of suspected cult groups in the South-south region.

On Friday, the police in Rivers announced that it had queried and relieved the divisional police officer in charge of Abuloma Division and the officer overseeing its police outpost after allegations that suspected cultists renovated the facility.

The police also ordered an investigation into the renovation and the possible involvement of police personnel after a video circulated on social media showing young men identified by a Facebook user as members of Aro Bagger at the outpost during what appeared to be a handover ceremony. Police officers were also seen taking photographs with them.

The police command in the state said legitimate community contributions towards improving police facilities were permissible, but warned that such support must not compromise police independence or confer legitimacy on suspected criminal groups.

The separate incidents have drawn attention to concerns about suspected cult groups and their activities in the region.

World.title: Diaz dazzles as Bayern Munich batter Leipzig 6-1 to go top
World.content:
Bayern Munich’s Colombian forward #14 Luis Diaz (C), Leipzig’s French defender #23 Castello Lukeba (L) and Leipzig’s German defender #16 Lukas Klostermann vie for the ball during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and RB Leipzig in Munich, southern Germany, on October 17, 2026. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP) / DFL REGULATIONS PROHIBIT ANY USE OF PHOTOGRAPHS AS IMAGE SEQUENCES AND/OR QUASI-VIDEO

Luis Diaz hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich pummelled a listless RB Leipzig 6-1 on Saturday to climb to the top of the Bundesliga.

Borussia Dortmund had briefly edged ahead of Freiburg into top spot after their earlier draw at Union Berlin, but Bayern responded in typically ruthless fashion.

In his 100th Bundesliga match, Harry Kane scored a goal and laid on two assists as he pulled the strings from deep, while Aleksandar Pavlovic and Michael Olise also got on the scoresheet.

The dominant display was probably Bayern’s best performance of the season and a boost to their confidence ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash with English champions Arsenal.

“A big game against one of the best in Europe, you have to enjoy these occasions,” Kane told reporters. “We’re testing ourselves against one of the best.”

Diaz had faced criticism after four league games without a goal but the Colombian sparked to life at the Allianz Arena in Munich, terrorising Leipzig defender Lukas Klostermann down the left.

“Lucho (Diaz) has had some criticism this season but he was excellent tonight. Definitely the man of the hour,” Bayern captain Joshua Kimmich said.

Confined to his chair with a hip complaint, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany produced a masterclass against opposite number Martin Demichelis, his former Manchester City teammate.

“You can come here and lose a match, but not like that,” Demichelis said to Sky Germany. Leipzig travel to face Real Madrid in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Bayern have now won their past three games against Leipzig by a combined scoreline of 17-1.

This result came after two successive draws, a rare run of middling form for the German giants, but they shook off the funk early on, with Diaz, Pavlovic and Olise putting the hosts in control before half-time.

Diaz scored either side of a Kane tap-in after the break, with the England captain and former Tottenham striker withdrawn before the hour mark ahead of old rivals Arsenal’s visit.

Leipzig’s Andrija Maksimovic got on the board with a consolation in stoppage time.

– Dortmund draw in Berlin –

Dortmund missed a chance to stay ahead of Bayern after being held to a scoreless draw at Union Berlin.

After starting the season strongly with six wins in a row in all competitions, Dortmund have stalled of late, drawing two and losing one of their last three matches.

“We simply have to get better in attack. Right now, it’s just not good enough,” Dortmund’s Waldemar Anton told Sky.

Serhou Guirassy had a golden chance to snatch all three points for his side at the end of a match of few opportunities, but headed just wide with 11 minutes remaining.

It was the first draw between the two sides in their history, with each of their previous 16 clashes in all competitions producing a winner.

Compounding Dortmund’s woes was a serious-looking ankle injury to substitute midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas, who was helped from the pitch just eight minutes after coming on.

“Let’s hope it’s not too serious. He’s not feeling great right now,” Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book told reporters.

Stuttgart suffered a blow ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Atletico Madrid, going down 1-0 at Hamburg after an 88th-minute Miro Muheim winner.

Elsewhere, promoted Elversberg continued their impressive debut season in the top flight, winning 4-3 at home to Augsburg.

Lukas Petkov, Lasse Guenther, Maximilian Rohr and Frederik Schmahl scored as Elversberg, from the smallest town to ever host a Bundesliga side, climbed to sixth in the table.

Niclas Fuellkrug scored for the fifth straight Bundesliga match as his brace helped Werder Bremen come from two goals down to draw 2-2 at home to Paderborn.

A first-half goal from Phillip Tietz was enough for Mainz to win 1-0 at Schalke and climb to fifth in the standings.

AFP

World.title: Hunters kill kidnappers who came for ₦10m ransom in Kano
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

Two suspected bandits have been killed by local hunters, while ₦10 million paid as ransom for a kidnapped man has been recovered in Falgore Forest, Doguwa Local Government Area of Kano State.

This was contained in a statement by CSP Abdullahi Haruna Kiyawa, Police Public Relations Officer on Saturday.

According to the statement, the kidnapped victim, identified as 45-year-old Kabiru Aliyu of Falgore Village, was released unharmed after the suspects collected the ransom

“The incident occurred at about midnight on Saturday, when three suspected bandits allegedly emerged from Falgore Forest to collect the money demanded for Aliyu’s release.

According to the statement, the victim was kidnapped on September 11, 2026, and had spent several days in captivity before his release.

The police said that shortly after collecting the ₦10 million ransom and releasing the victim, the suspects were ambushed by local hunters known as Yan Bula while returning to their hideout in Falgore Forest.

“During the ambush, two of the suspected bandits were neutralised, while the third suspect escaped with injuries. The entire ransom sum of ₦10 million was recovered intact from the neutralised suspects,” the statement said.

The command said preliminary investigations had identified one of the suspects killed as Dogo Isah, a commercial motorcycle rider from Maigwanda Village in Kubau Local Government Area of Kaduna State.

The police said the suspects were believed to have come from Maigwanda Village before the incident.

The Commissioner of Police in Kano State, CP Ibrahim Adamu Bakori, commended the Yan Bula hunters for their efforts in supporting security operations in the area.

Bakori said the hunters’ activities continued to complement the police operation against kidnapping, banditry and other violent crimes in the state under Operation Kukan Kura.

Following the incident, the commissioner directed the Area Commander, Divisional Police Officers and tactical teams operating in the area to immediately search the forest and surrounding communities for the fleeing suspect.

He also directed the teams to intensify efforts to arrest the suspect and recover any weapons used by the group.

The police further disclosed that the rescued victim had been debriefed, medically examined and reunited with his family.

The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property.

Vanguard News

World.title: Sahel states restart dialogue with ECOWAS
World.content:
Mali, Niiger and Burkina Faso junta leaders

Three junta-ruled Sahel states on Saturday resumed dialogue with the ECOWAS regional bloc which they quit over 18 months ago, agreeing to work together towards a cooperation “framework agreement”.

Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso, led by juntas that came to power between 2020 and 2023, left the Economic Community of West African States in January 2025, after teaming up to create their own group, the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

Talks between ECOWAS and the AES had been under way since January 2025 but Saturday was their first official ministerial meeting.

In a joint statement issued Saturday evening, the two sides “welcomed the spirit of fraternity, mutual respect and openness” of the talks, and stressed the importance of maintaining relations of “good neighbourliness” particularly with “respect for sovereignty”.

They agreed to “set up joint thematic working groups (…) to reach a framework cooperation agreement”.

The AES delegation was led by Karamoko Jean-Marie Traore, Burkina Faso’s foreign minister, and the Ecowas delegation by Cheikh Niang, his Senegalese counterpart.

The AES juntas have all turned their backs on France, the former colonial power, and by extension on several countries in the region such as Cete d’Ivoire and Benin, which they consider too close to Paris.

The trio have moved closer politically to Moscow, claiming an anti-imperialist and pro-sovereignty vision, and they have bitterly criticised west African coastal countries which have remained close to France.

World.title: Dubois destroys Wardley in round two to retain WBO heavyweight crown
World.content:
Daniel Dubois scored a crushing second-round knockout victory over fellow Briton Fabio Wardley to retain his World Boxing Organization heavyweight crown on Saturday.

In a much-anticipated rematch of their bruising 11-round classic earlier this year, Dubois dominated Wardley from the opening bell to batter his rival into submission in the second round.

Dubois dropped Wardley after 17 seconds of the contest at the O2 Arena in London, catching the challenger flush on the chin with a huge overhand right.

The 29-year-old Dubois continued to land punches at will throughout the first round, which finished with Wardley clinging on desperately under a barrage a punches on the ropes.

The second round started as the first had ended, with the 6ft 5in Dubois uncorking an array of punches that left Wardley in desperate trouble.

With Dubois unloading on a defenceless Wardley, the towel came in after two minutes and 21 seconds of the round.

Dubois improved to 24-3-0 with 23 knockouts while the 31-year-old Wardley fell to 20-2-1.

AFP

World.title: Ambassador Dele Cole devoted his life to national service — Tinubu
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has expressed sadness over the death of the veteran journalist and diplomat, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, saying that the late statesman devoted his life to national service.

Ambassador Cole died at the age of 86.

President Tinubu, in his tribute titled “Farewell to Ambassador Dele Cole, distinguished diplomat, journalist and public servant,” said the late veteran journalist brought distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.

The tribute read: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, and public servant, who died at 86.

“Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.

“His career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.

“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story.

“At 86, Ambassador Dele Cole witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service. His life stands as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.

“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time.

“May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss.”

World.title: Nigeria’s economy needs continuation of Tinubu’s reforms – Wike
World.content:
Photo: NAN

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says Nigeria’s full economic recovery depends entirely on sustaining the bold reform policies initiated by President Bola Tinubu.

Wike said this on Saturday, at the Rainbow Coalition’s stakeholders’ consultation in Ogba-Egbema-Ndoni Local Government Area of Rivers.

He said that only the continuation of the current administration’s economic direction could permanently pull the country back from the brink of collapse.

He noted that the hard economic choices being implemented presently were necessary remedies to salvage a system that was virtually “dead” when Tinubu took office.

“Only the continuation of the economic reforms initiated by the Tinubu government can bring this country back from the economic comatose it was in before this present administration took over,” he said.

He said that the presidential candidate of the Africa Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Abubakar Atiku and his vice, Rotimi Amaechi, had nothing to offer to Nigerians.

The minister urged residents of the state not to surrender the country’s progress to “career politicians” and “political opportunists” whom he likened to “chronic pool betters” who repeatedly gamble with public trust.

According to him, supporting politicians who have made decades-long pursuits for power would mean diverting national funds to recoup lost campaign expenses rather than consolidating economic gains.

Wike further said that the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, would not make any meaningful difference if elected, stressing that Tinubu was the person who had shown true commitment.

Reaffirming that leadership must be judged by past governance records, the former Rivers governor challenged his predecessor to account for major capital allocations in Rivers.

Explaining the political strategy behind the cross-party Rainbow Coalition movement, he said that delivering economic recovery required total alignment between the executive and the national assembly.

He urged voters to support Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates vying for the Senate and House of Representatives seats in the area to ensure legislative cooperation for the president’s economic policy agenda.

He also called on party leaders and community mobilisers to prepare for an overwhelming turnout on election day.

“I want total mobilisation on Jan. 16, 2027. Everybody must be mobilised. Make sure we vote and win decisively to protect our collective future,” he said.

In his remarks, the Executive Chairman of the council, Dr Chukwu Shedrack, commended Wike for his historic development projects in the council, including road construction, hospital upgrades, and human capital investments.

Shedrack highlighted several local governance achievements which he said aligned with the FCT minister’s leadership model.

Reaffirming the council’s political commitment to the Tinubu administration’s economic recovery drive, he pledged a complete block vote for the APC across all elective positions come 2027.

“We are fully mobilised, ward by ward and unit by unit. Come the 2027 general elections, our people will deliver 100 per cent. From president to national assembly and house of assembly, no vote will drop,” Shedrack assured. (NAN)

World.title: Benue 2027: Ex-Otukpo council chair, APC, ADC, ZLP chieftains defect to PDP
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

A former Caretaker Chairman of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue state, Mr. Inalegwu Adakonye, has defected from the All Progressives Congress (APC) to the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), alongside other political stakeholders and their supporters from the APC, African Democratic Congress (ADC) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP).

The defection featured several prominent political figures from Adoka and Ugboju communities in Otukpo council.

Among prominent politicians who weekend in Otukpo joined the PDP with the former chairman of Otukpo were Adoga Edache, popularly known as Ebo, from the ADC; Emmanuel Akoche of the ZLP; Garuba Sule of the APC; and Mr. John Ojonye, ADC Chairman of Ugboju Ehaji Ward, alongside other party members and supporters.

Explaining his decision to return to the PDP, Adakonye said the party’s ideology of inclusiveness and collective participation informed his choice, arguing that its approach to politics differed from that of the APC.

He said “the PDP treats its members as one family and offer a platform where everyone can participate. And I am confident that the party is best positioned to rescue Benue state from bad governance.”

Adakonye, who led APC members from Adoka and Ugboju into the PDP, also cited the emergence of Dr. Oyije Ogbenjuwa as the party’s deputy governorship candidate as a factor behind their decision.

He said they could not afford to remain outside the political movement of their brother and friend, who he expressed confidence would soon become the deputy governor of the state.

The defectors also cited the PDP’s people-oriented ideology, leadership and prospects in forthcoming elections as reasons for abandoning their former parties for the opposition platform.

Receiving the new members were the PDP deputy governorship candidate, Dr. Ogbenjuwa; the Otukpo Local Government PDP Chairman, Godwin Ochapa; the party’s House of Assembly candidate for Otukpo/Akpa, Johnson Egli; its candidate for Adoka/Ugboju, Gabriel Olofu; and the Senior Legislative Aide to the Senate President, Chief George Alli.

Speaking on behalf of the party, Ogbenjuwa welcomed the defectors and assured them of “equal opportunities and full integration into the party’s activities.”

He described their decision to join the PDP “as evidence of the party’s growing acceptability across Benue South Senatorial District, and your support will further strengthen our political base ahead of future elections.”

The new members, in turn, pledged their loyalty and commitment to working for the success of the PDP at all levels.

World.title: Oyedele: World Markets Have Written Off Opposition, Eyeing Tinubu’s 2nd Term
World.content:
•Rules out return to fuel subsidy, warns of risks to naira

•CBN seeks Chinese capital, deeper financial ties to boost investment in Nigeria

• World Bank report: ADC asks Tinubu to explain ‘missing’ $12.4bn

Nume Ekeghe in Bangkok, Thailand and Chuks Okocha in Abuja

The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said financial markets and the international community have largely written off Nigeria’s opposition political parties as unserious, with investors already pricing in the prospects of President Bola Tinubu securing a second term and expecting continuity in his economic reforms.

This is just as the Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, also said policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Meanwhile, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, an equivalent of about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

Oyedele and Cardoso spoke at the closing press briefing of the IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, where the CBN governor said policy consistency would be critical to attracting long-term capital, sustaining economic stability and accelerating growth.

On his part, Oyedele argued that investors’ expectations of continuity under Tinubu had influenced their assessment of Nigeria’s economic outlook, including their response to opposition proposals to restore fuel subsidies.

“In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious. That is why they have not priced in the proposed return of subsidy,” he said.

He added that any indication that the president intended to restore the subsidy would immediately be reflected in market prices.

“So, maybe the international and domestic markets are aware about who is sincere about Nigeria and what direction they should travel,” he said.

“As I said, the markets and the international community have been pricing in the prospect of a second term for the President, and they expect continuity in the reforms.”

The minister’s comments followed repeated questions from investors about whether the government would sustain its policies as Nigeria approaches another election cycle.

He said concerns about possible policy reversals had featured prominently in his engagements with investors in Thailand and during two visits to London, particularly over whether electoral pressures could force the administration to abandon its reform agenda.

“Throughout the meetings we have had this week, as well as those I attended before now, including two visits to London to meet investors, one question has repeatedly come up: Are you going to reverse your reforms? Are you under pressure because of elections?” he said.

According to Oyedele, the government remained committed to the reforms, which he described as necessary to restore macroeconomic stability and lay the foundation for sustainable growth.

He said the next phase of the economic programme would focus on translating the gains in stability into stronger investment, lower financing costs, job creation and improved economic opportunities for Nigerians.

Oyedele said private investment had increased twentyfold since the reforms began, rising from about $300 million in 2023 to $6 billion in 2026.

He also highlighted improvements in Nigeria’s external position, saying net reserves had risen from barely $3 billion to more than $45 billion, representing a fifteen-fold increase.

Oyedele ruled out a return to fuel subsidies and multiple exchange rates, warning that reversing the reforms could undermine investor confidence, trigger capital flight and put renewed pressure on the naira.

“Let me be clear: there will be no return to fuel subsidies or multiple exchange rates,” he said.

“If, for any reason, Mr President were to say today that we were considering bringing back fuel subsidies, what happened in Indonesia would be child’s play in comparison,” he said.

“At the end of the day, capital would leave because investors understand what such a decision means.”

He argued that capital flight could intensify pressure on the foreign exchange market and weaken the naira, with the consequences ultimately borne by ordinary Nigerians.

“When capital leaves, the foreign-exchange market will come under pressure, and the naira will crash. The exchange rate could move to N3,000, N3,500 or N4,000 to the dollar,” he said.

Oyedele said such a development would worsen the economic pressures facing households.

The minister also defended the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s recent temporary reduction in petrol retail margins, insisting that it was a commercial decision rather than a subsidy financed with public funds.

“The recent temporary reduction in the retail margin on fuel was a time-bound commercial decision by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited to reduce margins and support Nigerians,” he said.

“It is not a subsidy paid for with public funds.”

He explained that a company’s decision to reduce its profit margin to lower prices should not automatically be classified as a subsidy.

“If you offer a discount by reducing that profit margin, how does that become a subsidy?” he asked.

Cardoso: Policy Consistency, Transparency Critical to Investor Confidence

Meanwhile, Cardoso has stressed that policy consistency and transparency were essential to sustaining investor confidence, as improvements in economic and foreign exchange stability created better conditions for long-term investment.

Cardoso said Nigeria was seeking to deepen financial cooperation with China to attract more Asian investment into its markets and improve cross-border payments, settlement arrangements and trade finance.

He disclosed that discussions with the Governor of the People’s Bank of China, Pan Gongsheng, had focused on practical ways to strengthen cooperation among financial institutions in both countries.

Cardoso said China’s developed payments infrastructure offered lessons for Nigeria, while stronger financial links could facilitate trade and investment between the two economies.

He said the discussions would be followed by technical engagements during his forthcoming visit to Beijing, where officials would examine specific areas of cooperation and identify initiatives capable of delivering practical results.

The CBN governor said Nigeria was particularly interested in attracting Chinese capital into its financial markets, noting that investment in Nigerian financial instruments had remained limited despite the substantial liquidity available in China.

“Finally, bear in mind that, despite the considerable liquidity available in China, there has not been much investment in Nigerian financial instruments over time,” he said.

“This could be an opportunity to change that trajectory and generate greater interest from Asian markets in Nigerian instruments and African instruments generally.”

Cardoso said the initiative formed part of a broader effort to strengthen Nigeria’s financial relationships with Asian economies and expand the pool of capital available to domestic markets.

World Bank Report: ADC Asks Tinubu-led Govt to Explain ‘Missing’ $12.4bn

Meanwhile, the ADC has called on President Tinubu to explain the $12.4 billion gap, equivalent to about N16.5 trillion, in Nigeria’s external accounts identified in the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update.

In a statement issued yesterday by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said Tinubu owed Nigerians a clear account of the discrepancy, especially as families struggling with the cost-of-living crisis were forced to account for every naira.

Citing the report, the ADC said Nigeria recorded a $12 billion current-account surplus and $6.2 billion in net financial inflows in the first half of 2026.

The party said these inflows should have strengthened the country’s reserves, but the report instead identified a $12.4 billion gap.

Abdullahi said the World Bank attributed the gap, in part, to oil export earnings that were not repatriated. He added that the report noted that the repatriation of export proceeds remained limited, partly because Nigerian oil had been pledged against several long-term loans.

“The scale is staggering,” the ADC said.

“This unexplained gap is larger than the entire current-account surplus for the same period. It is about 5.6 times the $2.2 billion Nigeria attracted in foreign direct investment. In naira terms, it is almost a quarter of the N68.32 trillion 2026 federal budget.

“This cannot be dismissed as a minor accounting discrepancy. President Tinubu welcomed this report. He cannot celebrate one part of the report and stay silent on a gap bigger than the surplus that he and his government are celebrating.

“Due to President Tinubu’s failed policies, families across Nigeria are forced to skip meals and account for every naira just to survive. Meanwhile, money that could have eased their hardship is currently unaccounted for. Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation.

“Sacrifice cannot be compulsory for everyday citizens while accountability remains optional for the government that is in charge of our collective resources.”

The ADC called on the federal government to publish a full public reconciliation of the $12.4 billion gap and disclose all oil-backed loans and pledged crude commitments.

It also demanded updated net reserve figures and clear evidence that higher revenues were improving essential services such as health, education and power.

“President Tinubu must open the books. Nigerians have sacrificed enough. We deserve answers,” the party said.

World.title: North Will Give Tinubu Over 70% of Votes in 2027, Says Yilwatda
World.content:
•Shettima: Region will re-elect president

•Makinde will defeat Tinubu in his 12 battleground states, others, says campaign council

Deji Elumoye, Chuks Okocha and Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has predicted that the North will give President Bola Tinubu more than 70 per cent of its votes in the 2027 presidential election.

Vice President Kashim Shettima has also said the North will re-elect Tinubu, stressing that the region had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction for Tinubu’s re-election.

But the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Speaking yesterday in Abuja when Shettima unveiled the Arewa for Asiwaju Campaign Head Office and formally inaugurated the campaign structure of the northern think tank, Yilwatda urged people in the North to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing infrastructure projects, appointments and other initiatives of the President’s administration.

The APC chairman listed road projects across northern states, the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline, irrigation dams, railway projects, healthcare initiatives and the Nigerian Education Loan Fund among the interventions he said should encourage the North to support Tinubu for a second term.

“I can’t mention all of them, but President Bola Tinubu has done wonderfully. He has covered all the geopolitical zones in the North in terms of road projects,” he added.

He moved a motion for the northern region to support the re-election of the Tinubu/Shettima ticket, outlining reasons why the region should mobilize massively for the president.

He noted that the region’s strong backing stems from the Vice President’s inclusive leadership and progressive mindset over the past three years.

Shettima: Region Will Re-elect President in 2027

Also speaking, Shettima declared that the North will re-elect Tinubu, adding however, that the growing northern support for president’s re-election was not a blank check.

According to him, Tinubu’s administration will earn it through facts, radical transparency and measurable results.

He maintained that expanding loyalty in the region would demand greater accountability and an honest dialogue with citizens about ongoing reforms undertaken by the administration.

Shettima said the North had spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction in its support for the President.

According to him, renewed political confidence should never be taken for granted, adding that the government and its supporters must continue to engage Nigerians with facts and show how the ongoing reforms are improving security, livelihoods, and economic opportunity.

“By now, I believe the North has spoken. We have spoken with a resounding voice and unmistakable conviction. From Adamawa to Zamfara, from Borno to Niger, we have spoken. Such confidence places an obligation upon us that no officeholder should ever underestimate,” he stated.

The Vice President noted that President Tinubu’s bid for a renewed mandate must rest on the administration’s record and a clear account of how another term would advance Nigerians’ interests.

He restated that the North had nothing to fear in President Tinubu’s second term as Nigeria’s leader.

Shettima acknowledged that Nigerians had endured difficult economic adjustments, warning campaigners against dismissing genuine concerns or relying on political slogans to defend government policies.

“Our citizens have endured difficult adjustments. We cannot pretend otherwise. What we owe them is an honest account of the decisions taken, the gains achieved and the difficulties that persist. We lose our hearing when applause becomes our only source of information,” he added.

The Vice President said the concerns of traders facing higher costs, graduates searching for work and families struggling with daily expenses must remain central to government decision-making.

“A failed policy enters somebody’s home as a missed meal, an unpaid school fee or an opportunity lost,” he said.

He also defended criticism as essential to democratic governance, saying the administration must remain open to useful ideas irrespective of political affiliation, ethnicity, religion or region.

“There is no democracy without critics. Progress demands that our assumptions endure the examination of those who disagree with us,” Shettima said.

The Vice President said the administration’s priorities remain security, economic opportunity, poverty reduction, education and stronger public institutions.

“The farmer should be able to cultivate in safety. A child’s education should prepare that child for a productive life. Public institutions should give citizens confidence that effort can yield opportunity,” he said.

Earlier, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin said the inauguration of the A4A structure for the 2027 presidential elections came at a time when the region needed a strong, trusted platform to mobilise support for Tinubu.

Similarly, Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, said history was beckoning the North to act with wisdom and evidence, not sentiment, in its decision to support the Tinubu administration in the 2027 elections.

On his part, Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, speaking on behalf of all the governors of the North, said the northern region’s support for the President in the forthcoming elections would be based on its conviction to uphold fairness, equity, unity and the progress of the country.

In his welcome address, the Director General of A4A and former Jigawa State governor, Abubakar Mohammed Badaru, said the group’s emergence was not accidental, but born of the conviction that President Tinubu and his deputy have performed well and deserve re-election.

Makinde Will Defeat Tinubu in His 12 Battleground States, Others, Says Campaign Council

Meanwhile, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has declared that its presidential candidate on the platform of the APM, Governor Makinde will defeat Tinubu in the 12 battleground states identified by the president, as well as in other states across the federation.

Makinde also declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem is grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

The MDPCO, in a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Hon. Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, asserted that Makinde would decisively defeat Tinubu and his APC Presidential Campaign Council in Rivers State and the FCT, insisting that no amount of political manoeuvring, intimidation or abuse of incumbency by the President’s henchmen can reverse the growing tide of opposition to his re-election.

The organisation said the arrogance and political overreach of Tinubu’s inner circle had deepened public resentment and further weakened his electoral prospects.

It added that President Tinubu’s decision to personally visit and campaign in only 12 states — Oyo, Kaduna, Rivers, Plateau, Borno, Enugu, Bauchi, Sokoto, Delta, Kano, Adamawa and Lagos — further confirmed his apprehension over the mileage and foothold already achieved by Makinde with his RESET NIGERIA Agenda message in the aforementioned and other states of the federation.

“Mr President should know that his visit to these states, if he eventually does, will not in any way change the direction or the determination of the people to vote him out, given his unpardonable failures in office which have brought unprecedented hardship across the country,” the organisation said.

“President Tinubu has no meaningful achievement he can boast of in these and other states of the federation where Nigerians now refer to his government as ‘T-Pain’ following the suffering they have been subjected to by the policies of the Tinubu administration in the last three and a half years.”

The MDPCO challenged President Tinubu not to have a change of mind but to visit the states to face the people.

“We challenge President Tinubu to travel around the country by road and witness the decrepit state of federal highways, the squalor in which Nigerians live and the level of infrastructural decay across the country, while his government squanders trillions of Naira on white elephant projects and wasteful programmes.

“If President Tinubu believes he is popular as he claims, he should not stop at the rally ground or at the airport when he gets to any of the states. He should go beyond waving to a gathering of APC rented crowd and be bold enough to directly engage the people in the communities and towns to seek their votes, as the APM candidate, Makinde, has been doing since he started his campaign,” it said.

“Nigerians are gravitating towards the core campaign pillars and proposals in Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda, which include the establishment of an all-inclusive, four-year transitional government of national unity with four priority pillars of education, economy, security and socio-political policies.

“Unlike President Tinubu’s visionless, thoughtless and rudderless rule characterised by crass arbitrariness, Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA Agenda offers data-driven strategies that revolve around tackling poverty through massive production; a security plan that prioritises intelligence gathering, social reorientation and decisive kinetic and non-kinetic actions; an education plan that focuses on expanding access to quality functional education; and institutional reform that emphasises inclusive governance and sincere public leadership.”

The campaign urged Tinubu “not to waste the nation’s resources on his ‘Nebuchadnezzar’ Campaign Council of failed politicians who, like the president himself, cannot attract votes from Nigerians.”

In another development, Makinde has declared that Nigeria’s biggest problem was grinding poverty, not religion, urging Christians to stop shunning politics and take an active role in transforming the country.

He said Christians could not afford to stand aloof from politics because it was dirty or because they should not serve under leaders who did not share their faith, stressing that national transformation required their active participation.

Makinde spoke yesterday in Abuja after receiving a Christian Icon Award at the Christian Association of Nigeria’s (CAN) 50th anniversary celebration.

The governor said Christians should draw lessons from biblical figures who accepted difficult assignments in pursuit of a greater purpose.

Makinde cited David, who, despite having been anointed king, served in the palace of Saul, from whom God had departed.

World.title: Tinubu Mourns as Journalist, Ex-Nigerian Ambassador, Dele Cole, Dies in London at 86
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja



President Bola Tinubu last night expressed profound sadness at the news of the passing of a distinguished diplomat, journalist, politician, historian and elder statesman, Ambassador Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at 86.

Cole’s death was confirmed yesterday by a family source, who disclosed that the former Nigerian ambassador died earlier in the morning following weeks of deteriorating health.



The source revealed that Cole had recently been discharged from the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), but his health had continued to decline.

“He left ICU a few days ago. He had been doing poorly in recent weeks leading to this end,” the family source said.

Born on August 4, 1940, Cole turned 86 in August, barely two months before his death.

He was widely known for his contributions to Nigeria’s diplomatic service, journalism, and historical scholarship, having held several prominent positions throughout his career.



Before entering diplomatic service, Cole established himself in Nigeria’s media industry, serving on the editorial board of The Guardian newspaper and subsequently as Managing Director of Daily Times, one of the country’s most influential newspapers.

He later represented Nigeria as Ambassador to Argentina and Brazil, extending his public service career into international diplomacy.

He served as Special Adviser on International Relations under President Obasanjo from 1999 to 2007. He was also appointed Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil and Argentina.



He also ventured into politics and was associated with the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in the 1990s.

Beyond his diplomatic assignments, Cole was recognised for his involvement in national discourse, particularly on governance, politics, and Nigeria’s historical development.



His career spanned journalism, public administration, and diplomacy, placing him among a generation of Nigerian public figures who contributed to the country’s political and institutional development.

In a statement he personally signed, President Tinubu said Ambassador Cole devoted his life to national service, bringing distinction to his work in diplomacy, journalism and politics.



Tinubu noted that Cole’s career reflected the enduring value of dialogue, tact, mutual respect and the pursuit of shared interests in advancing national development and international cooperation.

“His contributions to Nigeria’s media landscape were particularly notable. As Managing Director of the Daily Times, he upheld the vital role of the press in holding public officials accountable, speaking truth to power, and strengthening democratic governance. His legacy in journalism and public life remains an enduring part of our national story,” Tinubu explained.



The president added that at 86, the deceased witnessed defining moments in Nigeria’s history and contributed to the nation’s development through his work in the media, diplomacy and public service.



According to Tinubu, his life stood as a testament to the value of experience, principled engagement and commitment to the public good.

“As we mourn his passing, I extend my heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, professional associates and all whose lives he touched. I pray that memories of his remarkable life will bring them comfort and strength at this difficult time. May Almighty God grant Ambassador Cole eternal rest and give his family and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this profound loss,” the statement added.

World.title: Over 40 Companies Raise N2.45 Trillion from Stock Market in Nine Months
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Over 40 companies raised N2.45 trillion from the Nigerian capital market between January and September 2026, as businesses positioned themselves for growth amid persistent economic pressures, according to data on corporate listings on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX).



The capital-raising surge underscores the NGX’s growing importance as a source of long-term financing for businesses seeking alternatives to expensive bank loans.

Data on corporate listings on the NGX show total corporate capital raising hit about N2.45 trillion in nine months of 2026, covering public offers, private placements and supplementary listings.



The surge came as the Nigerian Exchange Limited All-Share Index gained 61.43 per cent year-to-date (YtD) as of September 2026 to 251,211.67 basis points, making Nigeria one of Africa’s best-performing exchanges.

Among the over 40 companies are: Dangote Sugar Refinery, which raised N485.88 billion through a rights issue; Abbey Bank raised N64.547 billion; Guinea Insurance listed 12.673 billion new shares; Regency Alliance Insurance raised N6.051 billion; Sunu Assurance raised N9.339 billion; Sovereign Trust Insurance raised N5.022 billion; Neimeth International Pharmaceuticals raised N2.442 billion; Critical Minerals Financing Corporation raised N1.807 billion and Eunisell Interlinked raised N200 million, among others.



Of the corporate listings, Fidelity Bank Plc, United Bank for Africa Plc (UBA), FCMB Group Plc, First HoldCo Plc, Access Holdings Plc, Sterling Financial Holdings Company Plc and Guaranty Trust Holding Company Plc led the listed firms, with listings of N883.8 billion in the period under review.



The N883.8 billion listing on the NGX by these four financial institutions came against the backdrop of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) policy mandating that firms raise fresh equity to meet paid-up capital thresholds.

As GTCO listed N10 billion after a successful private placement of 125,000,000 ordinary shares of 50 kobo each at N80.00 per share, NGX admitted UBA’s and First Holdco’s N157.8 billion and N128.7 billion rights issue and private placement in early January 2026, respectively. Access Holdings, N21.4 billion; FCMB Group, N231.83 billion; Sterling Financial Holding Company, N106.978 billion; and Fidelity Bank, N227.05 billion, were new listings on NGX.



The Managing Director of Globalview Capital Limited, Mr. Aruna Kebira, said the recent surge reflected rising investor confidence in the Nigerian Exchange, not apathy, and that confidence is key to capacity building.

Speaking on market participation, Kebira said innovations, improved transparency and the T+1 settlement cycle, where investors get proceeds a day after selling, have deepened retail participation and awareness.

Kebira cited the Dangote Refinery offer, where platforms like OPay and banks actively mobilised investors, as a driver of serious market awareness.



He said the market had evolved significantly since 2011 and was aligning with global standards, moving away from the speculative ‘kalokalo’ approach seen in 2004.

On funding options, Kebira said equity remained the cheapest way to run and expand a manufacturing organisation, as interest on bank loans must be paid regardless of profitability, while equity allowed profits to be ploughed back into the company to do more for shareholders.



He added that the funds had a multiplier effect on capacity expansion, technology adoption and job creation.

He said boards would be under pressure to deliver value, increase production, pay good dividends and put square pegs in square holes because reputation was at stake, adding that the recapitalisation in insurance was necessary to restore the ability to pay claims and rebuild public confidence in the sector.



On his part, the National Chairman of New Dimension Shareholders Association, Mr. Patrick Ajudua, however, stated that fresh capital raising did not automatically translate to higher dividends or immediate job creation.

“You need to know that investment has a risk element. Not all companies that raise fresh capital deliver better dividends,” Ajudua said.

He noted that, in fairness, many companies had delivered dividends, particularly since this administration came to power, which stabilised the economy, especially the foreign exchange market.

World.title: Kwara APC: Ex-VC Leads High-profile Group to Resolve Disputes, Reconcile Aggrieved Members
World.content:
Elder statesman and former Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ilorin, Prof. Oba AbdulRaheem, is leading a group of prominent Kwara indigenes to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and mobilise support for the party ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group, which held its inaugural meeting at Abdulraheem’s Ilorin residence on September 17, said it is committed to resolving all disagreements that trailed the outcome of the APC’s primaries.

Abdulraheem, also a former Chairman of the Federal Character Commission (FCC), chairs the group, the Kwara APC Peace Committee.

Apart from Abdulraheem, eminent indigenes of Kwara in the group include Dr. Johnson Adewumi, a foremost educationist/ entrepreneur and founder of the Thomas Adewumi University, Oko; former Minister and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Issa Bio Ibrahim; and former Secretary to Kwara State Government and former Member, Federal House of Representatives, Hon. AbdulGaniyu Cook Olododo.

Other members include Oloriewe Raheem Adedoyin, a veteran journalist and member representing Africa in the Executive Board of the International Press Institute; elder statesman and former Speaker, Kwara State House of Assembly, Hon. Benjamin Ezekiel Issa; elder statesman and Member of Tinubu Shettina PCC, Pastor John Dara; and former Commissioner, Federal Character Commission, Hon. James Jiya Kolo.

According to the statement, the committee intends to serve as a voice of conscience among APC leaders by addressing internal grievances and promoting the achievements of the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

It said the group had reached out to some aggrieved political leaders and influential stakeholders to encourage reconciliation and forge a common front ahead of the elections.

The committee is also canvassing support for the APC’s governorship candidate, Hon. Yakubu Danladi, and other party candidates in the state.

The statement said the initiative aimed to secure the backing of party stakeholders for the candidates and strengthen cohesion within the APC ahead of the general election.

World.title: Elumelu Backs $15bn Infrastructure Investment Drive Across West Africa
World.content:
Festus Akanbi

Heirs Holdings Chairman Mr Tony Elumelu is backing efforts to assemble a $15 billion portfolio of infrastructure projects across West Africa, as regional leaders and investors seek to turn economic integration ambitions into bankable investments.

The initiative, being developed ahead of the inaugural West Africa Integration and Investment Summit (WAIIS) in Sierra Leone next month, will bring selected projects before prospective financiers to mobilise capital for infrastructure and productive enterprises.

Elumelu, who co-chairs the summit, disclosed the plans in an emailed response to questions from Bloomberg, which reported the development on Thursday.

Potential financiers include United Bank for Africa (UBA), the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank), Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Africa50. Priority sectors comprise energy, trade, industrialisation, strategic minerals, agriculture and digital infrastructure.

The proposed $15 billion represents the anticipated value of the investment pipeline, rather than funding already committed by Elumelu or the participating financial institutions.

Organisers have so far shortlisted 26 projects worth more than $10 billion from 170 submissions spanning more than 10 countries, with expectations that the portfolio will expand before the November gathering.

Special Envoy for WAIIS, Dr Kandeh Kolleh Yumkella, said the selection reflected progress towards presenting investors with concrete opportunities across the region.

“We received 170 project submissions and have selected 26 real projects worth more than $10 billion from over ten countries,” Yumkella said in a statement issued by the organisers.

“We expect that portfolio to reach $15 billion or more,” he added.

Convened by Sierra Leone’s President, Julius Maada Bio, the summit is scheduled for November 17 and 18 at the Julius Maada Bio International Conference Centre in Lungi. It will bring together governments, business leaders, project developers and development finance institutions to advance strategic regional investments.

The investment drive places project preparation and access to finance at the centre of West Africa’s integration agenda. Its immediate task is to connect viable proposals with institutions capable of financing their development, while aligning commercial opportunities with national and regional priorities.

Energy and transport connections, agricultural investment and digital networks are central to that ambition, offering opportunities to strengthen trade, expand production and improve access to markets.

The initiative also comes against the backdrop of efforts to develop major cross-border infrastructure, including the proposed $25 billion Nigeria–Morocco Gas Pipeline, also known as the African Atlantic Gas Pipeline.

Backed by the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the project is intended to carry Nigerian natural gas through several West African countries to Morocco, with potential connections to European markets.

The proposed gas link illustrates the scale of the region’s infrastructure ambitions and the importance of coordinating governments, project sponsors and financiers across national boundaries. It is a separate undertaking from the investment portfolio being assembled for the summit.

Elumelu’s involvement in the regional financing initiative coincides with the expansion of his interests in Nigeria’s energy sector.

According to Nairametrics, Heirs Energies Limited acquired an additional six million shares in Seplat Energy Plc on September 30, increasing the combined holdings of Heirs Energies and Heirs Holdings from 120.4 million to 126.4 million shares.

The acquisition raised their combined voting interest from 20.07 per cent to 21.07 per cent.

A separate analysis by the publication estimated that the combined market value of Elumelu’s holdings in Seplat, UBA and Transnational Corporation Plc rose by N684.59 billion between June and September, reaching approximately N2.43 trillion.

For the West African initiative, the next milestone is presenting the shortlisted projects to prospective financiers in Sierra Leone, where the proposed portfolio will be tested against investors’ financing requirements.
