World.title: Shirley Manson’s Garbage to headline free Zócalo show next month
World.content:
Garbage in the Zócalo! And for free?

No, we’re not talking about a sanitation worker’s revolt or some weird twist to recycling and reusing household waste.

The American rock band Garbage will play a free concert in the Zócalo on Saturday, Nov. 14, the final show of their North America tour which kicked off back in September 2025.

Lead singer Shirley Manson, aka “The Godmother of Rock,” said the show will mark the close of 30 years of traditional, continuous bus-touring for the band, saying long-term heavy touring has become economically and personally unsustainable.

Shortly after the Mexico City mayor’s office jumped the gun (officials shared the announcement through the government’s official X account before deleting the post), Garbage confirmed the gig on Instagram.

“Well. The news got leaked so here we are — a little off balance and rushing to catch up,” the band wrote. “We were going to announce this show tomorrow, but someone has beaten us to it.”

Overcoming the spilled beans, Garbage — which has sold 17 million albums worldwide — declared they were enthusiastic about the invitation.

“We are so immensely proud and deeply honoured to have been invited by the Mexican Government to play in Mexico City on the 14th of November at Mexico City’s most prestigious venue – The Zócalo,” the band said.

Manson also heaped praise on the band’s Mexican fans for supporting the group since their first visit in 1996. Since then, Garbage has played in Mexico 16 times, including three shows last year (April 4 in Zapopan, Jalisco; April 6 in Monterrey and Nov. 14 in Mexico City).

“We are one of the most fortunate bands in the world to have enjoyed playing in Mexico since we first arrived on the scene but this is the absolute cherry on the top of what has been a passionate and 30 year long love affair,” the Instagram post said.

Formed in 1993 in Madison, Wisconsin, the band’s four-member line-up has remained unchanged: the Scottish lead singer Manson and American musicians Duke Erikson (guitar, bass, keyboards), Steve Marker (guitar, keyboards) and Butch Vig (drums, percussion).

With reports from El Financiero, Consequence, Chilango and Billboard

World.title: Spain Regularisation Drew 1.17 Million Applications
World.content:
SPAIN · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening Spain’s extraordinary migrant regularisation closed on 30 June 2026 with 1,174,978 applications, the Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration reported on 2 July. — Why it matters The volume is well above the government’s initial estimate. If most files succeed, hundreds of thousands of workers, many of them Latin American, move into Spain’s formal economy, with consequences for residency planning and remittances. — The numbers Of the 1,174,978 applications, 609,737 had been admitted for processing by 2 July. About 79.6% sought the new extraordinary-roots permit and 20.4% came from asylum seekers, and 83.2% were filed online. Spain counted 7,437,543 foreign nationals on 1 July 2026, according to the national statistics institute INE, with Colombians, Venezuelans and Moroccans the largest groups arriving in the second quarter. — Who is who The Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration, led by Minister Elma Saiz, ran the process. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez presented the wider Integration and Citizenship Plan on 30 June, and the opposition People’s Party (PP) leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has called the measure a pull factor. — What to watch Files still in review face a three-month decision limit under the decree, after which silence counts as a refusal, and approved holders must request their foreigner identity card within one month. — What it means for you Americans with Spanish residency plans should not treat this scheme as a fallback, since it covered people already in Spain without status before 1 January 2026, not future legal applicants.

Spain’s extraordinary regularisation closed on 30 June 2026 with 1,174,978 applications, well above the government’s initial estimate. For Americans weighing Spanish residency or tracking Latin American migration, it shows how far Spain now relies on newcomers, many of them Latin American, to fill its workforce.

Spain has long been Europe’s gateway for Latin American migration, and this decree tested whether an administrative fix can turn an informal population into taxpayers, payroll workers and banked consumers. This analysis explains who could apply, what the permit allows, how Latin Americans fit into the picture and what is still unresolved.

Background comes from the Europe Intelligence Brief of 17 October 2026.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Regularisation Actually Was

Spain’s extraordinary regularisation was not an automatic amnesty. It was created by Royal Decree 316/2026 of 14 April, published in the state gazette (BOE) on 15 April 2026, which amends the Immigration Regulation approved by Royal Decree 1155/2024.

The decree entered into force the next day, and the application window ran from 16 April to 30 June 2026. Successful applicants receive a one-year residence permit that lets them live and work anywhere in Spain, as employees or self-employed, in any sector.

There were two routes. One was for people who had applied for international protection (asylum) before 1 January 2026.

The other, the “extraordinary roots” permit, was for people who were in Spain before that date without any permit.

Applications could be filed online or in person at Post Office (Correos), Social Security and immigration offices. The ministry said 448 offices were enabled nationwide.

File photo: a street in Sabadell, Catalonia. Spain counted 7,437,543 foreign nationals on 1 July 2026.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Spain Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Qualified and Who Did Not

For the extraordinary-roots permit, an applicant had to be an adult, be in Spain when applying and have been in the country before 1 January 2026. The decree also required five months of uninterrupted presence before filing, which could be shown by any valid evidence carrying the person’s identity details.

Applicants also needed a copy of a passport or travel document, which could be expired. They needed no criminal record, with records that can be cancelled in Spain set aside, and could not be a threat to public order, public security or public health.

On top of that, each applicant had to meet at least one of three conditions. They had worked in Spain or could show a job offer or a self-employment declaration; they lived with a family unit that included minor children, dependent adults or parents; or they were in a situation of vulnerability certified by social services or an accredited non-profit.

Several groups were excluded. People who already held a stay or residence permit, people with a pending procedure for one, and anyone who had held Ukrainian temporary protection could not use this route.

The Latin American Weight

The ministry’s closing tally, as we could find it, gives no breakdown of applicants by nationality. The wider population data show why Latin Americans matter in this story.

As of 1 July 2026, Spain counted 7,437,543 foreign nationals, up 87,197 in the second quarter, according to INE. Colombians were the largest group of arrivals in that quarter at 34,000, followed by Venezuelans at 23,300 and Moroccans at 21,100.

Departures offset part of that inflow: 11,500 Colombians and 5,900 Venezuelans left over the same three months. These figures cover people with regular status, so they do not measure the undocumented population.

They do show that Colombian and Venezuelan migration into Spain is large and ongoing. How many of the 1.17 million applicants held those passports is not yet public.

The Political Divide

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez presented the regularisation as part of a wider Integration and Citizenship Plan on 30 June 2026, the day the window closed. The plan has four axes, 16 measures and 10 objectives for 2030.

The government says the plan has an allocation of more than €505 million for 2026, reviewed each year (about US$568 million at the RT rate of US$1.124 per euro). It includes the regularisation, legal labour-mobility channels, integration measures and a planned State Agency for Human Mobility.

The decree’s own preamble argues that Spain faces rapid ageing and negative natural population growth, and that bringing working-age people into the system helps balance contributors and pensioners. It also cites sectors that struggle to hire.

Opponents disagree. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo has called the mass regularisation an “irresponsibility” with an obvious pull effect.

Economic and Business Stakes

For Spanish employers, the scheme can turn informal workers into declared employees with payroll records and social-security contributions. A provisional right to work began as soon as processing started, so hiring did not have to wait for the final decision.

For remittance businesses, regularisation could move some workers from cash pay to banked income. That may improve access to leases, credit and formal remittance channels, though we found no official estimate of the fiscal or remittance effect.

The application fee was €38.28 (about US$43), set by Order PJC/617/2025 for exceptional-circumstances residence permits.

If it is expressly refused, the provisional right to work ends.

What It Means for You

For Americans considering Spanish residency, this scheme is not a substitute for ordinary immigration routes. It was aimed at people already in Spain without regular status, not future applicants entering legally under the digital-nomad visa, non-lucrative residence or employment permits.

A US citizen who enters Spain legally should use the route that matches their plans. A person who overstays should not treat this scheme as a predictable fallback, because the window has closed and the decree set a cut-off date.

Nationality also differs by passport. Under Article 22 of the Spanish Civil Code, nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal, plus Sephardic Jews, can apply for citizenship after two years of legal residence, while most other nationalities, including Americans, need ten.

For US readers comparing immigration debates, Spain used an executive decree with a fixed deadline and a one-year initial permit. US regularisation proposals generally run through Congress and statutory eligibility categories, so the two systems are legally distinct even where the political arguments overlap.

What Is Not Known

The final number of approved applications is not yet public, and we did not find a breakdown of applicants by nationality. The ministry’s 2 July tally said 609,737 files had been admitted for processing, not how many were granted.

The government has not published an estimate of the fiscal or remittance effect that we could find. How many holders will secure an ordinary residence route after the first year is also unknown.

What to Watch

Files still in review run on the decree’s clock: three months from entry in the competent office’s register, after which silence counts as a refusal. The clock can be suspended while an applicant corrects defects, and the provisional permission to work stays valid in the meantime.

Within one month of a favourable decision, the applicant must request the foreigner identity card (Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero).

We found no sign of a new application window in the official sources. The continuing events are administrative: decisions, appeals and the first-year permit changes.

The Integration and Citizenship Plan’s budget will be a benchmark for whether the wider agenda, including the planned State Agency for Human Mobility, moves forward in 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who qualified for Spain’s migrant regularisation in 2026?

Adults who were in Spain before 1 January 2026, either without any permit or as asylum applicants, with five months of continuous presence and no relevant criminal record. Most also had to show work, a family unit with minors or dependants, or certified vulnerability. The window closed on 30 June 2026.

How many people applied?

The Ministry of Inclusion, Social Security and Migration reported 1,174,978 applications at the close on 30 June 2026, well above the government’s initial estimate. By 2 July it had admitted 609,737 of them for processing.

Is Spain’s regularisation an amnesty?

No. It was an application procedure with documentary requirements and an administrative decision. Successful applicants receive a one-year residence and work permit, not permanent status.

Can Americans apply for Spain’s regularisation?

No, not in practice. The scheme covered people who were already in Spain before 1 January 2026, and the window is closed. Americans planning to move should use ordinary routes such as the digital-nomad visa or non-lucrative residence.

What happens after the one-year permit?

Holders can ask to change to another residence authorisation under the royal decree and the ministry’s guidance.

How much did the application cost?

The fee was €38.28 (about US$43 at US$1.124 per euro) for the exceptional-circumstances residence permit, set by Order PJC/617/2025.

World.title: Indonesia Could Lose Emerging Market Status
World.content:
INDONESIA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening On 15 October 2026 MSCI opened a consultation on moving Indonesia from Emerging Market to Standalone Market status, citing opaque shareholding structures and suspected coordinated trading.

— Why it matters A Standalone label would take Indonesia out of MSCI’s emerging-market family, so funds that track that family could be forced to sell Indonesian shares regardless of company fundamentals.

— The numbers Indonesia’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell to 0.43% on 30 September 2026 from 1.16% at the end of 2025, as the free-float-adjusted value of the MSCI Indonesia Index fell about 55% (US$119.1 billion to US$53.4 billion).

— The timeline Feedback is open until 30 April 2027, and MSCI will announce its decision on or before 30 June 2027; the freeze on Indonesian index changes that began in January 2026 stays in place.

— Who is who MSCI is the global index provider; OJK is Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority; IDX is the Indonesia Stock Exchange; KSEI is the central securities depository.

— What to watch Whether OJK, IDX and KSEI can show enforced disclosure of real owners and a higher minimum free float before the consultation closes on 30 April 2027.

— What it means for you US investors in broad MSCI Emerging Markets ETFs or mutual funds could see Indonesian exposure cut automatically if the reclassification goes ahead.

MSCI said on 15 October 2026 that it wants to reclassify Indonesia from Emerging Market status and proposed moving it to Standalone Market status. For US investors, this means benchmark-tracking funds could be forced to sell Indonesian stocks, creating mechanical selling pressure that has nothing to do with company earnings.

Indonesia is Southeast Asia’s largest economy and a regular fixture in global emerging-market portfolios. This analysis explains what MSCI proposed, how index changes move money, and what US investors should watch before the final decision due by 30 June 2027, building on our Asia Intelligence Brief of 16 October.

What MSCI Proposed on 15 October

MSCI launched a consultation on a proposal to reclassify the MSCI Indonesia Indexes from Emerging Market to Standalone Market status. It welcomes feedback from market participants until 30 April 2027 and will announce its decision on or before 30 June 2027.

MSCI said market participants had raised significant concerns about the investability of Indonesian equities. It named two problems: persistent opacity in shareholding structures and suspected coordinated trading behaviour.

MSCI also said it could proceed with the reclassification unless the consultation shows clear evidence of material improvements in market governance and functioning. In other words, the burden of proof now sits with Indonesian regulators and the exchange.

The existing freeze on Indonesian securities in MSCI indexes remains in place until further notice. Under it, MSCI does not raise Foreign Inclusion Factors or share counts, add stocks to the MSCI Indonesia Investable Market Index, or move companies up between size segments.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Indonesia Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How We Got Here: From the January Freeze to October

The freeze began in late January 2026, after global investors questioned how reliably Indonesia classifies its shareholders. On 28 January the Jakarta Composite Index closed down 7.35% and the exchange briefly halted trading, according to Indonesian market coverage.

IDX said at the time that MSCI’s feedback was important for strengthening the credibility of Indonesia’s capital market. It had begun publishing free-float data for listed companies on 2 January 2026, with monthly updates planned.

In its June 2026 market classification review, MSCI said that if sufficient progress was not evident by the November 2026 Index Review, it would consider launching a consultation on reclassifying Indonesia. In October it concluded, citing market participants, that progress had not been consistent across the market.

Indonesian authorities had announced reforms, including finer disclosure of shareholders, more detailed investor categories and a roadmap to raise the minimum free float to 15%. MSCI said, however, that it had seen little meaningful evidence of enforcement.

File photo: the Jakarta business district at night.

What MSCI Does and Why It Matters

MSCI Inc. is a global index provider whose equity benchmarks determine how institutional investors measure country and company performance. Many mutual funds, exchange-traded funds and pension mandates are designed to track or benchmark against MSCI indexes.

When MSCI changes a country’s classification, it alters the group of funds that may or must hold that market. A downgrade can therefore trigger selling even when the underlying companies are profitable.

Here the dispute is not about economic development or company size. It is about market accessibility, meaning whether international investors can tell who owns shares and how much stock is truly available to trade.

MSCI weights companies by free-float-adjusted market capitalisation, so a stock’s index weight depends on the shares realistically open to international investors. Shares held by controlling shareholders, governments or insiders may be excluded or discounted, and if the ownership data cannot be trusted, weights cannot be calculated accurately.

The Numbers That Define the Shock

MSCI reported that Indonesia’s weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell to 0.43% as of 30 September 2026, down from 1.16% at the end of 2025. The free-float-adjusted market capitalisation of the MSCI Indonesia Index dropped from US$119.1 billion on 31 December 2025 to US$53.4 billion on 30 September 2026, a fall of about 55%.

The index also shrank from 18 to 9 constituents over the same period, per MSCI’s consultation figures. Together these figures show a market that has shrunk sharply inside MSCI’s indexes.

Bank Indonesia reported official reserve assets of about US$146.3 billion at the end of September 2026, enough for 5.3 months of imports. Consumer-price inflation was 3.28% year-on-year in September (3.19% in August), according to Statistics Indonesia, inside Bank Indonesia’s 2026 target range of 2.5% plus or minus 1 percentage point.

The Actors and What Each Wants

MSCI controls access to benchmarks used by a large share of the world’s institutional capital. It wants reliable ownership data and credible price formation before it keeps Indonesia in the Emerging Market family.

Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, or OJK, is Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority, and PT Bursa Efek Indonesia, or IDX, runs the Indonesia Stock Exchange. Both are under pressure to show enforcement, not only new rules.

PT Kustodian Sentral Efek Indonesia, or KSEI, is the central securities depository. It holds the shareholding records that MSCI needs to verify free-float calculations.

Bank Indonesia manages the rupiah and monitors cross-border portfolio flows. It is not part of the classification dispute, but it would handle the currency effects of any large foreign selling.

Emerging, Frontier and Standalone Explained

These categories are MSCI investment classifications, not legal rankings and not judgments on a country’s economic quality. They shape how global funds are organised and where capital is allowed to flow.

An Emerging Market is a relatively broad, institutionally investable market included in major global emerging-market benchmarks. A Frontier Market is smaller or less accessible, with a narrower base of institutional investors.

A Standalone Market is not part of MSCI’s developed, emerging or frontier country-index groups. That can be a harsher benchmark outcome because many country-allocation strategies are built around those main families.

The proposal MSCI published on 15 October is specifically for Standalone Market status, not Frontier. That distinction matters because a Frontier move would keep Indonesia inside a smaller MSCI group.

How Index Changes Move Money

Index-tracking funds seek to match a benchmark’s holdings and weights. When MSCI changes a country’s status, passive funds and benchmark-sensitive active managers may need to trade near the effective date.

Arbitrageurs may trade in advance, anticipating the required flows. A country-level downgrade can therefore create selling pressure even if companies’ operating results have not changed.

The size of the flow depends on how much money is benchmarked to the index, how much of it is passive, and whether the change is phased. The effect is not always one-way, since investors who are not tied to a benchmark may buy cheaper assets.

The US Investor Angle

US investors can be exposed through mutual funds, ETFs and institutional mandates that track or use MSCI benchmarks. Exposure can be direct through Indonesia-focused products or indirect through broader emerging-market funds.

An Indonesia-focused fund may be free to keep holding Indonesian shares. A broad MSCI Emerging Markets tracker may have to reduce Indonesia if its benchmark weight falls.

An active emerging-market manager may not be forced to sell, but a lower benchmark weight makes an overweight position riskier against the index. The final cash flow cannot be estimated until MSCI sets the final index treatment, the affected securities and their revised weights.

Foreign Ownership and the Rupiah

Selling Indonesian equities can be accompanied by converting rupiah proceeds into foreign currency, which puts depreciation pressure on the rupiah. That link is not automatic, because the rupiah also responds to US interest rates, the dollar, Indonesia’s trade position, commodity prices and central-bank intervention.

Bank Indonesia’s foreign-exchange operations include currency purchases and sales, repos, term deposits and Bank Indonesia securities. These tools can calm disorderly markets, but they cannot rule out weaker rupiah if outflows are sustained.

For a US investor, the return that counts is the local share-price return combined with the currency move. A falling rupiah can turn a positive local return into a weak or negative dollar return.

For expats, a weaker rupiah raises the purchasing power of incoming foreign income. It also cuts the dollar value of rupiah savings and local investments.

What Past Classification Changes Show

MSCI classification changes can alter the funds permitted to invest, a country’s weight in global benchmarks, liquidity and the visibility of local stocks among international allocators. Indonesia’s case should still not be read as a repeat of earlier Emerging-to-Frontier moves, because the stated trigger is ownership transparency and trading integrity.

MSCI has not said Indonesia lacks investable companies. It has said international investors cannot reliably see ownership, effective free float and price formation across the market.

That makes credibility the central issue. Unless reforms show consistent enforcement, the reclassification risk stays active through the decision due by 30 June 2027.

What It Means for You

If you hold a broad MSCI Emerging Markets ETF or mutual fund, your exposure to Indonesia could shrink automatically if the reclassification proceeds. You would not need to act, but you should know the manager would adjust holdings to the new benchmark.

If you hold an Indonesia-focused fund, the manager may keep more freedom to hold Indonesian shares. Much depends on the fund’s mandate and whether it follows MSCI or another index provider.

The practical step is to check which benchmark your emerging-market fund tracks. If it tracks MSCI, the decision due by 30 June 2027 will matter to your portfolio.

What Is Not Known

The final decision is not known. MSCI said it could reconsider if the consultation shows clear evidence of material improvements in governance.

The implementation date, the affected indexes and any phasing of changes are not known. MSCI has not published the size of any expected selling, and brokerage estimates vary widely.

The rupiah impact is not known either. It depends on many factors beyond equity flows, including US rates and Bank Indonesia’s operations.

What to Watch

The next date to mark is 30 April 2027, when MSCI’s consultation feedback window closes. The decision follows on or before 30 June 2027.

Until then, the freeze on Indonesian index changes continues. Watch whether OJK, IDX and KSEI publish enforcement actions, ownership data and free-float figures that MSCI can verify.

Market indicators to follow include foreign buying or selling in IDX equities, free-float estimates for individual stocks, trading spreads and the rupiah.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between MSCI Emerging Market and Standalone Market status?

An Emerging Market is included in major global emerging-market benchmarks and attracts large allocations from international funds. A Standalone Market sits outside MSCI’s developed, emerging and frontier country-index groups, which can shrink the number of benchmark-linked investors.

Why is MSCI considering reclassifying Indonesia?

MSCI cites persistent opacity in shareholding structures and suspected coordinated trading behaviour. Those concerns affect both the free-float calculation and confidence in the prices used to build indexes.

When will MSCI make its final decision on Indonesia?

MSCI will announce its decision on or before 30 June 2027. Feedback on the proposal is open until 30 April 2027.

What has MSCI already done about Indonesia?

Since January 2026 MSCI has frozen increases to Foreign Inclusion Factors and share counts, additions to its investable-market index and upward moves between size segments for Indonesian securities. It says the freeze stays in place until further notice.

How big is Indonesia in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index now?

Indonesia’s weight fell to 0.43% on 30 September 2026 from 1.16% at the end of 2025. The MSCI Indonesia Index’s market value dropped from US$119.1 billion to US$53.4 billion over the same period.

How could a reclassification affect the rupiah?

Selling Indonesian equities can be accompanied by converting rupiah proceeds into foreign currency, which puts depreciation pressure on the rupiah. However, the rupiah also responds to US interest rates, trade balances, commodity prices and Bank Indonesia’s operations.

What should US investors do about the MSCI review?

US investors should check which benchmark their emerging-market fund tracks. If it tracks MSCI, the decision due by 30 June 2027 will matter directly to their portfolio.

World.content:
BRASÍLIA · Culture

Zé Neto and Cristiano play Mané Garrincha stadium on Saturday 17 October, Buraco do Jazz closes its tenth season from 22 to 24 October, and TEDxBrasília ends the month on the 31st. The rest of October, day by day.

Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

BRASÍLIA — This guide is for people who live in the capital, not weekend tourists. It covers things to do in Brasília in October 2026 from Saturday 17 October to Halloween, with venues, prices where published and practical notes for expats and long-stay visitors.

The second half of the month is strong. A sertanejo (Brazilian country-pop) duo plays its first stadium show on 17 October, a free jazz series says goodbye on the 22nd to 24th, and a music festival and a talks evening close October.

Politics shares the calendar. Brazil votes in the second round on Sunday 25 October, and the race for governor of the Federal District is one of the governor run-offs, with polling stations open from 08:00 to 17:00.

Prices below are in reais with the US dollar value in brackets, converted at about R$5.07 per US$1 (16 October 2026). Where a price has not been published, we say so instead of guessing.

The Eixo Monumental, the avenue that links many of the venues in this guide. File photo. Photo: Senado Federal, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October: A Stadium Night and Free Theatre

Saturday 17 October, gates 17:00, show 21:00 Zé Neto and Cristiano Arena BRB Mané Garrincha, Setor Recreativo Norte, Asa Norte · From R$80 (about US$16) The duo celebrates 15 years in music with what is billed as the biggest show of its career and its first in a stadium. First-lot prices were R$80 to R$160 (about US$16 to US$32) for lower seats, R$160 to R$320 (about US$32 to US$63) for the pitch and R$590 to R$1,180 (about US$116 to US$233) for the On Stage open-bar area.

Tickets were sold on the Baladapp website and at a box office in Sudoeste, at up to six per CPF (the Brazilian taxpayer number) and two half-price tickets. The show is rated 16+, and children aged 5 to 15 must come with a parent or guardian.

The figures above are first-lot prices, so check Baladapp for current availability. Solidarity tickets, the middle price in each sector, require a donation of 1 kg of non-perishable food.

Through Sunday 18 October Festival de Teatro do Distrito Federal Teatro Sesc Paulo Autran, Taguatinga · Free The second edition of the festival has eight competing local productions, plus workshops, conversation circles and tributes to people in the performing arts. Sessions offer Libras (Brazilian sign language) interpretation and audio description, and the festival closes on Sunday 18 October.

Vale Jurássico Dinosaur Park

Limited-time season, opened 8 October Vale Jurássico Parque da Cidade · Tickets on Ingresse The dinosaur attraction opened on 8 October with animatronic dinosaurs, a catamaran ride that simulates an expedition and a guided Jurassic Laboratory. Visitors then explore the Jurassic Forest freely, with a kids’ space, photo sets and a themed dining area along the route.

Entry is in sessions every 30 minutes, tickets are sold for specific dates and times, and sale dates are released gradually. The end date of the season has not been published, so check Ingresse for current opening hours before you go.

Thursday 22 to Saturday 24 October: Buraco do Jazz Finale

Thursday 22 to Saturday 24 October Buraco do Jazz, Grand Finale of the Tenth Season Centro Cultural Três Poderes, Praça dos Três Poderes · Free Brasília’s open-air jazz series, which has passed 350 editions, ends its tenth season with three nights. Bivalves open on Thursday 22 at 20:00, Maíra Guedes plays on Friday 23 at 20:00, and Saturday 24 brings a surprise band at 17:00 followed by Encontro Racional at 20:00.

Entry is free, with voluntary contributions accepted, and doors open at 18:00, two hours before the main shows. Arrive early if you want a good spot, since a free event in the capital can fill up.

Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October: Festival and Talks to Close the Month

Friday 30 October Festival Estilo Brasil 2026, Opening Night Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães · Tickets on sale at festivalestilobrasil.com.br The third edition opens with Criolo, Amaro Freitas and Dino D’Santiago, with a special appearance by Iza. The festival then runs to 25 November, with Marina Sena on 19 November and Seal on 25 November.

The start time and the opening-night prices were not published in the sources we checked. Confirm both on the festival website before you buy.

Saturday 31 October, 18:00 TEDxBrasília Teatro Nacional Cláudio Santoro, Via N2, Setor Cultural Norte · Price and sales channel not yet announced This year’s theme is “A Construção do Futuro” (Building the Future), with short talks, cultural interventions and the exhibition “2D, do Daltonismo à Dislexia” by Wós Rodrigues and Murilo Frade. Speakers, ticket price and sales channel had not been published when local media reported on the event on 29 September.

TEDx events are independently organised under licence from TED, and this one is curated by journalist Rafael Souza. Check the organisers’ channels for tickets before planning around it.

Planning your Brasília in October

Sunday 25 October is the second round of voting. In the Federal District the governor’s race goes to a run-off, so expect heavy political news.

Check venue pages for any schedule changes that day, and see our report on moved polling places if you are registered to vote locally.

Brasília is a car city, and the venues above sit far apart. Use ride-hailing apps for late shows at the Centro Cultural Três Poderes or the Centro de Convenções, and allow extra time before and after big events.

For more October ideas in another Brazilian capital, see our Belo Horizonte guide.

Ticket sellers for the Zé Neto and Cristiano show capped sales at six per CPF. Visitors without a CPF should ask the box office or the organiser how to buy for big concerts.

For last-minute changes, check Agenda BSB, the cultural roundups of Correio Braziliense and Metrópoles, and Agência Brasília. Organisers’ own pages and ticket platforms remain the final word on times and prices.

What it means for you

For a visitor from the United States, October is cheap by comparison with major US stadium shows. Stadium seats for Zé Neto and Cristiano started at about US$16 at half price in the first lot, and the jazz finale costs nothing.

The free events, Buraco do Jazz and the theatre festival, are the easiest way to meet the city’s residents. The paid ones, especially the Estilo Brasil opening, are best bought through the official channels listed above.

More: Brazil news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Buraco do Jazz finale free?

Yes. Entry to the 22 to 24 October finale at Centro Cultural Três Poderes is free, with voluntary contributions accepted.

How much are tickets for Zé Neto and Cristiano in Brasília?

First-lot tickets for the 17 October show at Arena BRB Mané Garrincha ranged from R$80 (about US$16) for lower-seat half price to R$1,180 (about US$233) for the full-price On Stage open-bar area. They were sold through Baladapp and a box office in Sudoeste.

What is on in Brasília on the last weekend of October 2026?

Festival Estilo Brasil opens on Friday 30 October at Ulysses Centro de Convenções with Criolo, Amaro Freitas and Dino D’Santiago. TEDxBrasília follows on Saturday 31 October at 18:00 at Teatro Nacional Cláudio Santoro.

When is the second round of voting in Brasília?

On Sunday 25 October, with polling stations open from 08:00 to 17:00. The Federal District also votes in a governor run-off.

Are there tickets for TEDxBrasília on 31 October?

Local media reported on 29 September that the price and sales channel had not been announced. The event is on Saturday 31 October at 18:00 at Teatro Nacional Cláudio Santoro, so check the organisers’ channels.

World.title: Russia Puts Tarkett, Ontex Under State Management
World.content:
RUSSIA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat this means, and what's next › RT Ask Rio Times This story and the bigger picture. × Economy impact Key players Stability What's next Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → — What is happening President Vladimir Putin signed Decree No. 738 in mid-October 2026, placing the Russian units of five European-linked companies, including flooring maker Tarkett and hygiene maker Ontex, under temporary management.

— Why it matters The mechanism lets Moscow take operational control of foreign-owned subsidiaries without formally transferring legal title, leaving investors with uncertain recovery prospects.

— The legal basis Presidential Decree No. 302 of 25 April 2023 allows temporary management of property, shares and property rights linked to countries Russia calls unfriendly. Each new case is added by amending its list.

— Who is who Putin signs each decree and alone ends the management. The Federal Agency for State Property Management (Rosimushchestvo) is the default manager, but the president can name another, as he did with the company Centre Capital (Tsentr Kapital) in this case.

— What to watch Parent-company impairment statements, further amendments to the Decree No. 302 list, and any European decision on frozen Russian central-bank assets.

— What it means for you US and European investors with exposure to Russian subsidiaries should review impairment charges, control rights and political-risk coverage, because restoration depends on a presidential decision rather than an automatic legal process.

Russia keeps adding foreign-owned companies to a 2023 legal instrument that hands their control to the state or to managers it names. For US investors and executives, the mechanism matters because it lets Moscow take operational control without formally taking legal title, leaving recovery uncertain.

In mid-October 2026 Putin placed the Russian units of Tarkett, Ontex and three packaging groups under temporary management. This analysis explains the legal mechanics, what the earlier cases show about getting assets back, and what owners can realistically do, drawing on the Europe Intelligence Brief and Russian primary sources.

How Temporary Management Works

The legal basis is Presidential Decree No. 302, signed on 25 April 2023 and titled “On Temporary Management of Certain Property.” It covers movable and immovable property in Russia, shares in Russian companies, securities and property rights.

Moscow justifies the decree as a response to “unfriendly actions” by foreign states that deprive Russia or Russian owners of property abroad. It also cites national, economic and energy security interests.

The default manager is the Federal Agency for State Property Management, known as Rosimushchestvo, headed by Vadim Yakovenko. The president can name another manager, and in several recent cases he has chosen private Russian companies instead.

The manager exercises the owner’s powers, including inventory and preservation of the assets, but has no power to dispose of them. That means the foreign shareholder can remain the owner on paper while losing control over governance, cash flows and appointments.

Temporary management ends by decision of the President of Russia. The decree sets no fixed timetable and no court-based expiry date.

The tool is used through amendments. Each new case is a short decree that amends the property list attached to Decree No. 302, and the amendment takes effect on the day it is published.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Nestlé Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Original Targets and the 2023 Cases

The first list in 2023 named the Russian holdings of Germany’s Uniper (in the power producer Unipro) and of Finland’s Fortum. Moscow framed those cases as a reply to Germany and Finland taking steps against Russian-linked assets.

On 16 July 2023 Putin signed Decree No. 520, extending the list to Danone Russia and to Baltika Breweries, in which Carlsberg’s Swedish unit held 98.56% of the equity. Carlsberg had already agreed to sell its Russian business, and the decree made that sale uncertain.

These two cases also show that the measure can be reversed. A later decree removed Danone from the list in March 2024, and Carlsberg’s Baltika was also taken off before Carlsberg agreed to sell its shares to Baltika employees.

Reversal is possible, but it has come only after a presidential decision. It has also come in the context of a sale or exit negotiated with Russian authorities.

What Changed in 2026

The measure has kept growing this year. Decree No. 604 of 24 August 2026 created a second, separate ground for temporary management: owners of critical infrastructure who fail to secure it, including against drone attacks.

Under that decree the government decides on the president’s instruction, and Rosimushchestvo manages the assets while property rights do not formally end. It is broader than Decree No. 302 because it applies to Russian and foreign owners alike.

The same day Putin signed Decree No. 602, which went the other way. It removed the stakes in the Ken-Pak and Ken-Pak Zavod Upakovki companies, held by Poland’s Canpack and France’s Tapon France, from the temporary-management list.

On 31 August 2026 Decree No. 619 transferred 100% of the cable maker Dielectric Cable Systems, formerly held by Italy’s Adventus International, to a company called Development of Construction Assets. A decree of 17 September 2026 (No. 661) amended the list again, and reports named Auchan, Nestlé, Lemana PRO and FM Logistic among those affected.

On 28 September 2026 Decree No. 689 added the Russian units of Germany’s Metro group and named JSC UK Torg Rus as manager. Meduza, citing The Bell, reported that the company was registered on 8 September, about three weeks before the decree.

The Latest Decree: Tarkett, Ontex and Three Packaging Groups

Decree No. 738 of mid-October 2026 amended the list again. It places the Russian units of five companies under the management company Centre Capital (Tsentr Kapital).

The five are Tarkett, Kappa Rus, Menshen Packaging CIS, Ontex Ru and Eviosys Packaging Kuban.

Interfax described Kappa Rus as a paper-packaging maker formerly owned by Ireland’s Smurfit Kappa, and Ontex Ru as a hygiene-products maker of the Belgian Ontex group. It linked Eviosys Packaging Kuban to the Dutch unit of Sonoco and Menshen Packaging CIS to Germany’s Menshen.

In Tarkett’s case the decree covers shares of the Russian company Tarkett held by a Serbian Tarkett subsidiary, plus 100% of the company Tarkett Sommer. Tarkett makes flooring and, according to Meduza, has two plants in Russia, in the Moscow and Samara regions.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the transfer a continuation of a trend and said all five companies come from unfriendly countries. He pointed to what he called the illegal detention of Russian money and the unlawful expropriation of Russian companies’ property in those countries.

Can Owners Get Assets Back?

Legally yes, but not automatically. Under Decree No. 302 the management ends by presidential decision, so the route back is political rather than judicial.

Past cases suggest several paths: a decree removing the assets from the list, a negotiated sale or exit, or a wider political settlement. Litigation in Russian courts or arbitration abroad is possible, but a foreign judgment is hard to enforce inside Russia.

The practical obstacles are large. Owners lose control of local management and records, cash extraction can be blocked, and sanctions may prevent payment even where a sale is permitted.

The assets can also lose value while under state-directed management. Investors should not treat the measure as an ordinary temporary receivership.

What It Means for the United States and Latin America

For US readers the issue is exposure. American and European groups with Russian subsidiaries face the same mechanism, and 2026 shows Moscow adding cases at a steady pace, including a US-linked packaging case reported in September.

The link to frozen Russian central-bank assets creates a second channel of risk. Moscow says its measures answer Western holds on Russian property, so any European step from immobilising those assets toward using the principal could prompt further retaliation.

For Latin America the relevance is indirect. The decree offers a template of state control without formal expropriation, which investors in strategic sectors will watch.

Brazilian and Mexican companies with European or US parents should check whether any Russian subsidiary could be affected. The same applies to supply links that run through Russia.

Investor Options

The first step is to separate three exposures: book value, control and recovery. Each needs its own analysis and its own mitigation.

Investors should read the exact decree and the Russian legal entities it lists. They should also track Russian corporate-register changes and parent-company impairment charges.

Before any sale or settlement they should map sanctions, export-control and payment restrictions. They should also preserve treaty and contract claims and check whether political-risk insurance or arbitration rights apply.

Valuations should be stress-tested under three scenarios: restoration, a forced sale and indefinite state control. Each scenario implies a different impairment and a different disclosure.

The Scenarios

The stabilising scenario is a broader political settlement that links asset restoration to the treatment of Russian property abroad. Temporary management could then be reversed by new decrees, as happened with Danone and Baltika.

The escalation scenario is a European move from immobilising income on frozen reserves to using the principal. That could trigger further retaliation against Western companies still operating in Russia.

A third scenario is creeping de facto nationalisation. Management stays formally reversible, but a later sale to a Russian buyer makes recovery harder.

What It Means for You

If you hold shares in a Western company with Russian operations, check whether the parent still claims control of its Russian subsidiary. Also look at whether it has impaired the investment and how it describes recovery in its latest filings.

If you are an executive with exposure to Russia, review the exact decree that affects your entities. Keep treaty, contract and shareholder-rights claims intact before any sale or settlement.

The central point is that “temporary” does not mean low-risk or short-term. Ownership may survive on paper while the state controls operations, and restoration depends on a new presidential decision.

What Is Not Known

The financial impact on each parent company is not yet clear. Their disclosures will show whether they still claim control, have impaired the investment or regard recovery as uncertain.

It is also not known whether Moscow will add more sectors or companies. Nor is it clear how Centre Capital will run the five businesses.

What to Watch

Watch for further amendments to the Decree No. 302 list and for any decree that removes assets from it. Both appear on the official legal portal on the day of signing.

Watch for parent-company statements on impairment and control. Watch also for EU and US decisions on Russian reserves, since Moscow ties its measures to them.

For wider context, see our Europe and Russia coverage and our report on how a Russia sanctions waiver leaves Latin American buyers exposed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is temporary management under Russian law?

Temporary management is a presidential decision that hands control of assets in Russia to a state-named manager, while title does not formally pass. It rests on Presidential Decree No. 302 of 25 April 2023, which targets property linked to countries Moscow calls unfriendly.

Who runs the assets?

The default manager is Rosimushchestvo, the federal property agency. The president can name another manager, and in the October 2026 case he named the company Centre Capital.

Which companies were hit most recently?

Decree No. 738 of mid-October 2026 covers the Russian units of Tarkett, Kappa Rus, Menshen Packaging CIS, Ontex Ru and Eviosys Packaging Kuban. Earlier 2026 decrees affected Metro, Auchan, Nestlé, Lemana PRO and FM Logistic, according to reports.

Can owners get their assets back?

Legally yes, but not automatically. Temporary management ends by presidential decision, as with Danone and Carlsberg’s Baltika, which were later removed from the list.

How does it differ from expropriation?

The manager can run the assets but cannot dispose of them, so the foreign shareholder can remain the formal owner. In practice the owner loses control over governance, cash flows and appointments.

What should investors do?

Investors should separate book-value, control and recovery exposure and read the exact decree. They should also track impairment charges and check political-risk insurance and arbitration rights.

World.title: What to Do in La Paz in October 2026
World.content:
LA PAZ · Culture

Todos Somos Ángeles Rock Fest closes the month on Saturday 31 October, with a Uriah Heep special the night before. This guide covers ten confirmed events from 17 to 31 October, day by day.

Illimani, the snow-capped peak that frames La Paz. Archive photo. Photo: Senorhorst Jahnsen, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

LA PAZ — This is the guide to things to do in La Paz in October 2026 for the rest of the month, from Saturday 17 October. It lists ten events that the organiser, the city or a ticket seller has confirmed, with venue and time.

Prices are in bolivianos (BOB), with US$ values in brackets.

The month ends with the first Bolivian date of Todos Somos Ángeles Rock Fest, an open-air show led by the Mexican band Ángeles del Infierno. Before that, the city agenda offers a stage production, a Uriah Heep special evening, a music honours evening and several small cultural events in museums, libraries and a children’s space.

We checked each listing against the municipal cultural agenda (Jiwaki, run by the La Paz city government), the festival organiser and the ticket seller on 17 October 2026. Where a price or detail is not published, we say so instead of guessing.

We found no confirmed November event yet, so the guide stops at 31 October.

17 to 21 October: theatre, a museum evening and the city anniversary

Saturday 17 October, 19:00 Antiurbano Teatro Municipal Alberto Saavedra Pérez, Centro · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The city agenda lists this production for tonight at the main historic theatre in the centre. The listing gives no description of the programme and no ticket price, so ask at the box office before you go.

Tuesday 20 October, 18:30 Seres del Séptimo Sentido Museo Costumbrista Juan de Vargas, Centro · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The city agenda lists this evening at the costumbrist museum on 20 October, the day La Paz marks its founding in 1548. The agenda gives no programme details, so treat the time as the only firm fact.

The municipal agenda also lists a psychopedagogy talk on managing emotions in children and teenagers at the Villa Victoria zonal library on Wednesday 21 October at 15:00. The listing gives no price.

Both evening venues are in the central district, so you can reach them without crossing the city. La Paz lies above 3,500 metres, so newcomers should walk slowly on the hills and drink water before a long evening out.

24 to 25 October: weekend afternoons for families

Saturday 24 October, 15:00 Bat Pepper Club: Scrapbooking Murciélaguero Espacio Interactivo Memoria y Futuro Pipiripi · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The city agenda lists a scrapbooking workshop with a bat theme at the Pipiripi interactive space. The listing gives no age range or price.

Sunday 25 October, 15:00 Ch’iti Warmi “Cholitas Skaters” Espacio Interactivo Memoria y Futuro Pipiripi · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The agenda lists the session under the name Cholitas Skaters. It does not describe the format, so confirm details with the venue.

27 to 30 October: municipal honours and a Uriah Heep evening

Tuesday 27 October, 19:30 Recognition of living Bolivian authors and composers Teatro Municipal Alberto Saavedra Pérez, Centro · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The city honours songwriters and composers who are still alive. It is a useful evening if you want to hear how Bolivian musicians describe their own tradition.

Thursday 29 October, 19:00 10th Meeting of Adults and Older Adults: Art and Dance with Our Elders Teatro Municipal Alberto Saavedra Pérez, Centro · Price not listed · Municipal agenda This is a community event with art and dance by older residents. It is a quieter look at city life than the larger rock shows of the month.

The agenda also lists a children’s storytelling session, Aptapi of La Paz Tales for Children, at the Villa Victoria zonal library on Thursday 29 October at 15:00.

Friday 30 October, 19:30 Mírate a ti mismo: a Uriah Heep special Cine Teatro Municipal 6 de Agosto, Centro · Price not listed · Municipal agenda The programme is a special dedicated to the British rock band Uriah Heep. The agenda does not say who performs, so we cannot confirm whether it is a tribute band or a screening. It suits classic-rock fans who prefer a seated theatre to an open-air crowd.

The municipal agenda does not publish ticket prices for these events. Ask at the theatre box office or check the agenda before you go.

31 October: the rock festival

Saturday 31 October, 20:00 Todos Somos Ángeles Rock Fest 2026 Teatro al Aire Libre, Av. del Poeta · Tickets BOB 230 to 666 (about US to US) per the festival page The line-up is Ángeles del Infierno, José Andrëa (the vocalist known from Mago de Oz), Basca, Jocker, Sarcasmo, Hate, Ikael and Templario. The organiser, Abrakdabra Producciones, calls it the first time the festival has come to Bolivia.

The festival’s own page gives a start of 20:00 and an end of 23:30. The BuenPlan ticket page shows 14:00 for the same day, and the two do not agree, so check the time printed on your ticket.

The festival page also shows a ticket range of BOB 230 to 666 (about US$20 to US$57), which differs from the four BuenPlan zones above. Buy only through the official platform and compare the zone before you pay.

Planning your La Paz in October

Bolivia moved to a flexible exchange-rate regime this year, and the central bank now updates the official dollar rate daily. The rate was BOB 11.73 per US$ for 10 to 12 October (Banco Central de Bolivia, as reported by Correo del Sur), and we use it for every US$ figure here.

It can move by the day you buy, so treat the dollar values as approximate.

BuenPlan sells the rock festival. The other events had no ticket platform in the agenda we checked, so entry rules and prices are unconfirmed.

For the latest changes, check the municipal cultural agenda at lapaz.bo, because programmes can shift at short notice. For background on the country that surrounds these evenings, read our explainer on Bolivia’s role in Latin America, our report on the Chile Bolivia accords and the Bolivia news hub.

What it means for you: if you are visiting from the United States, the open-air festival is the only large ticketed show on this list, and its time and price are the two details to confirm first. The municipal events are small and local, so they suit a short evening in the centre, but check each price first. At this altitude, nights are cold in spring, so bring a warm layer and plan your way home before the show starts.

What is not known: the agenda does not publish prices for most events, and no November programme with confirmed dates had appeared by 17 October. Programmes can also change at short notice.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest events in La Paz in late October 2026?

Todos Somos Ángeles Rock Fest on Saturday 31 October at the Teatro al Aire Libre is the largest listed event. The municipal agenda also lists a Uriah Heep special evening on Friday 30 October.

How much are tickets for the La Paz rock festival?

The festival page lists tickets from BOB 230 to 666 (about US to US, at BOB 11.73 per US$). Prices can change by sales phase, so confirm at checkout.

What time does the Todos Somos Ángeles Rock Fest start?

The festival page gives 20:00 to 23:30 on Saturday 31 October. The BuenPlan ticket page shows 14:00, so check the time printed on your ticket.

Which bands play the 31 October rock festival in La Paz?

The line-up is Ángeles del Infierno, José Andrëa, Basca, Jocker, Sarcasmo, Hate, Ikael and Templario. The organiser is Abrakdabra Producciones.

Are there events in La Paz in November 2026?

We found no November listing with a confirmed date, time and venue at the organiser or ticket seller by 17 October 2026. The municipal agenda ends on 31 October for now, and we will add November events once they are published.

World.title: Sahel Jihadist Rivalry Becomes a Regional War in 2026
World.content:
MALI · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province have fought across the borderlands of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, and recent reporting says the conflict has spread into western Niger and northwestern Nigeria.

— Why it matters The rivalry is destabilising a region where Mali is a major gold producer and Niger mines uranium, and it sits on smuggling routes toward coastal West African states.

— The numbers The groups fought more than 320 battles from 2019 through September 2026, causing approximately 2,200 deaths, according to ACLED data.

— Who is who JNIM is al-Qaeda’s Sahel coalition; Islamic State Sahel Province is more rigidly ideological.

— What to watch Whether clashes spread from Niger’s Tillabéri region into Dosso and Maradi, which border Nigeria’s northwestern states.

— What it means for you US investors should monitor gold and uranium supply chains from Mali and Niger, where insecurity is already disrupting fuel and mining operations.

The rivalry between al-Qaeda’s JNIM and Islamic State Sahel Province has grown into a regional war that, according to Africanews, now reaches western Niger and northwestern Nigeria. For US readers, it threatens gold and uranium supply chains, counter-terrorism policy and the security of Gulf of Guinea states that host American investment.

The Sahel is the semi-arid belt south of the Sahara that stretches from Senegal to Sudan. This analysis explains who the two factions are, why they are fighting each other and where the violence could spread, drawing on Africanews, Le Temps and our own Africa Intelligence Brief.

How the Rivalry Escalated

Fighting between the two groups has intensified since September 2026 in the borderlands where Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger meet. On 1 September the factions clashed near N’Daki, close to the Mali–Burkina Faso border; sources differ on which side of the line it lay.

ISSP-linked channels claimed between 100 and more than 250 JNIM fighters killed, depending on the report. None of these tolls has been independently verified.

In October fighting broke out in Burkina Faso’s Oudalan province, near the Mali and Niger borders. On 12 October ISSP claimed it had killed more than 400 JNIM fighters, a claim not confirmed by independent sources.

ACLED analyst Heni Nsaibia said that, if confirmed, this would be the deadliest single battle recorded between the two groups. ACLED data he cited show more than 320 battles and about 2,200 deaths between 2019 and September 2026.

The escalation follows years of competition that began in 2019. In early April 2026 ISSP claimed 35 JNIM fighters killed in Niger’s Tillabéri region, reportedly the first documented clash between the two in Niger.

Africanews reports that the fighting has since spread into western Niger and northwestern Nigeria. This turns a contest once contained in the tri-border area into a wider regional security crisis.

JNIM remains the stronger group, with an estimated 7,000 to 8,000 fighters against about 2,000 for Islamic State, Africanews reports. That gap makes ISSP’s claims of mass kills hard to assess without independent confirmation.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Burkina Faso (Mali) Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Are JNIM and Islamic State Sahel?

JNIM: Al-Qaeda’s Sahel Coalition

JNIM is the Arabic acronym for Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims. It was formed in Mali in March 2017 from several al-Qaeda-aligned factions, including Ansar Dine, al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb’s Sahara emirate, al-Mourabitoun and the Macina Liberation Front.

JNIM operates as a coalition rather than a single centralised army. Its strength is local embedment: alliances with communities, recruitment among aggrieved populations, shadow courts, taxation and control of rural transport corridors.

That does not make JNIM moderate, because it has attacked civilians, imposed coercive rules and disrupted commerce. But compared with ISSP, it has generally shown greater flexibility toward local leaders and non-jihadist armed groups.

ISSP: Islamic State Sahel Province

ISSP is the Islamic State’s Sahel branch, formerly widely known as the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara. Its Malian stronghold around Ménaka has been central to its expansion.

Its main operating zone runs from northeastern Mali through western Niger into parts of Burkina Faso. Africanews reports that its reach now extends into Niger’s Tahoua, Dosso and Maradi regions.

ISSP follows a more rigid transnational doctrine and treats rival armed groups, community leaders and alleged collaborators as enemies. Africanews notes that it does not shy away from targeting civilians who refuse to accept its authority.

File photo: landscape in northern Burkina Faso, where fighting between JNIM and Islamic State Sahel has been reported.

Why They Are Fighting Each Other

The groups compete for the same rural populations, cattle corridors, smuggling routes, border crossings and taxation bases. Where governments have limited reach, control of a village or road can bring food, recruits, intelligence, revenue and influence over local chiefs and traders.

The tri-border zone is valuable because borders are porous while national security forces are stretched. Fighters can attack in one country and retreat into another.

JNIM’s al-Qaeda lineage accepts tactical alliances and gradual consolidation. ISSP regards such accommodation as ideological compromise, so each group treats the other as an illegitimate rival for leadership of jihad in West Africa.

The rivalry is not merely theological. Ideology shapes whom each faction recruits, taxes, negotiates with or punishes, so a local alliance that helps JNIM can become a target for ISSP.

Military coups and the exit of foreign forces have weakened the region’s security architecture. The insurgents are therefore contesting not only remote areas but also local state authority.

The Junta Governments and Russia’s Role

Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) and formed the Alliance of Sahel States, a confederation of the three juntas. Their governments present the move as sovereign self-reliance.

In operational terms, the shift has reduced intelligence-sharing and coordination with Western and regional partners while the insurgency remains unresolved. In July 2026 Mali’s government also publicly rejected reports of a US intervention against JNIM, Africanews reported.

Russia has become the juntas’ main security partner. In Mali, the Africa Corps, which reports to Russia’s Defence Ministry, replaced the Wagner Group and supports the army in combat.

Russia supplies military assistance, advisers and political backing, but it has not shown that it can replace Western intelligence, airlift, surveillance and training. The security record remains poor: South Africa’s BusinessDay quoted a security source saying 130 soldiers died in the 10 September attack on Dioura, and a diplomatic source saying about 120.

Where the Fighting Could Spread

Western Niger

Western Niger is the most immediate expansion zone. ISSP claimed 35 JNIM fighters killed in Tillabéri in early April 2026, reportedly the first clash between the two inside Niger.

Tillabéri surrounds Niger’s capital, Niamey, and links the Mali and Burkina Faso conflict zones to the more populated southwest. ISSP has also been active in Dosso, which borders Benin and northwestern Nigeria.

A sustained rivalry in western Niger could bring attacks on bases and border posts, road disruption around Niamey and displacement toward safer areas. It could also add pressure on Niger’s isolated junta and open routes into northern Nigeria.

Northwestern Nigeria

Northwestern Nigeria could serve as a rear area because of weak border coordination, insecurity and criminal economies. Africanews reports that ISSP’s reach now extends through Niger’s Tahoua, Dosso and Maradi regions toward Nigeria’s northwest.

The risk is not necessarily an immediate large-scale takeover. A more plausible path is the gradual establishment of cells, logistics networks, weapons channels and recruitment links.

Nigeria already faces Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province in the northeast. A second jihadist corridor in the northwest could stretch its security forces across multiple fronts.

Benin, Togo, Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire

The Gulf of Guinea states are the most important strategic frontier. ADF Magazine reports that JNIM has launched attacks into Benin from the W-Arly-Pendjari park complex, and Burkina Faso’s southern border creates routes toward Togo, Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.

Threats to coastal states could arrive through cross-border raids, attacks on rural security posts, intimidation of local officials, recruitment in marginalised border communities, smuggling and kidnapping. Transport and energy infrastructure could also be targeted.

Benin and Togo face the greatest immediate exposure because their northern regions abut Burkina Faso. Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire have stronger state capacity, but their northern corridors and border communities remain vulnerable.

Economic and Business Stakes

Mali is a major gold producer and Niger mines uranium, so insecurity in the central Sahel matters for commodity supply chains. The IMF said fuel supply disruptions after terrorist attacks in the fourth quarter of 2025 dampened Mali’s economic activity that year.

The IMF approved the second and final review of Mali’s Staff-Monitored Program on 18 March 2026. It expects recovery in 2026 if fuel supply is restored, security improves, domestic arrears are repaid and the mining dispute is resolved.

The IMF’s Rapid Credit Facility disbursement of about US$129 million, equal to 50 percent of Mali’s quota, was approved on 16 April 2025. The staff report on the review was published on 6 July 2026.

In September 2026 JNIM said it had struck air defence systems at the airport in Sévaré, in Mali’s Mopti region, which houses military aircraft and drones. Such attacks threaten the transport and logistics that businesses depend on.

What It Means for the United States

The US Department of State rates Mali Level 4: Do Not Travel, citing crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest and health risks. Its advisory is dated 9 January 2026.

Mali suspended visa issuance to US citizens at the end of December 2025, with limited exceptions, in response to Washington’s travel ban on Malian nationals. The State Department notes that extortion and kidnapping for ransom are significant sources of financing for terrorist and criminal groups.

For US counter-terrorism policy, the rivalry presents a dilemma. The factions may weaken each other in some areas, but their competition also drives expansion into new territory and more violence against civilians.

US strike options are constrained because the juntas have rejected Western military cooperation. Without basing rights, intelligence-sharing or overflight permissions, American counter-terrorism operations in the central Sahel are severely limited.

For US investors, the key exposure is through commodity markets. Disruption to Malian gold production or Nigerien uranium exports could affect global prices and supply chains, and companies with suppliers in West Africa should monitor security in the Gulf of Guinea states.

What It Means for Latin America

Latin American gold miners compete in the same global market as Sahel producers, so Sahel disruption matters to them mainly through price. A supply shock in Mali could lift gold prices, which would affect miners in Brazil, Peru and Mexico.

Brazilian and Mexican mining firms with African operations or partnerships should assess their exposure to West African security risks. Insecurity also disrupts regional trade routes that connect to Atlantic ports.

For Latin American governments, the Sahel shows how quickly local insurgencies can become transnational when borders are porous and coordination is poor. Weak state presence in border areas invites armed groups to fill the gap.

Scenarios: What Could Stabilise or Tip the Crisis

A stabilising scenario would involve the juntas reaching pragmatic security arrangements with local communities, restoring basic services and reopening channels for regional intelligence-sharing. Even limited cooperation with Gulf of Guinea states on border monitoring could slow the southward expansion.

A tipping scenario would see ISSP consolidate control around Ménaka and push further into Niger’s Dosso and Maradi regions, opening a corridor toward northwestern Nigeria. That would stretch Nigerian security forces and create a new front in Africa’s most populous country.

Another risk is that heavy-handed counterinsurgency by the army and its Russian partners increases civilian grievances and recruitment. That could also draw Moscow deeper into the conflict or prompt a reassessment of its commitment.

The most likely near-term outcome is continued fragmentation: several insurgent theatres connected by mobile fighters, criminal logistics and weak interstate coordination. That does not mean state collapse, but it does mean persistent insecurity that erodes governance and economic activity.

What It Means for You

If you hold investments in gold, uranium or West African markets, the Sahel rivalry is a supply-chain risk that deserves monitoring. The conflict is no longer confined to remote desert areas and is moving toward populated regions and international borders.

US citizens should heed the Level 4 travel advisory and avoid all travel to Mali. Businesses with personnel in the Gulf of Guinea states should review security protocols for northern regions of Benin, Togo, Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.

The rivalry also matters for US foreign policy. Washington’s limited leverage in the Sahel means that regional partners such as Nigeria and the Gulf of Guinea states will carry much of the burden of containing the spread.

What Is Not Known

The true casualty figures from the jihadist-on-jihadist fighting are not independently verified. ISSP’s claims of killing between 100 and more than 250 JNIM fighters in September and more than 400 in October are battlefield assertions, unconfirmed by independent sources.

Public reporting documents only limited clashes between the two groups inside Nigeria. Reports of spread into northwestern Nigeria therefore remain broad.

The exact territorial control of each faction is unclear. Public reporting provides snapshots of clashes but not a reliable map of which group controls which villages, roads or border crossings.

Internal leadership dynamics of both groups remain opaque. JNIM is associated with figures such as Iyad Ag Ghaly and Amadou Koufa, but current command structures are not fully documented in public sources.

The extent of Russian operational involvement is also uncertain. The number of personnel, their rules of engagement and their capacity for offensive operations are not publicly verified.

What to Watch

Watch whether clashes continue in Niger’s Tillabéri region and whether they spread into Dosso and Maradi, which border Nigeria. Any confirmed ISSP-JNIM fighting on Nigerian soil would mark a significant escalation.

Monitor whether jihadist operations are confirmed in Nigeria’s northwestern states. That would indicate the establishment of a new front.

Track whether the IMF’s recovery assumptions for Mali hold. Fuel supply, gold output and the mining dispute are the signals to follow after the programme review closed in March 2026.

Watch for updates to the US State Department travel advisory for Mali and neighbouring states. Any expansion of warnings to Gulf of Guinea states would indicate a worsening trajectory.

Finally, watch for renewed diplomatic engagement between the juntas and regional or Western partners. The spread of the rivalry toward Nigeria could create pressure for pragmatic coordination.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who are JNIM and Islamic State Sahel?

JNIM is al-Qaeda’s Sahel coalition, formed in Mali in 2017. Islamic State Sahel Province is the Islamic State’s branch, formerly known as the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara, with a more rigid transnational doctrine.

Why are JNIM and Islamic State Sahel fighting each other?

They are competing for the same rural populations, smuggling routes, border crossings and taxation bases. Their ideologies also reject each other: JNIM accepts tactical local alliances, while ISSP considers such accommodation evidence of ideological compromise.

Where could the Sahel jihadist rivalry spread next?

The most immediate expansion zone is western Niger, where ISSP attacked a JNIM position in Tillabéri in April 2026. From there, the conflict could spread into Dosso and Maradi, which border Nigeria’s northwestern states, and toward Benin, Togo, Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire.

How many people have died in the JNIM-ISSP rivalry?

ACLED data cited by analyst Heni Nsaibia show more than 320 battles and about 2,200 deaths between the two groups from 2019 to September 2026. These figures cover the fighting between the two groups, not the wider insurgency against states and civilians.

What is Russia’s role in the Sahel conflict?

Russia supplies military assistance, advisers and political backing to the juntas in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger. Its Africa Corps supports Malian government forces, but Russia has not shown that it can replace Western intelligence, airlift, surveillance and training.

How does the Sahel conflict affect gold and uranium supply?

Mali is a major gold producer and Niger mines uranium, so insecurity in the central Sahel matters for commodity supply chains. The IMF said fuel supply disruptions after terrorist attacks in the fourth quarter of 2025 dampened Mali’s economic activity, and it expects recovery in 2026 if fuel supply is restored.

Is it safe for US citizens to travel to Mali?

No, because the US Department of State classifies Mali as Level 4: Do Not Travel, citing crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest and health risks. Mali also suspended visa issuance to US citizens at the end of December 2025, with limited exceptions.

World.title: What to Do in Tunis in October 2026: JAOU and Concerts
World.content:
TUNIS · Culture

JAOU Tunis 26 opens on Friday 23 October, Yasmine Hamdan plays the Conference Palace on Sunday 25 October, and tickets run from 5 TND (about US$2) to 100 TND (about US$33) for the JAOU pass. The rest of the month, day by day.

The Tunis skyline across the Lake of Tunis. (File photo) Photo: Smailtn Camera location36° 48′ 10.53″ N, 10° 13′ 12.12″ E View this and other nearby image, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
