TUNIS — The second half of October is the busiest stretch of the Tunis cultural calendar. This guide lists what is on from Saturday 17 to Saturday 31 October, with venue, time and ticket price as shown by the ticketing platform tunis.events.

The anchor is JAOU Tunis 26, a contemporary art biennial that runs from 23 October to 22 November. Its concerts, dance and theatre fill the Conference Palace, B7L9 Art Centre and Le 4ème Art with tickets from as little as 5 TND (about US$2).

Prices below are converted at 1 TND = US$0.334 (RT, 17 October 2026, about 2.995 TND per US dollar). Every listing was checked on tunis.events on 17 October, and details can change, so confirm on the ticket page before you travel.

Key Facts Who: expats, travellers and locals in Tunis, Gammarth, La Marsa and Sidi Bou Said. What: JAOU Tunis 26 (23 October to 22 November) plus concerts, theatre and club nights. Why it matters: tickets run from 5 TND (about US$2) to 100 TND (about US$33) for the JAOU pass; the full JAOU pass is 100 TND (about US$33).

Saturday 17 to Thursday 22 October: Club Night, Workshop and Film

Saturday 17 October, 19:45 Special Moonraker with Atef & Franco Cinelli AÏNA, Gammarth · Ticket price not shown An electronic night at AÏNA with two DJs, listed to run until about 04:00 on Sunday. The ticket page does not show a price, so check it before you go.

Sunday 18 October, 14:00 Ceramic Workshop with Cera Concepts Studio FAN, Tunis · From 40 TND (about US$13) A hands-on pottery session with little reliance on language. tunis.events marks it as almost full, so book soon if you want a place.

Thursday 22 October, 19:00 Movie Night: Papillon d’or Sociale, Sidi Bou Said · From 20 TND (about US$7) A film evening at Sociale, a venue in the hilltop village of Sidi Bou Said. The listing does not give film or language details, so ask the venue first.

Friday 23 to Sunday 25 October: JAOU Opens

Friday 23 October to Sunday 22 November JAOU Tunis 26, Full Fest Access Venues across Tunis · From 100 TND (about US$33) The eighth JAOU Tunis is organised by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation with the Centre d’art contemporain Genève and the Fondation Art Explora. It hosts the Geneva Moving Image Biennial in Africa for the first time, with 16 artists commissioned for the edition.

Friday 23 October, 19:30 Gathering, Samar Haddad King / Yaa Samar! Dance Theatre Le 4ème Art, Tunis · 5 TND (about US$2) A dance-theatre evening at Le 4ème Art on Avenue de Paris. tunis.events lists JAOU as the ticket seller and marks the show as almost full.

Saturday 24 October, 20:30 C!S–T E M E R R O R: The H in my name is not silent Le 4ème Art, Tunis · 5 TND (about US$2) A performance piece by Nadim Bahsoun, listed with the same ticket seller as the other Le 4ème Art shows.

Sunday 25 October, 15:30 Glacier | Preset B7L9 Art Centre, Bhar Lazreg · 5 TND (about US$2) An afternoon performance by Enrico DauYang Wey at the free, non-profit art space run by the Kamel Lazaar Foundation.

Sunday 25 October, 18:00 Shabaab, Samar Haddad King / Yaa Samar! Dance Theatre Le 4ème Art, Tunis · 5 TND (about US$2) A second evening of the dance-theatre programme at Le 4ème Art, early enough to combine with a later concert.

Sunday 25 October, 19:30 Yasmine Hamdan & Soudeni Conference Palace, Tunis · From 30 TND (about US$10) The Lebanese-born singer, well known in Europe and the Arab world, plays the Palais des Congrès. It is the first of two headline concerts there this week.

Monday 26 to Thursday 29 October: Concerts and Performance

Monday 26 October, 19:00 Il Pleut, Il Plaint, Il Rage Le 4ème Art, Tunis · 5 TND (about US$2) A piece by Charles Brécard on the same low-price programme at Le 4ème Art.

Monday 26 October, 20:00 Shabaka / Obos: Vipa Conference Palace, Tunis · From 30 TND (about US$10) The second concert of the week at the Palais des Congrès, billed as Shabaka / Obos: Vipa. The ticket page gives no further detail on the line-up, so check the organiser’s announcement.

Tuesday 27 October, 19:00 Losing it, Samaa Wakim & Samar Haddad King Le 4ème Art, Tunis · 5 TND (about US$2) A dance performance at Le 4ème Art, one of several evenings there this month.

Wednesday 28 October, 20:00 Tuqus, Khalil Epi Cité de la Culture, Théâtre des Régions · 5 TND (about US$2) A midweek performance at the Cité de la Culture, the national cultural complex on Avenue Mohammed V.

Thursday 29 October, 19:30 Big Murk × Toumba × Julmud B7L9 Art Centre, Bhar Lazreg · From 20 TND (about US$7) A three-act music bill at B7L9, the Kamel Lazaar Foundation’s art space.

Friday 30 and Saturday 31 October: B7L9 Closes the Month

Friday 30 October, 19:30 Sacred Disorientation (Sara Dziri) / I, The Hybrid and the Antidote (Liliane Chlela) B7L9 Art Centre, Bhar Lazreg · From 20 TND (about US$7) A double bill of two artists’ performances at B7L9, billed together on one ticket page.

Saturday 31 October, 19:30 Nadah El Shazly B7L9 Art Centre, Bhar Lazreg · From 20 TND (about US$7) The Egyptian singer and composer is known for experimental Arab music. It is the last headline concert of the month in this guide.

Planning Your Tunis in October

Thursday 15 October was Evacuation Day, a public holiday, according to the Tunisian press and the official 2026 holiday calendar. The next one is Revolution Day on Thursday 17 December, so offices, banks and shops should keep normal hours from 17 to 31 October.

Tickets for almost every event above are sold through tunis.events, which lists prices in Tunisian dinars. Some low-price shows at Le 4ème Art are already marked almost full, so buy early.

Venues are spread across the metropolitan area: Le 4ème Art is on Avenue de Paris in the centre, B7L9 is in Bhar Lazreg, AÏNA is in Gammarth and Sociale is in Sidi Bou Said. Allow travel time if you plan two events in one day.

What It Means for You

For US visitors and remote workers in Tunis, JAOU is the clearest reason to plan an evening out this month. At about US$2 a ticket for many shows, it is one of the cheapest ways to meet the city’s artists and writers.

The programme also shows how the Kamel Lazaar Foundation, Geneva’s Centre d’art contemporain and Art Explora are bringing a European art biennial to North Africa. Readers following Tunisia’s cultural economy can watch whether the model repeats; read our Addis Ababa and Johannesburg guides for other African cities this month.

What Is Not Known

The Moonraker ticket page shows no price, and the Shabaka concert listing gives no line-up details. We have left out any event we could not confirm with the organiser or ticketing platform.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest event in Tunis in late October 2026?

JAOU Tunis 26, the contemporary art biennial, opens on Friday 23 October and runs to 22 November across venues in Tunis. A full-festival pass costs 100 TND (about US$33) on tunis.events.

Is there a public holiday in Tunis from 17 to 31 October 2026?

No. Evacuation Day fell on Thursday 15 October, and the next public holiday is Revolution Day on Thursday 17 December.

Where can I buy tickets for concerts and theatre in Tunis?

Most events in this guide are sold through tunis.events, with prices in Tunisian dinars. Some shows at Le 4ème Art are marked almost full.

How much are the cheapest shows?

Several JAOU performances at Le 4ème Art and B7L9 cost 5 TND (about US$2), while the Yasmine Hamdan and Shabaka concerts start at 30 TND (about US$10).

When do Yasmine Hamdan and Nadah El Shazly play Tunis?

Yasmine Hamdan & Soudeni play the Conference Palace on Sunday 25 October at 19:30. Nadah El Shazly plays B7L9 Art Centre on Saturday 31 October at 19:30.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro Asks Court to Curb Meta Ads
World.content:
Court president Kassio Nunes Marques speaks at his swearing-in on 12 May 2026. He voted with Mendonça to keep the order, and the photo does not show the vote. Photo: Luiz Roberto/TSE / Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Saturday, 17 October, 5:01 p.m. ET · Source: Folha de S.Paulo and CNN Brasil, citing the campaign’s filing at the electoral court (TSE)

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Friday 16 October, Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign asked the electoral court (TSE) to join Lula’s case against Meta, the US owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

The claim The campaign says Meta lets negative ads against Flávio be paid for and shown, including by Lula’s official page, which the electoral court forbids.

Meta’s reply Meta says it “does not take sides in this or any other election” and will keep applying its rules.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 77% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (17 October, 4:58 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 81% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 20% and 21% ), as of 17 October, 11:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The court had not ruled on Flávio’s request to join the case, as of reports on 17 October.

The campaign of Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro and conservative presidential candidate, asked Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) on Friday 16 October to let him join President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s case against Meta. He says Meta is negligent in letting paid negative ads against him spread, Folha de S.Paulo reported on Saturday.

The filing turns a complaint by Lula’s side into a fight over how a US tech giant treats both candidates about a week before the Brazil election 2026. It matters to US readers because Meta is a US-listed company now accused of bias from both camps, and because the court’s answer can shape what Brazilians see online before the vote.

What Flávio Bolsonaro Asked the Court

His lawyers want to join as an interested third party in the case Lula’s campaign filed on 9 October, Folha reported. Lula’s lawyers had argued that Meta, owner of Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp, failed to deliver content from Lula and his supporters.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Flávio’s filing says Meta’s negligence is turning the work of his campaign and of the court into an “eternal and unacceptable” exercise in futility, in Folha’s account. The campaign says the negative ads are paid for by Lula’s official account and by third parties.

According to CNN Brasil, it asks the court to order Meta to stop paid negative ads until the runoff ends and to bar individuals and companies from buying electoral ads. It also asks that any ads restored to Lula’s page may not carry negative content.

The Numbers the Campaign Cites

The campaign relies on Meta’s public ad library, CNN Brasil reported. It says Lula’s Facebook page has paid for 3,908 negative ads against Flávio since September and that 2,035 of 2,624 ads started on 9 and 10 October were negative.

It also says 423 negative ads were still active on the morning of 16 October. These are the campaign’s own claims, and we have not verified them against the ad library.

Meta Denies Taking Sides

Meta told Folha it “does not take sides in this or any other election” and that claims it favours any campaign are unfounded. It said it will keep applying its rules, obeying Brazilian election law and correcting mistakes.

Folha also reported that Meta staff admitted in internal messages to restrictions that hurt Lula’s Instagram accounts and the algorithmic recommendation of Flávio’s profile on Instagram and his WhatsApp channel. On 9 October Lula’s official profile could not boost Instagram posts for almost 24 hours, according to the paper.

How the Meta Dispute Reached This Point

On Thursday 15 October the court ordered Meta to treat both campaigns alike, and we reported that Meta admitted technical faults on Lula’s accounts in a note to the court. Flávio’s filing now argues that the imbalance runs the other way, and that Lula’s side has benefited from paid distribution for months.

Folha quotes the filing as saying a Meta error that restricted one candidate’s ad account for a few hours should not be judged alone. The campaign says the other candidate has faced paid negative distribution for months.

What It Means for US Readers

Meta is a US company, so a ruling or fine in Brazil could reach its business and its political-ad rules in a country of more than 200 million people. The case also tests how far a foreign court can push a US platform to manage political ads.

For investors, a race priced at about 77% for Flávio on Polymarket can move on court news as well as polls. Our Brazil election odds page tracks the latest market prices.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5%, with each outcome priced separately (17 October, 4:58 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$185.4 million in total bets.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 80.8% · Lula 19.5% (US$187 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21% As of 17 October, 11:20 pm ET (04:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

As of reports on 17 October, the court had not said whether it will accept Flávio as an interested party or order any change to Meta’s ads. The campaign’s ad counts come from its own reading of Meta’s library and have not been confirmed by Meta or the court.

It is also unclear how much paid advertising either side can still run before the vote. The filing alleges bias by Meta toward Lula, while Lula’s earlier filing alleged the opposite.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign file against Meta?

It asked the electoral court (TSE) on Friday 16 October to join Lula’s case as an interested party. It says Meta lets negative ads against Flávio be paid for and spread.

Why did Lula’s campaign sue Meta?

According to Folha, on 9 October it told the court that Meta was failing to deliver content from Lula and his supporters. It also asked for data on negative ads paid for against him.

What does Meta say about the accusations?

Meta says it does not take sides in any election and will keep applying its rules. It says claims that it favours either campaign are unfounded.

What does the campaign want the court to do?

It wants Meta ordered to stop paid negative ads until the runoff ends and individuals and companies barred from buying electoral ads. As of reports on 17 October, the court had not ruled.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. The winner takes office as president.

World.title: Costa Rica Office Vacancy Could Hit 27% by 2030 as Multinationals Cut Jobs
World.content:
More than a quarter of Costa Rica’s office space could be sitting empty by 2030 if multinational companies keep cutting jobs, according to Daniel Álvarez, chief executive of Cushman & Wakefield | AB Advisory, a commercial real estate firm allied with Cushman & Wakefield. Álvarez puts the current average office vacancy rate near 19% and projects it will reach 27.1% by the end of the decade.

Álvarez said job-loss figures capture only about a third of the impact. Fewer corporate operations, he argued, mean emptier buildings, pressure on rents and knock-on effects for banks, builders, suppliers and retailers that depend on those companies.

His warning comes after data from the Costa Rican Social Security System (CCSS) showed free-zone employment fell by 2,205 jobs in July compared with the same month a year earlier, to 200,203 salaried workers. It was the first year-on-year decline in seven years. Business services and manufacturing, which together account for 85% of free-zone jobs, showed the sharpest slowdown.

Álvarez estimates that each job in the sector occupies about 11 square meters (118 square feet) of office space. On that basis, the July losses alone would free roughly 24,000 square meters (258,000 square feet), comparable to a Class A office tower.

He said Costa Rica already has more office space than demand supports. By his count, San José trails only Mexico City among Latin American cities in office space per 1,000 economically active residents, which in his view makes it unlikely that vacated buildings will refill quickly.

In separate remarks published last week, Álvarez cited office availability of 17.7% and said net absorption fell 11.7% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period of 2025. Availability and vacancy are related but distinct measures, and he did not reconcile the two figures publicly.

Álvarez said lenders that financed office construction and renovation would be exposed if building income falls and owners struggle to service their debt. Larger markets have specialized funds that buy obsolete buildings and reposition them, he noted, but Costa Rica’s market lacks the liquidity and depth to offer that kind of fallback.

The effects would reach well beyond real estate, according to Álvarez. He described a chain in which banks finance developers and builders, process payroll and extend credit cards and car and apartment loans to the workers multinationals employ. When those workers lose their jobs or leave the country, he said, demand for rental housing, vehicles and other goods and services falls with them.

Álvarez attributed the risk of foreign investment moving elsewhere to the prolonged appreciation of the colón against the dollar, which raises payroll costs for companies that earn their revenue in other currencies. He named Mexico, Guatemala, the Philippines and India as more competitive destinations.

Costa Rica originally drew service companies with qualified, bilingual and low-cost labor, Álvarez said, but that labor is no longer low-cost. He described the country as now among the most expensive in Latin America in which to operate.

The colón strengthened from ₡507.17 to ₡451.10 per dollar between July 31, 2025, and July 31, 2026. The Association of Free Zone Companies (Azofras) has said currency appreciation raised operating costs in free zones by as much as 30% over the past four years, and coffee producers have raised similar complaints about the exchange rate.

Several large employers have closed facilities or cut staff in Costa Rica since 2025, including Intel, Qorvo, Viant, Amazon and Boston Scientific, according to company announcements. Western Union said in September it would eliminate more than 1,000 positions over 12 months, adding to a string of job losses across the export sector.

Álvarez said he expects the trend to continue for some time, given how closely service companies watch their cost structures. How far office vacancy rises will depend in large part on the path of the exchange rate and on whether new investment arrives to fill the space that departing operations leave behind.

World.title: Costa Rica Through A Canadian’s Eyes: More Than Just Pura Vida
World.content:
It has been nine years since I made the move from Canada to Costa Rica, and I often find myself asking a simple question: Why do I feel so blessed to call this place home? Is it simply Pura Vida? Is it the climate, the ocean, the slower pace of life, or something much deeper?

Over the years, I have discovered that living in Costa Rica is about far more than the beautiful scenery and the lifestyle so many people dream of. It is about what happens to you when you step outside the life you have always known and allow yourself to become part of something different.

Of course, there are days when you question your decision. Anyone who has lived here for a significant amount of time knows that not everything is effortless. Banking can be complicated. Applying for or renewing a driver’s license can test your patience. Navigating residency and other administrative processes can require patience and persistence.

There are moments when you wonder why something that seems so simple elsewhere can feel so complex here. But then something happens that reminds you why you came.

Finding Small-Town Roots in a New World

When I moved to Costa Rica, I chose a small community, a little off the beaten path and away from the heavily touristed areas. I wanted an experience that would change my life. I wanted to discover what it meant to live somewhere completely different, to learn another culture, and to see the world from a new perspective. And I found it.

What surprised me most was how familiar parts of Costa Rican life felt. I grew up in Saskatchewan, Canada, where small-town connections, neighbors looking out for one another, and a deep sense of community were part of everyday life. In my corner of Costa Rica, I discovered something remarkably similar.

People welcomed me into their world. Neighbors became friends. Invitations to celebrations and local gatherings offered glimpses of a way of life that you cannot fully understand as a visitor simply passing through.

Becoming Part of the Rhythm

Acceptance did not happen overnight. It came through small, consistent moments: showing up, participating, accepting invitations, and being present. It came from taking the time to listen, learn, and appreciate traditions that were not my own.

I began to understand that becoming part of a community is not something you can expect simply because you have bought a home. It grows through relationships, consistency, and a genuine willingness to embrace the people and the culture around you. There is a difference between living in Costa Rica and becoming part of Costa Rica.

Neither is right or wrong. Many people come here and find their happiness within the vibrant international expat community. Those friendships and shared experiences can be incredibly valuable when building a new life far from home. There is no single way to experience this Costa Rica, and everyone must find the path that feels right for them.

For me, the greatest gift was the opportunity to step beyond what was familiar and become part of a community that has its own rhythms, traditions, and ways of seeing the world.

What Pura Vida Really Means

I have learned that Pura Vida is not a promise that every day will be easy. It does not eliminate paperwork or the occasional moment of wondering what on earth you were thinking when you packed up your life. Instead, perhaps Pura Vida is found in the moments between those frustrations.

It is in the neighbor who welcomes you, the invitation you did not expect, the celebration you are grateful to be included in, and the friendships that develop slowly and naturally over time. It is in realizing that the life you came here to find may look very different from the one you imagined before you arrived.

Perhaps the real journey is not about changing Costa Rica at all, but about allowing Costa Rica to change you. And if you allow it, that may be the most beautiful part of all.

From Personal Journey to Professional Purpose

That realization is what eventually shaped my professional life here. Today, I work in real estate across the Gold Coast in Guanacaste—from Playa Flamingo, Potrero, and Tamarindo north toward Playas del Coco.

After nearly a decade working alongside buyers and sellers on the Gold Coast, I have come to understand that purchasing property in Costa Rica is rarely just a transaction. It represents a fundamental shift in lifestyle, a new chapter, or the realization of a vision someone has held onto for years.

Moving across borders is a profound transition, both financially and personally. Having walked that path myself—from Saskatchewan winters to Guanacaste sunsets—I consider it a privilege to guide others as they navigate not just the legal and market realities of buying a home here, but the deeply personal journey of building a life in Costa Rica.

Whether you are in the early stages of dreaming, navigating the move yourself, or looking to buy or sell on the Gold Coast, my door is always open for a real conversation about what life here truly looks like. Nearly a decade after making that move myself, I am still learning from this country, its communities, and the people who welcomed me into their world.

Costa Rica became much more than the place where I chose to live.

It became the place that taught me a different way to live.

Author Bio

Wendy Stoneham moved from Saskatchewan, Canada, to coastal Costa Rica nearly a decade ago. Today, she works in real estate across Guanacaste—including Playa Flamingo, Potrero, Tamarindo, and Playas del Coco—guiding buyers and sellers through the financial, legal, and lifestyle transitions of moving to the Gold Coast.

World.title: Matthew McConaughey’s Tequila Brand Debuts in Costa Rica Through Luxury Hotel Partnership
World.content:
Pantalones Organic Tequila, the brand owned by actor Matthew McConaughey and his wife, Camila McConaughey, has made its official debut in Costa Rica through a partnership with Nekajui, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, on the Papagayo Peninsula in Guanacaste. The debut, announced on Oct. 14, introduces The Cowboy & Mermaid, a collection of four exclusive cocktails created for the resort. The menu blends Costa Rican ingredients with nods to the couple’s Texas and Brazil roots and to the sabanero cowboy heritage of Guanacaste.

“We literally met over margaritas, and have been known to enjoy a paloma as well. Tequila was the juice on our lips when we first spoke the language of love,” Matthew and Camila McConaughey said. “Bringing Pantalones to Costa Rica feels natural and Nekajui offers the perfect place to kick off your boots, sip tequila, and enjoy the view.”

The cocktails are served at five venues across the resort. They include Puna, the signature restaurant conceived by chef Diego Muñoz, and Ámbar, a bar suspended among the treetops. The collection is also available at Niri Beach Club, at Cooper’s, a hidden speakeasy, and at La Casona, the resort’s lobby lounge.

“At Nekajui, we believe the most meaningful travel experiences reveal the spirit of a destination,” said Cristian Albacar, general manager of Nekajui, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve. “Our collaboration with Pantalones has given us the opportunity to put a Nekajui twist on Matthew and Camila’s favorite cocktails, paying homage to their Texas and Brazil roots while continuing to deliver the rare, immersive experiences that define a Ritz-Carlton Reserve stay.”

Each of the four drinks reworks a classic with local ingredients. The Goiaba is a margarita made with reposado tequila, pink guava, agave, citrus and guava salt, a tribute to a fruit loved in both Costa Rica and Brazil. The Tixos Old Fashioned combines añejo tequila with cacao distillate, Costa Rican cold brew coffee and spiced chocolate bitters. It is meant to bridge the bold character of Texas with Costa Rica’s coffee and cacao traditions.

Guacachile is a spicy margarita built on blanco tequila and mezcal, with mandarin lime, agave, avocado, jalapeño and Tajín. Palomitas, a take on the paloma, mixes blanco tequila with Texas Ruby Red grapefruit, Costa Rican mandarin lime and coconut soda, finished with a popcorn salt rim that gives the drink its name.

Pantalones is a USDA-certified organic tequila made from 100% blue Weber agave and distilled in Amatitán, in the Mexican state of Jalisco. The company describes the Costa Rica launch as part of a broader international expansion and says the brand has collected more than 55 awards, including Double Gold medals at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition.

Nekajui, whose name comes from the Chorotega word for “lush garden,” opened in 2025 as the first Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Central and South America. The resort has 107 ocean-facing rooms, suites and treetop tents, along with 36 private residences, and sits about 45 minutes from the international airport in Liberia. It is part of a wave of high-end openings that is reshaping Guanacaste’s luxury hotel scene.

The cowboy theme draws on a tradition that remains central to life in Guanacaste, where the sabanero, the area’s working cattle hand, is still celebrated at fiestas, topes and rodeos across the region.

World.title: Your Android Phone May Soon Warn You Before a Costa Rica Earthquake Hits
World.content:
If you have an Android phone in Costa Rica, it may soon buzz with a warning a few seconds before strong shaking reaches you. Google announced yesterday that it is expanding its Android Earthquake Alerts System from 98 countries and regions to more than 200. Costa Rica was reported among the newly covered countries in the updated coverage list published alongside the announcement.

Do not count on it yet. Google’s announcement named Panama and Guatemala but not Costa Rica, and Google has not published its full list of new countries. Even in Panama, where President José Raúl Mulino announced the country’s inclusion on Thursday, phones were still showing the feature as unavailable that evening, a sign the rollout is gradual. Local reports said phones in Costa Rica showed the same message. Google has not said when, or whether, the alerts will switch on here.

The timing matters. A week ago, the magnitude 7.7 earthquake centered in Panama was felt across most of Costa Rica, and the Volcanological and Seismological Observatory of Costa Rica (OVSICORI) measured it at the same 7.7. Aftershocks from that quake have kept rattling the Southern Zone since.

Here is how the system works. Every smartphone has a tiny motion sensor called an accelerometer. When enough Android phones in one area register shaking at the same time, Google’s servers estimate where the quake started and how big it is, then send alerts to phones in the area expected to shake.

The warning is possible because earthquakes send out two kinds of waves. The first wave is fast and weak. The damaging wave travels slower. The alert races ahead of that second wave, which can buy you a few seconds to get under a table. Alerts go out only for quakes of magnitude 4.5 or higher. Google says the system has sent more than 1 billion alerts worldwide since it launched in 2021.

You would see one of three alerts, depending on how hard your location is expected to shake. A Be Aware alert is a simple notification for light shaking, and it respects your volume and Do Not Disturb settings. A Be Ready alert is meant for noticeable shaking and can break through Do Not Disturb. A Take Action alert fills your screen, plays a loud sound and tells you to drop, cover and hold on. It is reserved for moderate to strong shaking.

Google says that in the coming months the Be Ready alert will also show a map of where shaking was detected and the estimated magnitude. You do not need to download anything. Earthquake alerts are on by default in countries where the system is active. To check yours, open Settings, tap Safety and emergency, then Earthquake alerts. If you do not see that menu, try Location, then Advanced, then Earthquake alerts.

Keep Wi-Fi or mobile data on, because alerts arrive over the internet. Your phone uses your approximate location to decide whether you are in the shaking zone. Google says that location is not used to identify you. Know the limits before you rely on it. The system will not catch every earthquake. Magnitude estimates can be wrong. An alert may reach you before, during or after the shaking starts, and you may get one for a quake you never feel.

If you are very close to the epicenter, expect little or no warning, because the damaging wave arrives almost as soon as the first one. OVSICORI seismologist Marino Protti has said early warning systems tend to be most useful between 50 and 150 kilometers (31 and 93 miles) from the epicenter.

The Google system works only on Android. If you use an iPhone, or want an alert source that works right now, Costa Rica already has free options built on the national seismic networks. OVSICORI, at the National University (UNA), runs the OVSICORI-UNA Alerta Terremotos app for both Android and iPhone. It sends early warnings based on the observatory’s own seismic stations and lets you choose the minimum magnitude you want to hear about.

The National Seismological Network (RSN) at the University of Costa Rica has its own free app on Google Play and the App Store with official quake reports. The university’s Seismic Engineering Laboratory also posts strong-motion notices on Telegram and on X. The two kinds of systems detect quakes differently, so they will not always alert at the same moment for the same event. Using both is reasonable.

Costa Rica was left out of Google’s system for years. It has been reported that the feature was blocked here for legal reasons, because Costa Rican law gives the National Emergency Commission (CNE) authority over emergency alerts. In a July response to a formal information request, the CNE said it had no direct relationship with Google, that the company’s data was not an official source for its decisions, and that a tool limited to Android phones could not reach the whole population.

The commission did not cite a specific legal provision barring the service. Protti, consulted by the CNE, saw no conflict with the national alert system but warned that people could confuse the two tools. Whichever alert reaches you first, the advice when the ground starts moving does not change. Drop to the floor, take cover under something sturdy and hold on until the shaking stops. In a country where the ground moves often, a few seconds of warning only helps if you already know what to do with them.

World.title: Costa Rica’s President Says US Government Already Operates on Costa Rican Soil
World.content:
President Laura Fernández said U.S. government agencies already carry out operations on Costa Rican territory, describing them as the continuation of existing security arrangements rather than a new proposal. She made the remarks in an interview with Fox News when asked whether she would support U.S. forces operating here.

Fernández said a strict collaboration protocol with the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) began under the previous administration. She also pointed to joint patrols in Costa Rican waters and a shared strategy against what she called narcoterrorism.

She did not say how large the operations are, where they take place or how many U.S. personnel are involved. The Presidency has not released further details on their scope. Fernández stressed that Costa Rica has no army and relies on civilian police for its security. She said she will push hard-line legislative reforms against criminal groups and described the country as being on the threshold of a major transformation in security.

The comments go further than her remarks in September, when she said that U.S. ground operations would benefit national security if they targeted shared goals such as drug trafficking. At the time she said no such process was under way and that any step of that kind would require legislative approval.

Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and cooperation with the United States has largely run through a maritime counternarcotics agreement and through permits that the Legislative Assembly must approve before U.S. ships, aircraft and personnel can enter national territory.

The interview came during a week dominated by security policy. Fernández opened a prison modeled on El Salvador’s CECOT in Alajuela and announced that six Mexican cartels and three Colombian groups will be added to Costa Rica’s list of terrorist organizations.

Today she traveled to El Salvador to meet President Nayib Bukele and tour CECOT, accompanied by Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar. Costa Rican also moved three Mexican nationals linked to the Sinaloa Cartel to Juan Santamaría International Airport to be handed over to the DEA for extradition. The three were arrested in April 2025 aboard a yacht off Quepos carrying about 840 kilograms (1,850 pounds) of suspected cocaine.

World.title: Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28
World.content:
Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware is hosting a public auction of industrial equipment, commercial tools, generators, office machinery and surplus supplies.

The auction takes place on Wednesday, October 28, starting at 8:00am at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware in Belmopan. Everything will go to the highest bidder. Terms are cash, and food and drinks will be available on site.

Among the highlights is a wide range of power equipment, including a Katolight 125kW diesel generator, a Cummins 40kW diesel generator, Generac commercial and standby generators from 9kW to 222kW, Generac and Honda portable generators, and ASCO transfer switches.

Heavy equipment and shop tools include a Mitsubishi electric forklift, a John Deere backhoe extender attachment, Delta and Powermatic industrial table saws, a wood lathe, an electric pallet jack and hydraulic cylinders.

Also up for auction are large format printers, commercial food prep equipment, new pressure washers, a new air compressor, a 54 inch walk behind mower, appliances, furniture, electric scooters, solar batteries, building materials and much more.

The auctioneer is Henry B. Dueck, who can be reached at 610 0158. For enquiries, contact Frans Blatz at 615 9646.

World.title: NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops
World.content:
NASA Satellites track warming Pacific waters as El Niño develops

By Zoila Palma: NASA satellites are tracking signs of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean, including rising sea surface temperatures and changes in ocean levels and colour.

According to NASA, one of the first indicators appeared in January 2026, when a wave of warm water known as a Kelvin wave was detected near Micronesia in the western Pacific. By early April, the waves had reached the eastern Pacific, contributing to warmer ocean temperatures and rising sea levels in some areas.

Kelvin waves transport heat across the Pacific Ocean, helping trigger a chain reaction that weakens the trade winds and allows warm water to accumulate farther east. NASA reported that sea levels in parts of the eastern Pacific rose by approximately 1 to 1.3 feet, while levels around Indonesia and northern Australia were 6 to 8 inches below normal.

NASA data also show that sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific are approximately 3 degrees Fahrenheit, or 1.7 degrees Celsius, above the long-term average, with the possibility of further warming in the coming months. These temperature changes are significant because ocean heat influences atmospheric conditions, affecting rainfall and weather patterns around the world.

Another sign of El Niño is a change in the ocean’s colour as populations of microscopic marine plants known as phytoplankton decline in some equatorial Pacific waters.

NASA says that its scientists will continue monitoring El Niño through its fleet of Earth-observing satellites to better understand the phenomenon and its potential effects.

World.title: Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize
World.content:
Flood alert remains in effect as continued rains affect Belize

By Zoila Palma: A flood alert remains in effect across Belize as additional rainfall is expected over the weekend.

The National Meteorological Service (NMS) forecasts between 2 and 4 inches of rain in portions of the country over on Sunday.

Residents in low-lying, flood-prone and riverside communities are urged to remain alert and monitor official weather updates.

The NMS warns that smaller streams and tributaries could rise quickly.

Although several rivers remain at normal or below-normal levels, conditions could change rapidly as rainfall accumulates.

Residents are advised to exercise caution near rivers, streams and low-level crossings and never attempt to cross flooded roads or waterways.

World.title: National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service
World.content:
National Fire Service honors 27 officers for long service

By Zoila Palma: The National Fire Service (NFS) has recognized 27 officers for their years of dedicated service in protecting lives, safeguarding property and responding to emergencies across Belize.

The awards ceremony was held in Belize City on October 16, 2026, under the Ministry of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise.

The ceremony celebrated the commitment and contributions of officers who have dedicated years of their careers to public safety and supporting communities during emergencies. Their service reflects the important role the NFS plays in providing emergency response services and protecting Belizeans throughout the country.

Among those recognized were Assistant Divisional Officer Kenneth Mortis and Station Officer Brenton Gentle, who each completed 30 years of service. Retired Station Officer Miguel Medina was also honoured for completing 20 years of service. Their years of experience and dedication highlight the commitment required to serve in the National Fire Service.

Minister of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise, Henry Charles Usher, emphasized the importance of recognizing officers who have devoted their careers to serving and protecting the people of Belize. “Today, we honour not only the years these officers have given, but also the important contribution they have made to our nation,” Usher said.

World.title: International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living
World.content:
International News: Police and protesters clash across France in major unrest over cost of living

By Zoila Palma: Violent clashes erupted between police and protesters across France today as hundreds of thousands of people reportedly took to the streets to demonstrate against rising living costs, inequality and declining public services.

The unrest, described as some of the country’s most destructive in years, resulted in at least 272 arrests, according to France’s Interior Ministry, following incidents in Paris, Marseille, Toulouse, Angers and Lyon, Reuters report.

The CGT union estimated that 800,000 people participated in the demonstrations, although the Interior Ministry did not provide its own estimate.

Protesters said many marches were peaceful and blamed the violence on individuals who joined to cause damage and confront police. In Paris, officers deployed tear gas as clashes intensified, while shops and restaurants were damaged, vehicles and trash cans were set on fire, and several central areas experienced disruption. In Lyon, protesters set fire to the tourist office, while Marseille’s mayor reported vandalism at the town hall.

French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said the government would not be intimidated by the violence, accusing the far-left and criminals of exploiting the demonstrations ahead of next year’s presidential election.

Meanwhile, protests over rising costs also took place in other European countries today.

World.title: Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage
World.content:
Belize celebrates International Day of Living Heritage

By Zoila Palma: Belize joined the global observance of the International Day of Living Heritage, celebrating the traditions, knowledge, skills and cultural practices that connect communities and help shape the country’s national identity.

The observance highlights the importance of preserving Belize’s rich intangible cultural heritage, including the customs and practices passed down through generations. These traditions continue to play an important role in strengthening community connections and maintaining Belize’s diverse cultural identity.

Through community-driven initiatives across the country, efforts are being made to place living heritage at the heart of national development, NICH noted.

NICH also expressed gratitude to its national and international partners and collaborators for their continued support in protecting and promoting the country’s living heritage.

World.title: International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America
World.content:
International News: Taiwan promotes Educational exchanges and talent development partnerships in Latin America

By Zoila Palma: Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) is strengthening educational exchanges and cooperation with Latin America through initiatives aimed at developing talent, encouraging innovation and expanding economic partnerships.

MOFA Deputy Minister Chen Ming-chi hosted a welcome luncheon for students participating in the Executive Master’s in Asia-Pacific and Latin American Studies at Tamkang University’s Department of Global Politics and Economics.

Chen thanked the university for its longstanding efforts to promote exchanges with Latin America and highlighted Taiwan’s continued investment in education, talent development and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence.

Chen also pointed to initiatives such as the Taiwan-Paraguay Polytechnic University project and Taiwan’s support for Taiwanese businesses seeking to expand internationally. He noted that these partnerships can help Taiwan’s diplomatic allies develop new industries through mutually beneficial cooperation. He encouraged the visiting students to explore opportunities for collaboration between Taiwan and their respective home countries during their stay.

Student representative Lorena Yael Piedra Cobo of Ecuador thanked MOFA and Tamkang University for organizing the academic courses and activities.

World.title: Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown
World.content:
Belize City Council, IDB explore plans to revitalize historic Downtown

By Zoila Palma: The Belize City Council is continuing discussions with the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) on a proposed comprehensive program to revitalize historic downtown Belize City, with plans being explored to improve public spaces, support businesses and preserve the city’s historic character.

The proposed revitalization area includes the Albert and Regent Street corridors, stretching from the Swing Bridge toward the House of Culture and surrounding historic centre.

Ideas under discussion include cleaning and repainting building façades, improving sidewalks and public spaces, updating traffic signs and making sections of downtown more pedestrian-friendly.

A possible pedestrian route could connect the Swing Bridge with the market, courthouse area and City Hall, while a waterfront boardwalk along the southern coast toward the House of Culture has also been discussed.

The Council and IDB have also explored ways to make better use of vacant or underused lots and encourage more people to live in the downtown area. The IDB’s “IDB for Cities and Regions” program was discussed as a potential avenue for supporting future investment. However, the Council emphasized that discussions remain at an early stage and that the scope of any project has not been finalized.

Any future program would require careful assessment of its costs, the City Council’s financial and legal capacity, and coordination with national partners.

The proposed downtown rejuvenation aims to create more inviting public spaces, support local businesses and protect Belize City’s heritage while making the historic centre a more attractive place to visit, work and live.

World.title: Manchester dad charged in suspected revenge killing of two men over daughter’s murder
World.content:
File photo of the crime scene in Land Settlement, Manchester where two men were gunned down in March 2026.

MANCHESTER, Jamaica – A Manchester father has been charged with conspiracy to murder in relation to the killing of two men in the parish in March that is believed to have been a reprisal for the shooting death of his daughter a month earlier.

Charged is 37-year-old Kumar Obrien, otherwise known as ‘Frazzle’, of Melrose Drive, Land Settlement.

The deceased have been identified as 29-year-old farmer Yakieni Shaw, also known as ‘Yankee’, of Comfort District, Manchester, and 21-year-old Damien Edwards, otherwise known as ‘Damie’, of Melrose Gardens, Williamsfield, in the parish.

Reports from the Mandeville Police are that Obrien allegedly conspired with other men to kill Edwards and Shaw, who were gunned down about 3:50 pm on Saturday, March 14, 2026.

The shooting is believed to have been a reprisal for the fatal shooting of Obrien’s four-year-old daughter, Saniyah Obrien, on Sunday, February 8, while they were seated in his Voxy motor car in the parish.

An investigations led to Obrien being apprehended, interviewed, and subsequently charged. He is scheduled to appear before the Manchester Parish Court on Wednesday, October 21.

World.title: Adam Stewart, Sheryl Lee Ralph honoured at AFJ Hummingbird Gala
World.content:
Sandals Resorts Executive Chairman Adam Stewart and Emmy Award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph pose with their awards after being honoured at the American Friends of Jamaica (AFJ) Hummingbird Gala at The Plaza in New York on Friday, October 16, 2026.

Sandals Resorts Executive Chairman Adam Stewart and Emmy Award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph were honoured at the American Friends of Jamaica (AFJ) Hummingbird Gala, held at The Plaza in New York on Friday,

Stewart received the International Achievement Award in recognition of his contribution to Caribbean tourism, business and philanthropy, while Ralph received the International Humanitarian Award for her achievements in entertainment and longstanding advocacy, particularly in HIV/AIDS awareness.

Prime Minister Andrew Holness and Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett were among the guests at the annual fundraising gala, which brought together business leaders, philanthropists and members of the Jamaican diaspora in support of AFJ’s work across Jamaica, including ongoing Hurricane Melissa recovery efforts.

World.title: DIRTY COWARDS
World.content:
Police personnel at the scene where one of their colleagues was fatally shot and another left with lifethreatening injuries in the Five Miles area of St Catherine on Friday. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

THE police have identified one of three men killed in a firefight in the Five Miles area off the Sligoville main road in St Catherine, Friday morning, during which gunmen used a child to draw cops closer before opening fire, killing one law enforcer.

He is Malique Hussey, otherwise called Mal Boss, from Spanish Town, St Catherine, with connections in Five Miles.

According to the police, Hussey was a known associate of a high-risk target identified as Kenroy Willis, who operates out of the St Andrew North Police Division and is wanted for four murders.

Up to news time the police had not determined the identities of the other two men who were fatally shot in the gun battle which also resulted in the death of Corporal Trevoy Shaw, who was assigned to the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Special Operations Unit, and the injury to a constable who, up to press time, was in hospital in critical condition.

A third cop suffered minor injuries, not gunshot-related, during the incident.

A 10-year-old child was also shot in what Jamaica Observer sources say was a deliberate attack by Hussey, who was her father.

According to the police, about 5:15 Friday morning members of its Special Operations Unit went in search of Willis, Hussey, and their cronies.

On arrival, the police were met with gunfire by men who had barricaded themselves in a house with a woman and three children, including a monthsold baby.

During the stand-off the men indicated that they wanted to surrender, and used one of the children to signal their willingness to lay down their illegal firearms.

“I can confirm that a child was held out the door, and it was declared that they were willing to surrender, and when the police approached, seeking to retrieve the child, fire was opened upon those policemen,” senior communications strategist at the Jamaica Constabulary Force Dennis Brooks told journalists metres from the shooting scene.

“The gunmen shot from behind the child, which placed the police in a precarious position, even in accessing the building, because of the presence of children,” Brooks said.

He explained that they were met by heavily armed men, and a woman declared from inside the building that she and two children were inside.

The woman, the injured 10-year-old, and the baby were allowed to leave the building by the gunmen, who kept a child inside the house as they continued to fire at the cops who were supported by members of the Jamaica Defence Force.

According to Brooks, the men manipulated the presence of the children in the house and the police’s willingness to accept their surrender, pretending to wave the ‘white flag’ multiple times.

“It is the intention of the police on every operation to bring persons to justice, place them before the court, and so it is not our intention to proceed marauding into a building — whether or not there are children and women in there.

And if there is an indication, even the slightest indication, that they are willing to surrender then we are going to engage that possibility,” Brooks said.

He lamented the death of the corporal who was trying to retrieve the child, describing it as heartbreaking.

“I left several policemen and women in tears in Kingston because they knew him well… He was promoted to the rank of corporal about a month ago, which speaks to his own dedication and the recognition of his work.

“I mean, imagine at this time he is just enjoying this new development in his career, and he is [the] pride of his family in this moment, and for his life, his light to be put out in such a manner in seeking to make this country a safer place — it is heartbreaking,” Brooks said.

The pain of Shaw’s colleagues was palpable at Spanish Town Hospital as news spread that two of their colleagues had been rushed there with gunshot wounds.

It became worse when it was confirmed that he had died while the constable had been rushed into surgery.

Shortly after 10:00 am a policeman was seen leaving the hospital’s Accident and Emergency Department (A&E), with sources indicating that he was the person who had suffered the non-gunshot-related injury.

The cop appeared to be in some discomfort as he limped towards a police vehicle parked on the grounds of the hospital.

The vehicle was quickly surrounded by other cops.

Shortly after 11:00 am, people who appeared to be related to the shot cops stormed onto the facility, with cries of grief, as they sought to enter the A&E Department seeking answers.

About five minutes later a black police vehicle raced onto the compound, with cops carrying what appeared to be the bodies of the three slain criminals.

For a minute chaos unfolded as several people hurried to the van to observe what was happening.

But this curiosity was stopped in its tracks by police personnel, who chased away civilians trying to capture videos or photos.

In his immediate reaction to the attack on the men and women under his command, Police Commissioner Dr Kevin Blake, who visited the scene, described the gunmen as murderous.

He said while death is always a possibility for a cop, “We prepare, we equip, so that every single member after an operation goes home to his or her family safe and injury-free.

Unfortunately this morning, that hope and that preparation was shattered.” Blake told the police on the scene that the best way to honour their fallen comrade would be to remain relentless.

“Because we are who we are, because we would rather take them in to face the court, we lost a member… let not that define how we operate going forward,” said Blake.

“I know it is a tough time, and for the colleagues of the officer killed and the officer injured, I understand,” added Blake.

The attack on the police was condemned by political representatives during Friday’s sitting of the Senate, human rights group Jamaicans For Justice, and several other organisations

World.title: Clarendon power shift stalled by court order
World.content:
Member of Parliament for Clarendon Central Delroy Williams (left) and May Pen Mayor Joel Williams (second right) celebrate with JLP supports after special sitting of the Clarendon Municipal Corporation on Friday at which an ex parte interim injunction was tabled which blocked the PNPs efforts to take over leadership of the corporation

THE People’s National Party (PNP) says it plans to challenge a Supreme Court injunction that has stalled its bid to take control of the Clarendon Municipal Corporation.

PNP senior councillor in the corporation Scean Barnswell has also questioned how the injunction was handled at the corporation, claiming it was not entered in its registry, and raised doubts about whether it had been properly served.

The dispute emerged at a special meeting of the corporation on Friday, where councillor for the May Pen North Division Tanyalee Williams formally made the switch from the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) to the PNP, giving the Opposition party a 12-10 majority in the 22-member council.

The switch had created an opening for the PNP to seek the removal of Mayor Joel Williams and Deputy Mayor Clivalee Mundle and elect replacements backed by the new majority.

However, the meeting was halted after the mayor said an ex parte interim injunction prevented the council from dealing with the matter.

In a statement issued on Friday, the PNP described the injunction as “profoundly anti-democratic”.

The PNP said its legal challenge is intended to allow the meeting to continue and the relevant resolutions to be considered.

Earlier, during the special meeting, Barnswell also raised concerns about how the injunction reached the corporation, questioning whether it had been formally recorded and properly served.

“Chairman, let the record reflect that we have asked the question of how the document has been received at the municipal corporation? We have a registry that logs all external correspondence that comes to the CEO.

It is logged into the registry and I just want to place on record that there is no indication of this document being logged into the council’s registry,” he said.

Barnswell later told reporters that the document appeared to have been presented without the usual procedures being followed.

“There was no signature on the document by the…judge who would have seen it.

There was no official seal or stamp on the document itself, [and] while we respect the court’s decision, we just want to highlight some of the things which we have a problem with the document, no signature, no file date, no official seal or stamp, and it was just a courtesy copy that was sent to us.

So… our attorney is vetting it some more, and they will advise further as to how we proceed,” added Barnswell.

CEO of the corporation Rowhan Blake told councillors during the meeting that he was served in his capacity as the defendant and had attended court at 9:05 Friday morning.

Blake said he then circulated the decision to councillors by email, using the same method through which he normally sends minutes and other correspondence.

He said the order restrained the corporation, its councillors and officers from considering, debating or voting on agenda items two to five, which were the ones that covered the proposed changes to the corporation’s leadership.

The mayor relied on the order to stop the meeting from proceeding.

But PNP councillors disputed his handling of the adjournment, arguing that the decision to end the meeting should have been put to a vote and decided by the majority.

Councillor Romain Morris (PNP, Mocho Division) referred to the Local Government Act and called on the corporation’s CEO to guide the meeting on how it should proceed.

“Mr CEO please note this meeting was not adjourned properly.

The motion of adjournment, Mr Chairman, is a question and is set out in the Local Government Act section 32(J) and with that said, Mr Chairman, it must be adhered to… With that being said the chairman is no longer in his seat, [and] I am going to ask if we can elect a member among ourselves to continue with the remainder of the meeting from the majority,” questioned Morris.

His intervention followed the mayor’s repeated attempts to end the meeting, citing the injunction.

The PNP councillors maintained that the decision to adjourn should have been put to a vote and decided by the majority, rather than the mayor declaring the meeting over.

As the dispute continued, Morris suggested that the councillors remaining in the chamber elect someone from their majority to continue with the meeting.

However, JLP councillors disputed that approach, maintaining that the mayor had already adjourned the meeting and that the council could not proceed in his absence.

PNP councillors continued to challenge the handling of the adjournment and called on Blake to advise them on the way forward, but Blake and the mayor subsequently left the chamber, even as the PNP members maintained that the meeting had not been properly adjourned.

The dispute over the adjournment added to the disagreement over the injunction, with the PNP unable to proceed with the planned leadership changes despite its new 12-10 majority.

Mayor Williams, speaking with the media after the meeting, defended his decision to seek court intervention.

“We are seeking to get clarity as it relates to the Section 16 of the Local Government Act… They are the ones who are playing political football with the people’s business, not us on this side.

We’re always serious about getting the people’s business done in the parish of Clarendon and [by] extension across Jamaica.

That’s what we’re here for, not to play games,” declared the mayor.

He declined to discuss Williams’s decision to leave the JLP, saying: “She’s on the other side and I don’t wish to speak on her.”

World.title: New custos commits to St Elizabeth’s post-Melissa recovery
World.content:
New custos rotulorum for St Elizabeth Bernard Henry gets a kiss from his wife Verna after he received his Instrument of Appointment from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen on Thursday. (Photos: Garfield Robinson)

BUSINESSMAN Bernard Henry has vowed to build on the work of predecessors as he moves into the role of custos rotulorum for St Elizabeth.

Henry received his Instrument of Appointment from Governor General Sir Patrick Allen, after taking the Oath of Allegiance and the Oath of Office during a ceremony at King’s House on Thursday.

He replaces Beryl Rochester who served 12 years as custos rotulorum for the parish.

“This is a humbling office; I’m very fortunate.

We have had an acting custos who was tremendous so we want to make sure that we work to continue to build on what our former custos, Honourable Beryl Rochester, put in place, and the custodes before, and also what Acting Custos Stevon Sheriffe… did.

So my role is really for us to build from there,” Henry told the Jamaica Observer following the ceremony.

According to Henry, the role is even more significant following the devastation caused by Hurricane Melissa last year.

“To be able to step into this role at this time, when we are in the process of rebuilding our parish, is significant.

And so we want to make sure that we operate with humility, that we are there to help, to add value, and to rebuild St Elizabeth.

“We are a very proud parish and we are a resilient people.

We want to show off who we are and what we do, and we want to make sure that the people who are hurting, we are there to lift them up — especially the youth,” Henry added.

The Category 5 storm, which hit Jamaica on October 28, 2025, left many residents of St Elizabeth scrambling to rebuild their lives, but Henry remains optimistic about the future of the parish.

“I’m hoping that we will get the support that we need to rebuild even better than what we had before.

I see the devastation but I’m also looking for the silver lining, and the silver lining is that we will be able to build back even better.

That’s what I see.

That’s what I want to support.

And so St Elizabeth people, we will come again,” Henry said.

In his address, Governor General Sir Patrick Allen charged Henry to execute the role with sound judgement, objectivity, and the ability to command public confidence.

“You will be my representative in St Elizabeth, and that means that you will support the administration of justice, provide leadership to the network of justices of the peace, and encourage civic participation.

I welcome your intention to improve access to the justices of the peace in St Elizabeth, to maintain meaningful engagement with communities, and encourage opportunities for our young people,” said Sir Patrick.

“Such priorities are especially pertinent as St Elizabeth continues its recovery and renewal.

You have spoken of the importance of listening, learning, and seeking wise counsel.

I encourage you to remain guided by these principles, recognising that the distinction of public office rests ultimately upon the honour with which its responsibilities are discharged,” added Sir Patrick.

The governor general said Henry’s long-standing investment in education, institutional governance, and national development has earned the businessman his confidence.

“He has demonstrated the vision and discipline required to establish enterprises, navigate complex responsibilities, and forge enduring partnerships.

However, his contribution to St Elizabeth extends beyond commercial enterprise.

“As inaugural chairman of the St Elizabeth Community Development Foundation, and through its involvement with the St Elizabeth Homecoming Foundation, he has helped to foster cooperation and advance the interests of the parish.

These experiences assume relevance as he undertakes the responsibilities of custos rotulorum,” said Sir Patrick.

World.title: Changes coming for Miss Jamaica World pageant
World.content:
The 23 finalists competing in the 2026 Miss Jamaica World pageant

Changes will be implemented for this year’s staging of the Miss Jamaica World beauty pageant.

At a sashing exercise and the Beach Beauty Fast Track competition held at the Jamaica Pegasus hotel in New Kingston on Tuesday night, Dahlia Harris, of the Miss Jamaica World Organization, gave an insight into how the new titleholder will be selected.

“Forty per cent of each contestant’s overall assessment will come from her performance throughout the training and development programme, while 60 per cent will come from the judges’ assessment.

Why have we made this change? Because we believe that how a young woman conducts herself throughout the journey is just as important as how she performs when she steps in front of the judges,” Harris told the Jamaica Observer.

“We want to reward punctuality, participation, discipline, deportment, commitment, and a willingness to learn.

We want contestants to understand that professionalism is not something you switch on when the spotlight comes on.

It is demonstrated in how you show up, how you treat people, how you respond to challenges, and how seriously you take the opportunities presented to you.

The crown should represent more than a performance on one evening; it should reflect the character, consistency, and commitment demonstrated throughout the competition.

And we believe this revised assessment structure will help us achieve exactly that.” Instead of a Top 10, a Top 12 will be selected and comprise the winners of the 5 fasttrack competitions; namely, Beach Beauty, Talent, Fitness Challenge, Top Model, and Beauty with a Purpose.

There will also be five judges’ selections and, for the very first time, the Head-to- Head and Multi-Media challenge winners.

“The Challenge events are, therefore, more extensive this year.

The Head-to-Head Challenge, for example, has already selected a top 10 based on their Round One performance and, on Thursday, October 15, they will compete in the semi-final and final rounds.

The judges will select a Top 5 and the public will select a People’s Choice winner, who will join them to complete a Top 6,” said Harris.

At Tuesday night’s event, the 23 finalists were sashed by their respective sponsors.

Afterwards, the Beach Beauty Fast Track competition took place, with Seana’Kay Wright, who is sponsored by Southdale Hardware and Glass Supplies, taking first place.

First runner-up was Matea Mahal Smith, Miss Aveeno, while medical doctor Samantha McLeod, Miss Island Smiles, was named second runner-up.

Ironically, at the recent Fitness Challenge, held at the Emancipation Park in New Kingston, Smith was declared the first-place winner and Wright was her first runner-up.

The coronation of Miss Jamaica World 2026 is scheduled for November 1 at Karl Hendrickson Auditorium, Jamaica College.

World.title: From Spanish Town dreams to Broward County honour
World.content:
D’Angel receives the key to the city of Tamarac from Marlon Bolton, Tamarac’s vice mayor during the Red Gala event in Florida last week.

WHEN dancehall artiste D’Angel received word that she would be honoured with the key to the City of Tamarac, Florida, the tears came before she could fully comprehend the magnitude of the moment.

And, as if that were not enough to process, she arrived in Florida to learn that she would also receive the key to Broward County. The double honour overwhelmed her. “I couldn’t hold back my tears of joy. I was like, ‘God, this is all you,’ ” she recalled.

For the woman who describes her journey in music as one of fighting, overcoming, and enduring more lows than highs, the recognition was more than a ceremonial milestone. It was an unexpected acknowledgement of the work she has put into her career and the resilience she has had to summon along the way.

The artiste, whose given name is Michelle Downer, said she had not realised the extent to which her efforts were being noticed, but was grateful for the recognition. “I never knew anyone was paying attention to what I’ve been doing because it has been a rough journey of fight and overcoming.

But look at me now, just a girl from Spanish Town who had big dreams,” she said. “I’m very grateful and thankful to be honoured outside my country in such high standard. Getting the key to the City of Tamarac and Broward County is mind-blowing.

I’m still processing it.” For D’Angel, the honour represents more than personal achievement, it speaks also to the weight she believes she has carried on behalf of Jamaicans through her music and charitable work.

That sense of responsibility is central to how she views the recognition. It also reinforces the importance of how she conducts herself and represents her country on the international stage.

“I definitely will continue to represent and live up to my honour through my music and deportment, because I’m not only representing my country, I’m now representing a city and a state I was not born in,” she said.

“I have to do my best…” D’Angel continued: “I had a lot of highs and lows moments, more lows than highs, but it never stopped me from pursuing my dreams…

I know I was born for greatness, and no naysayer could ever abort my destiny.

With every moment I had to overcome, I became stronger, more focused, and resilient.” Her ability to keep moving forward, she explained, has been shaped by the people and beliefs that have anchored her through difficult periods.

Among her strongest influences are her mother and her son, whom she identifies as the driving forces behind her life. Their influence helped her to keep going, even when the odds seemed stacked against her.

“I never felt like quitting. Yuh mad?” she said, laughing off the suggestion. “One thing my mom always tell me, never let anyone rejoice over me, so that alone kept me going.

Also, my son, who’s the driving force of my life.” Music itself has also served as a source of encouragement. Knowing that her work has strengthened others has reinforced her belief that she has a purpose to fulfil.

“My music also gave me strength, because I see where it strengthens others as well, so I know I’m purpose and I belong here,” she said. “Is only one Angel, so I had to carry my cross and let God do the rest.” That faith has become increasingly important to her approach to life and career.

D’Angel said that, while she has always worked hard to advance her ambitions, she has recently become more intentional about praying, relinquishing control over outcomes, and placing greater trust in God.

“I’m always working overtime, but since lately I start praying harder and leave everything in God’s hand, and the proof is in the results,” she said.

“Sometimes you have to let go and let God.” The latest honour, she believes, is not the end of the journey, as her work is not finished, “Once you believe in yourself and be authentic, everything else will be added and the world will respond,” she said.

World.title: No letting go
World.content:
MONTEGO BAY, St James — A man who reportedly refused to accept it when the woman was ready to end the relationship has found himself before the court facing charges of assault occasioning bodily harm.

Andre Edwards appeared in the St James Parish Court, before Judge Natiesha Fairclough-Hylton on Wednesday, to answer the charge which stems from an incident on August 28 when the woman visited his home in Norwood, St James, reportedly to collect money.

According to the allegations, the two became embroiled in an argument during which the woman expressed her intention to end the relationship.

Edwards allegedly refused to accept the decision, and the confrontation escalated when he began squeezing her neck.

A physical struggle followed during which Edwards allegedly pushed the complainant to the ground and strangled her with a cord.

She managed to break free and made her way to the police station to report the incident.

The woman reportedly suffered pain, swelling, and bruising to her throat and right eye.

Edwards was subsequently arrested and charged.

When cautioned by the police he reportedly denied the allegations and said, “Officer, yuh nuh si di woman deh a liar? Mi nuh wah nutten fi do wid da woman deh.” Judge Fairclough-Hylton extended his bail and set November 11 for the matter to be mentioned again.

World.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine a ‘planned operation’, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
The restrictions have revived questions on Ukraine’s reliance on the satellite system operated by a U.S. company amid escalating tensions between Kyiv and the White House. “This will cost many of us our lives,” an experienced Ukrainian officer told POLITICO and the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network earlier this week.

“We’re reaching out to everyone at the military level, at the Ministry of Defense level, and at the diplomatic level, including to SpaceX. Right now, no one is responding to our military or the Ministry of Defense,” Zelenskyy told reporters.

The European Union is under increasing pressure to provide Ukraine with an alternative to Starlink. But negotiations between Brussels and Kyiv over access to the bloc’s Govsatcom program — which gives participating governments secure communications capabilities— have been stalling. And IRIS², the EU’s in-house planned network to match Starlink, is only expected to come online in 2030.

“The Europeans are now raising the question of alternatives themselves. And they’re already working on them. They’re already making progress, and they’ll succeed in this area. I can already see that,” Zelenskyy said.

SpaceX did not immediately responded to a request for comment.

Earlier on Saturday, Zelenskyy accused Russia of looking to create a blackout across Ukraine, amid attacks on energy infrastructure and the waiver of U.S. sanctions on Moscow.

World.title: Police, demonstrators clash on sidelines of mass French protests
World.content:
“A very large majority of people are protesting without violence,” Paris’s police prefecture said on Saturday afternoon.

Around 4,500 secondary school pupils and university students involved in the Yellow Vests movement demonstrated side by side against the cost of living in Pau, south-west of France on 17 October 2026. | Jean-Christophe Chartre/AFP via Getty Images

Saturday’s demonstrations grew out of the student protests that began last month with school blockades and calls for better study conditions, more teachers and more funding. The movement has since spread nationwide — and become a political issue as the campaign for next year’s presidential election heats up.

In recent weeks, the government has struggled to deal with the crisis — which Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu described as “urban violence” — and is hoping the student movement will now fade because of a two-week school holiday that started Friday evening.

“The mobilization is marked by a very strong involvement of the ultra-left movement, which is only looking to cause disorder,” Nuñez’s office said Saturday, adding that the minister reiterated his “instructions of utmost firmness” to local prefects and police forces.

Footage showed Lyon’s tourist board office engulfed in flames on the city’s Place Bellecour. A police station was vandalized in Marseille, where a group of “rioters” also entered city hall, Mayor Benoît Payan said. He told BFMTV that “damage was objectively fairly limited,” although the act of vandalism was “unacceptable.” The headquarters of right-wing TV channel CNews in Paris was also targeted , authorities said.

World.title: Spain’s far left fails to unite ahead of November vote
World.content:
The Broad Front is made up of Sumar, the current junior partner in the Socialist-led government, the Catalan Comuns, the Communist-led United Left and Más Madrid. Some smaller local parties have also joined the ticket. The lead candidate for prime minister will be Ada Colau, the former mayor of Barcelona.

Sumar, the dominant force in the alliance, has seen its vote share more than halve since 2023, to 5%, according to POLITICO’s Poll of Polls.

Although Podemos has only been polling at 3%, its full involvement in the Broad Front would have meant a greater overall share of seats for the far left, according to analysts.
